children.title: Validity-Domain Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Valid inequalities classified by their reference set and domain of applicability.

children.title: Hull-Integrality Validity Pair
children.top_down_role: Validity relative to pure- or mixed-integer feasible hulls.

children.title: Pure-Integer-Hull Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity relative to feasible hulls with exclusively integer-constrained variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Pure-Integer-Hull Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity for the convex hull obtained by imposing integrality on every variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and define its pure-integer hull by \(P_I=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n)\). A linear inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\), with \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), is valid for the pure-integer hull precisely when \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in P_I\). Equivalently, it is valid when the inequality holds for every point of \(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality is pure-integer-hull valid exactly when every integer point of the underlying set, and hence every convex combination of those points, satisfies it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(P_I\) if and only if it holds on \(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\).

children.title: Mixed-Integer-Hull Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity relative to feasible hulls containing discrete plus continuous variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer-Hull Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity for a hull in which only a designated coordinate set is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Define the mixed-integer hull by \(P_I^{\mathrm{MI}}=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in P:x_i\in\mathbb{Z}\text{ for every }i\in I\}\). A linear inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(P_I^{\mathrm{MI}}\) precisely when it holds for every mixed-integer feasible point \(x\in P\) satisfying the designated integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-integer-hull valid inequality holds at every feasible point whose designated coordinates are integer; unrestricted coordinates may remain continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(P_I^{\mathrm{MI}}\) if and only if it holds on \(\{x\in P:x_i\in\mathbb{Z}\text{ for all }i\in I\}\).

notation.meaning: Mixed-integer hull of P for pattern I

children.title: Integrality-Pattern Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Changes in validity scope caused by alternative assignments of variable integrality.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Pattern Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity of hulls and validity as additional coordinates are required to be integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and integrality patterns \(I\subseteq J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(P_K=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in P:x_k\in\mathbb{Z}\text{ for every }k\in K\}\). Then \(P_J\subseteq P_I\). Consequently every inequality valid for \(P_I\) is valid for \(P_J\), while an inequality valid only for \(P_J\) need not be valid for \(P_I\). In particular, the pure-integer hull is contained in every mixed-integer hull formed from the same set \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Imposing integrality on more coordinates shrinks the hull and enlarges the collection of valid inequalities; the reverse implications generally fail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_J\subseteq P_I\), so validity for \(P_I\) implies validity for \(P_J\).

notation.meaning: Hull associated with integrality pattern K

children.title: Validity Locality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Validity throughout the model or within a restricted search region.

children.title: Global Model Validity
children.top_down_role: Inequalities applicable throughout the full model domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Model Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity over the complete feasible set, independently of branch-and-bound restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the feasible set of an optimization model. A linear inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is globally valid for the model when \(F\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\}\). Thus it may be added to the formulation at the root or at any descendant node without deleting a globally feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally valid inequality is satisfied by every feasible solution and can therefore be imposed throughout the entire search tree.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the model's complete feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is globally valid exactly when \(F\subseteq\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\}\).

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

children.title: Node-Local Validity
children.top_down_role: Inequalities applicable within a restricted branch-and-bound region.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditional on the domain restrictions defining one search-tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the global feasible set and let \(B_v\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) denote the branching domain at node \(v\). An inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid locally at \(v\) when \(F\cap B_v\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\}\). Such an inequality may be enforced at \(v\) and its descendants whose domains lie in \(B_v\), but local validity alone does not justify enforcing it elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-local inequality holds for feasible solutions compatible with that node's branching restrictions, but need not hold outside the node's subtree.
assumptions_latex: \(B_v\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the domain imposed at node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local validity at \(v\) means \(F\cap B_v\subseteq\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\}\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set restricted to node v

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

children.title: Local-to-Global Promotion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting reuse of region-specific inequalities outside their originating domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global Promotion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coverage condition separating merely local validity from global validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{v\in V}B_v\). If one inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid on \(F\cap B_v\) for every \(v\in V\), then it is globally valid on \(F\). Validity at only one node \(v\) does not imply global validity unless \(F\subseteq B_v\) or an independent argument establishes the inequality on \(F\setminus B_v\). Indeed, any \(x^\star\in F\setminus B_v\) with \(a^{\mathsf T}x^\star>\beta\) witnesses failure of promotion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local validity becomes global only after all feasible regions are covered; a feasible violator outside the local domain blocks promotion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity on every \(F\cap B_v\) implies validity on \(F\); validity on one restricted region generally does not.

notation.meaning: Index set of domains covering F

children.title: Cross-Space Validity Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Validity before and after lifting, projection, or reformulation.

children.title: Original-Space Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity expressed directly in the model's original variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Space Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of an inequality expressed solely in the model's original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a feasible set in the original variable space. An original-space inequality has the form \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\), where \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and is valid for \(Q\) exactly when \(Q\) lies in its associated halfspace: \(Q\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\}\). Its validity is therefore determined without assigning auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An original-space valid inequality uses only original variables and is satisfied by every feasible original-variable vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(Q\) if and only if every \(x\in Q\) satisfies it.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Projection with a Minimal System of Inequalities p. 31

children.title: Extended-Space Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity expressed in formulations containing auxiliary or lifted variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Space Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of an inequality involving original and auxiliary variables in an extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) be an extended feasible set with variables \((x,y)\), where \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is original and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^p\) is auxiliary. An extended-space inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x+c^{\mathsf T}y\leq\beta\) is valid for \(E\) exactly when it holds for every \((x,y)\in E\). If \(c=0\), the inequality is the lift of an original-space inequality; otherwise its direct meaning depends on the auxiliary representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-space valid inequality holds for every feasible pairing of original and auxiliary variables; it may involve both variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity means \(E\subseteq\{(x,y):a^{\mathsf T}x+c^{\mathsf T}y\leq\beta\}\).

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Projection with a Minimal System of Inequalities p. 31

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Projection with a Minimal System of Inequalities p. 31

children.title: Validity Preservation Under Projection
children.top_down_role: Validity behavior when extended-space inequalities are transferred to original variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Validity Preservation Under Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of original-space validity and validity of its zero-auxiliary lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) and let \(Q=\operatorname{proj}_x(E)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists y\text{ with }(x,y)\in E\}\). For every \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), the original-space inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(Q\) if and only if its lifted inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x+0^{\mathsf T}y\leq\beta\) is valid for \(E\). Hence exact projection preserves and reflects all inequalities depending only on projected coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality involving only original variables is valid after projection exactly when the same inequality is valid throughout the extended set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(Q\) if and only if \(a^{\mathsf T}x+0^{\mathsf T}y\leq\beta\) is valid for \(E\).

notation.meaning: Projection of E onto original coordinates
Zero coefficient block for auxiliary variables

children.title: Inequality Strength-Facial Classification
children.top_down_role: Geometric and representation-sensitive comparisons among valid inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalence, Dominance, and Maximality of Valid Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison and facial status of valid inequalities over the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\), and let \(\pi x\leq\pi_0\) and \(\gamma x\leq\gamma_0\) be valid for \(S\). They are equivalent if \((\gamma,\gamma_0)=\lambda(\pi,\pi_0)\) for some \(\lambda>0\). If they are not equivalent and there is a \(\mu>0\) such that \(\gamma\geq\mu\pi\) componentwise and \(\gamma_0\leq\mu\pi_0\), then \[\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:\gamma x\leq\gamma_0\}\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:\pi x\leq\pi_0\},\] so \(\gamma x\leq\gamma_0\) dominates \(\pi x\leq\pi_0\). A maximal valid inequality is one not dominated by another valid inequality. Every maximal valid inequality for \(S\) defines a nonempty face of \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\), and every facet-defining inequality of \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\) is maximal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scalar multiples are equivalent valid inequalities. Under the stated componentwise coefficient and right-hand-side conditions, a nonequivalent inequality dominates the other on the nonnegative orthant. An undominated valid inequality is maximal; every such inequality defines a nonempty face, and every facet-defining inequality is maximal.
assumptions_latex: \pi x\leq\pi_0\text{ and }\gamma x\leq\gamma_0\text{ are valid for }S
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\gamma,\gamma_0)=\lambda(\pi,\pi_0),\ \lambda>0\text{ defines equivalence; the stated }\mu\text{-conditions imply dominance; maximal valid inequalities define nonempty faces, and facet-defining inequalities are maximal.}

children.title: Valid-Inequality Strength Order
children.top_down_role: Order relations used to remove weaker or redundant inequalities.

children.title: Dominance Relations
children.top_down_role: Comparisons identifying inequalities whose feasible-region effect is no stronger than another's.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength ordering of valid inequalities relative to a fixed relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(H_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta_i\}\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\), with both inequalities valid for \(F\). Inequality \(1\) dominates inequality \(2\) relative to \(R\) when \(R\cap H_1\subseteq R\cap H_2\). It strictly dominates inequality \(2\) when this inclusion is proper. Dominance therefore compares the feasible regions remaining after each inequality is added to the same relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One valid inequality dominates another when, on the chosen relaxation, it leaves no point that the other would remove.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Inequality \(1\) dominates inequality \(2\) relative to \(R\) exactly when \(R\cap H_1\subseteq R\cap H_2\).

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

children.title: Equivalence Classes
children.top_down_role: Groups of inequalities with matching geometric or representational effect.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of inequalities that induce the same restriction on a fixed relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a relaxation \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). For inequalities represented by halfspaces \(H_1\) and \(H_2\), define \(H_1\sim_R H_2\) when \(R\cap H_1=R\cap H_2\). Equivalently, each inequality dominates the other relative to \(R\). The relation \(\sim_R\) is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive, so it partitions valid inequalities into classes having identical strengthening effect on \(R\). Positive rescalings of the same inequality belong to one class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two inequalities are equivalent on a relaxation when adding either produces exactly the same restricted relaxation; mutual dominance characterizes this equivalence.
assumptions_latex: \(H_1,H_2\) are halfspaces of valid inequalities for a common target set contained in \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_1\sim_R H_2\) if and only if \(R\cap H_1=R\cap H_2\), equivalently each dominates the other.

children.title: Minimal Valid Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Valid inequalities irreducible under the relevant strength ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Valid Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimality in the dominance preorder for a fixed target set and relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(H\) be the halfspace of a valid inequality for \(F\). The inequality is minimal relative to \(R\) when no valid halfspace \(H'\) satisfies \(R\cap H'\subsetneq R\cap H\). Equivalently, every valid inequality that dominates it is equivalent to it on \(R\). Minimality is therefore defined only after fixing both the validity domain \(F\) and the reference relaxation \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid inequality is minimal when no inequivalent valid inequality strictly dominates it on the fixed relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\) is minimal relative to \(R\) exactly when no valid \(H'\) has \(R\cap H'\subsetneq R\cap H\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness of a Minimal Inequality Description
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For a full-dimensional polyhedron, the inequalities in a minimal description are determined up to their ordering and positive rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a full-dimensional polyhedron, then it has a unique minimal description
\[
P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a^i x\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},
\]
where each inequality is unique up to multiplication by a positive scalar.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-dimensional polyhedron has a unique minimal inequality description, apart from reordering the inequalities and multiplying individual inequalities by positive scalars.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\text{ has a unique minimal inequality description, modulo permutation and positive rescaling of its inequalities}

children.title: Supporting Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Valid inequalities associated with supporting hyperplanes of the relevant hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Supporting Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting inequalities and their exposed faces for a convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. A linear inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq \beta\), with \(a\neq 0\), is supporting for \(P\) if it is valid for every \(x\in P\) and its equality set \(F=P\cap\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x=\beta\}\) is nonempty. The set \(F\) is the face of \(P\) exposed by the inequality. Relative to \(\operatorname{aff}(P)\), the inequality is nontrivial when \(F\neq P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supporting inequality is valid for the polyhedron and attained somewhere on it; its equality set is the exposed face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is supporting exactly when it is valid for \(P\) and \(P\cap\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x=\beta\}\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Face exposed by the supporting inequality.

children.title: Facet-Defining Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Inequalities inducing maximal proper faces of the relevant hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Facet-Defining Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet status measured relative to the affine dimension of the polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a polyhedron of affine dimension \(d\geq 1\). A valid supporting inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is facet-defining for \(P\) if its exposed face \(F=P\cap\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x=\beta\}\) has dimension \(d-1\). Equivalently, \(F\) is a maximal proper face of \(P\). Multiplication of the inequality by a positive scalar does not change the represented facet.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supporting inequality defines a facet when its equality face has dimension one less than the polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is a valid supporting inequality for \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is facet-defining if and only if \(\dim(F)=d-1\).

notation.meaning: Face on which the inequality holds at equality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary inequalities and facets of a full-dimensional polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of valid inequalities necessary in a description of a full-dimensional polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a full-dimensional polyhedron. A valid inequality \(\pi x\leq\pi_0\) is necessary in the description of \(P\) if and only if it defines a facet of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-dimensional polyhedron, a valid inequality is necessary in its description exactly when it defines a facet.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi x\leq\pi_0\text{ is necessary in the description of }P\iff \{x\in P:\pi x=\pi_0\}\text{ is a facet of }P.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Facet Status of the Tour-Downset Degree Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A symmetric-TSP specialization of facet-defining inequality theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=K_m with m\ge 3, let S be the characteristic vectors of Hamiltonian tours, and let T=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{E}:x\le x'\text{ for some }x'\in S\}. For every v\in V, the inequality \sum_{e\in\delta(\{v\})}x_e\le 2 defines a facet of \operatorname{conv}(T).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each vertex of a complete graph, the inequality allowing at most two selected incident edges defines a facet of the convex hull of edge sets contained in tours.
assumptions_latex: S=\{\text{characteristic vectors of Hamiltonian tours of }G\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{e\in\delta(\{v\})}x_e\le 2\text{ defines a facet of }\operatorname{conv}(T)\quad(\forall v\in V)

children.title: Lower-Dimensional Face Status
children.top_down_role: Valid inequalities inducing faces below facet dimension.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Dimensional Face Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of supporting inequalities whose exposed proper faces are not facets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) have affine dimension \(d\), and let the valid supporting inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) expose the proper face \(F=P\cap\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x=\beta\}\). The inequality has lower-dimensional face status precisely when \(\dim(F)\leq d-2\). Such an inequality supports \(P\) but is not facet-defining; its equality set has codimension at least two within \(\operatorname{aff}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supporting inequality has lower-dimensional status when its proper equality face has codimension at least two, so it is not facet-defining.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a polyhedron of affine dimension \(d\geq2\).
\(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) exposes a proper nonempty face \(F\) of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) has lower-dimensional status if and only if \(\dim(F)\leq d-2\).

notation.meaning: Exposed proper face of the polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Dependent Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutoff strength can vary between relaxations representing the same integer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cut strength is not determined solely by the represented integer points. For example, let \(S=\{0,1\}\), \(P_1=[0,1]\), and \(P_2=[0,3/2]\). Then \(P_1\cap\mathbb{Z}=P_2\cap\mathbb{Z}=S\), so both polyhedra are relaxations of the same integer set. The valid inequality \(x\leq1\) removes no point of \(P_1\), whereas it removes the nonempty interval \((1,3/2]\) from \(P_2\). Thus cutoff, violation, and comparable relaxation-based strength measures may change under reformulation or projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two relaxations can represent the same integer points while a valid cut removes different fractional regions, making measured strength representation-dependent.
assumptions_latex: Cut strength is evaluated relative to a continuous relaxation rather than only its integer points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_1\cap\mathbb{Z}=P_2\cap\mathbb{Z}\) does not imply equal relaxation-based strength for every valid inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity certified by a nonnegative weighted sum of known inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each inequality \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_i\), for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), is valid for a set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). An aggregation certificate for \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is a vector \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) satisfying \(\alpha=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i a_i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i b_i\leq\beta\). These finitely checkable relations certify that the aggregated inequality is valid for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative weights certify validity when their weighted left sides equal the target and their weighted right sides do not exceed its bound.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_i\) is valid for \(S\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(S\).

notation.meaning: Set on which the input inequalities are valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Multiplier Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral validity certified through nonnegative multipliers in Farkas form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b\}\) be nonempty. For \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), a Farkas multiplier certificate for validity of \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) on \(P\) is a vector \(y\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) such that \(A^{\mathsf T}y=\alpha\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\leq\beta\). The certificate is verified by matrix multiplication, componentwise nonnegativity, and the scalar bound; its existence certifies the target inequality on all of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative multiplier vector certifies a polyhedral inequality when it reproduces the target coefficients and yields no larger right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}y=\alpha\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\leq\beta\) certify \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in P\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedron described by the source inequalities.

children.title: Aggregation–Farkas Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation–Farkas Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between weighted-row aggregation and Farkas validity multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b\}\neq\varnothing\). For \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), the inequality \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(P\) if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) such that \(A^{\mathsf T}y=\alpha\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\leq\beta\). Row by row, the same vector \(y\) gives the nonnegative aggregation \(\sum_{i=1}^m y_iA_{i\bullet}=\alpha^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^m y_ib_i\leq\beta\). Hence aggregation certificates and Farkas multiplier certificates are two representations of the same polyhedral validity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty polyhedron, valid linear inequalities are exactly those obtainable from its rows using suitable nonnegative Farkas multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\text{ is valid on }P\iff\exists y\in\mathbb{R}_+^m:\ A^{\mathsf T}y=\alpha,\ b^{\mathsf T}y\leq\beta\).

notation.meaning: The i-th row of the constraint matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic witness that a linear form is integer-valued on mixed-integer feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index variables constrained to be integral on a feasible set \(S\), and let \(C\) be the complementary index set. A vector \(\pi\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is an integrality certificate for the linear form \(\pi^{\mathsf T}x\) when \(\pi_j\in\mathbb{Z}\) for every \(j\in J\) and \(\pi_j=0\) for every \(j\in C\). These coefficient checks certify \(\pi^{\mathsf T}x\in\mathbb{Z}\) for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer coefficients on integer variables and zero coefficients on continuous variables certify that a linear form is always integer-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_J\in\mathbb{Z}^{J}\) and \(\pi_C=0\) imply \(\pi^{\mathsf T}x\in\mathbb{Z}\) for every \(x\in S\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector of the certified integer-valued form.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity strengthened by rounding the bound of an integer-valued linear form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and suppose \(q^{\mathsf T}x\in\mathbb{Z}\) for every \(x\in S\). If \(q^{\mathsf T}x\leq\delta\) is valid for \(S\), then the pair consisting of this valid inequality and the integrality witness for \(q^{\mathsf T}x\) is a rounding certificate for \(q^{\mathsf T}x\leq\lfloor\delta\rfloor\). For a lower bound \(q^{\mathsf T}x\geq\delta\), the analogous certified rounding is \(q^{\mathsf T}x\geq\lceil\delta\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid bound on an integer-valued linear form can be rounded inward, with floor for upper bounds and ceiling for lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q^{\mathsf T}x\leq\lfloor\delta\rfloor\) is valid for \(S\).

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation-to-Rounding Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-integer Chvátal–Gomory certificate combining nonnegative aggregation with integer rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(C=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus J\), and \(S=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b,\ x_J\in\mathbb{Z}^{J}\}\). A vector \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) is an aggregation-to-rounding certificate when \(q^{\mathsf T}=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A\), \(q_J\in\mathbb{Z}^{J}\), and \(q_C=0\). Aggregation gives \(q^{\mathsf T}x\leq\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\), while the coefficient conditions certify that \(q^{\mathsf T}x\) is integer-valued on \(S\). The resulting certified inequality is \(q^{\mathsf T}x\leq\lfloor\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\rfloor\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate rows nonnegatively, ensure the resulting form is integer-valued, then floor its right-hand side to obtain a valid cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q^{\mathsf T}x\leq\lfloor\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\rfloor\) is valid for \(S\).

notation.meaning: Integer-variable indices and their complementary indices.

children.title: Disjunctive Certificates
children.top_down_role: Validity evidence derived from a union of restricted feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branchwise Farkas multipliers certify validity over a finite union of polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\bigcup_{i=1}^k P_i\), where each \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A^i x\leq b^i\}\) is nonempty. A disjunctive certificate for \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) consists of vectors \(y^i\geq0\), one for each term, satisfying \((A^i)^{\mathsf T}y^i=\alpha\) and \((b^i)^{\mathsf T}y^i\leq\beta\). These branchwise certificates establish validity on every \(P_i\), and therefore on \(D\) and \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is certified for a finite disjunction by providing Farkas multipliers proving it separately on every polyhedral term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A^i)^{\mathsf T}y^i=\alpha\) and \((b^i)^{\mathsf T}y^i\leq\beta\) for all \(i\) certify validity on \(D\) and \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\).

notation.meaning: Finite union representing the disjunctive set.

children.title: Lattice-Free Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Lattice-Free Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge-based intersection-cut validity certified by a lattice-free convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) be a closed, full-dimensional convex set with \(f\in\operatorname{int}(B)\) and \(\operatorname{int}(B)\cap\mathbb{Z}^q=\varnothing\). Define the gauge \(\psi_B(r)=\inf\{t>0:r\in t(B-f)\}\). For rays \(r^1,\ldots,r^k\), every \(s\in\mathbb{R}_+^k\) satisfying \(x=f+\sum_{j=1}^k r^j s_j\in\mathbb{Z}^q\) obeys the intersection cut \(\sum_{j=1}^k\psi_B(r^j)s_j\geq1\). Thus \(B\), together with its lattice-freeness check and gauge coefficients, is a validity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lattice-free convex set containing the fractional point yields gauge coefficients that certify the associated intersection cut for integer points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j=1}^k\psi_B(r^j)s_j\geq1\).

notation.meaning: Lattice-free convex set containing the reference point in its interior.
Gauge of the translated set B-f.
Rays emanating from the reference point.

children.title: Convexification Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between union convexification and forbidden-interior geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexification Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-convex-hull correspondence for linear valid inequalities, including disjunctive feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\mathcal V(S)=\left\{(c,\delta)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R: c^\top s\leq\delta\text{ for every }s\in S\right\}.
\]
For every \((c,\delta)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\), the inequality \(c^\top x\leq\delta\) is valid for \(S\) if and only if it is valid for \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(S)\). Moreover,
\[
\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(S)=\bigcap_{(c,\delta)\in\mathcal V(S)}\left\{x\in\mathbb R^n:c^\top x\leq\delta\right\}.
\]
Thus convexifying a disjunctive or lattice-restricted feasible set preserves precisely its linear valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set and its closed convex hull have exactly the same valid linear inequalities; intersecting all halfspaces defined by those inequalities recovers the closed convex hull.
assumptions_latex: Validity is restricted to closed linear halfspaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(S)\) is exactly the intersection of all closed linear halfspaces valid for \(S\).

notation.meaning: Closed convex hull of the feasible set.
Pairs defining closed linear halfspaces valid for the set.
A linear inequality with normal vector c and right-hand side delta.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-form pure-integer functional certificate with nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Subadditivity means \(f(u+v)\leq f(u)+f(v)\) for all \(u,v\in\mathbb{R}^m\). For every \(x\in X\), nonnegative integrality and \(Ax=\sum_{j=1}^n a_jx_j=b\) give
\[
f(b)=f\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^n a_jx_j\right)\leq\sum_{j=1}^n f(a_j)x_j.
\]
Consequently the displayed inequality is valid for every feasible integer point. The function \(f\), together with evaluations at \(b\) and the columns \(a_j\), is a directly checkable validity certificate.

children.title: Functional Duality Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Integer-programming duality links between the two functional certificate regimes.

assumptions_latex: The functions are real-valued on a common additive domain containing \(0,b,a_1,\ldots,a_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Negation bijectively pairs subadditive and superadditive certificates and negates their associated valid inequalities.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sign reversal algebraically interchanges subadditivity and superadditivity and reverses the induced inequality
source_fulltext_pending: supplied duality locators are not specific to functional integer-programming duality
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-reversal correspondence for equality-form functional certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A function \(f\) with \(f(0)=0\) is subadditive if and only if \(g=-f\) has \(g(0)=0\) and is superadditive. Under this bijection,
\[
f(b)\leq\sum_{j=1}^n f(a_j)x_j
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\sum_{j=1}^n g(a_j)x_j\leq g(b).
\]
Thus the lower-bounding certificate generated by \(f\) and the upper-bounding certificate generated by \(g\) describe the same valid halfspace after multiplication by \(-1\). Applying negation twice returns the original certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating a normalized subadditive function produces a superadditive certificate, and the resulting inequality is exactly the original inequality multiplied by minus one.
knowledge_statements.title: Functional Duality Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sign-reversal correspondence is internally correct and duality fits the terminal container, but no source with a specific functional-duality locator is supplied.

children.title: Sequential Up-Lifting
children.top_down_role: Variable-by-variable lifting from lower-fixed binary faces.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\times\{0,1\}^J\) is nonempty, and every maximized slice below is nonempty with finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursion produces a valid lifted inequality, with each coefficient maximal at the stage where it is computed.

notation.meaning: Binary variables being released from value zero.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary sequential up-lifting from a face fixing lifted variables to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize with the base inequality. For \(k=1,\\ldots,q\), set
\[
\alpha_{j_k}=\beta-\max\left\{a^\top u+\sum_{\ell<k}\alpha_{j_\ell}x_{j_\ell}:(u,x)\in X,\ x_{j_k}=1,\ x_{j_\ell}=0\text{ for }\ell>k\right\}.
\]
After the update, retain \(\alpha_{j_k}\) and continue to the next index. Output
\[
a^\top u+\sum_{k=1}^q\alpha_{j_k}x_{j_k}\leq\beta.
\]
At step \(k\), any larger value of \(\alpha_{j_k}\), with earlier coefficients fixed, violates validity on a maximizing point of the defining slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Release variables fixed at zero one at a time, assigning each the largest coefficient allowed by residual optimization over the newly exposed slice.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Up-Lifting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-maximization recursion has the expected sequential up-lifting form and algorithm is the correct role, but it lacks a source. The opening range contains malformed `\\ldots`, and the final maximality argument is proof text.

children.title: Sequential Down-Lifting
children.top_down_role: Variable-by-variable lifting from upper-fixed binary faces.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\times\{0,1\}^J\) is nonempty, and every maximized slice below is nonempty with finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursion validly releases variables fixed at one and gives stagewise maximal deviation coefficients.

notation.meaning: Deviation from the initially fixed value one.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: down-lifting is up-lifting applied to complementary binary deviations
source_fulltext_pending: no supplied locator specifically covers sequential down-lifting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary sequential down-lifting from a face fixing lifted variables to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(k=1,\ldots,q\), define
\[
\lambda_{j_k}=\beta-\max\left\{a^\top u+\sum_{\ell<k}\lambda_{j_\ell}(1-x_{j_\ell}):(u,x)\in X,\ x_{j_k}=0,\ x_{j_\ell}=1\text{ for }\ell>k\right\}.
\]
Keep each computed coefficient and output
\[
a^\top u+\sum_{k=1}^q\lambda_{j_k}(1-x_{j_k})\leq\beta.
\]
The construction is sequential up-lifting in the complementary variables \(1-x_j\). Each \(\lambda_{j_k}\) is the largest coefficient preserving validity after the first \(k\) fixed-at-one variables have been released.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace fixed-at-one variables by complementary deviations, then release those deviations sequentially using the same residual-maximization rule as up-lifting.

Set \(d_j(x)=x_j\) when \(q_j=0\), and \(d_j(x)=1-x_j\) when \(q_j=1\). At step \(k\), define
\[
\lambda_{j_k}=\beta-\max\left\{a^\top u+\sum_{\ell<k}\lambda_{j_\ell}d_{j_\ell}(x):(u,x)\in X,\ d_{j_k}(x)=1,\ d_{j_\ell}(x)=0\text{ for }\ell>k\right\}.
\]

children.title: Order-Dependent Lifting
children.top_down_role: Lifting settings where coefficient outcomes vary with variable order.

assumptions_latex: A deterministic sequential lifting recursion is defined for every permutation of a finite index set \(J\).
Each recursion is well-defined and returns a coefficient vector indexed by \(J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lifting is order-dependent exactly when two admissible permutations return unequal coefficient vectors.

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector returned under ordering sigma.
A permutation of the lifted indices.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: order dependence is precisely nonuniqueness of the sequentially generated coefficient vector across permutations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of order dependence for deterministic sequential lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each permutation \(\sigma\) of \(J\), let \(\lambda^\sigma\in\mathbb{R}^J\) be the final vector produced by sequential lifting in that order. The lifting procedure is order-dependent if and only if there exist permutations \(\sigma\) and \(\tau\) such that
\[
\lambda^\sigma\neq\lambda^\tau.
\]
Equivalently, at least one index receives different final coefficients under two admissible release orders. Order dependence concerns the generated representation, even when every resulting inequality is valid and all representations expose the same base face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential lifting is order-dependent when at least two release orders produce different final coefficient vectors, even though every resulting inequality remains valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Dependent Lifting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The criterion correctly expresses order dependence, but no source is supplied. Because the statement explicitly defines the term, `definition` would be more exact than `property` for this terminal record.

children.title: Sequence-Independent Lifting
children.top_down_role: Lifting settings where admissible sequences yield invariant outcomes.

assumptions_latex: A deterministic sequential lifting recursion is defined and finite for every permutation of \(J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sequence independence means \(\lambda^\sigma=\lambda^\tau\) for every pair of permutations \(\sigma,\tau\) of \(J\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector generated by ordering sigma.
Set of all permutations of J.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sequence independence is equality of the deterministic lifting output over all admissible permutations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global permutation-invariance condition for sequential lifting coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The lifting recursion is sequence-independent precisely when there exists \(\bar\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^J\) satisfying
\[
\lambda^\sigma=\bar\lambda\qquad\text{for every }\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}(J).
\]
Because adjacent transpositions generate every permutation, it is sufficient to verify that swapping any two adjacent, currently unlifted indices leaves the two updated coefficients and the resulting recursion state unchanged, provided this commutation test holds at every reachable intermediate state. Under this condition the lifted inequality is determined by the base face and recursion, not by the chosen release sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifting is sequence-independent when every variable order produces one common coefficient vector; statewise commutation of all adjacent lifting steps is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Independent Lifting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Permutation invariance is the correct sequence-independence condition and the content kind fits. The stronger reachable-state adjacent-commutation criterion is plausible but requires a precise source and formal definition of the recursion state.

children.top_down_role: Structural sources of noninterchangeable lifting choices.

assumptions_latex: Sequential up-lifting uses the residual-maximization rule for a less-than-or-equal inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict interaction between jointly released variables can make lifting operators noncommutative and the final coefficients order-dependent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete two-variable boundary showing failure of lifting commutativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
X=\{(z,x_1,x_2):(z,x_1,x_2)\in\{(0,0,0),(1,1,0),(1,0,1),(3,1,1)\}\}.
\]
The inequality \(z\leq0\) is valid on the face \(x_1=x_2=0\). Lifting \(x_1\) first gives coefficient \(-1\), after which lifting \(x_2\) gives \(-2\); the result is \(z-x_1-2x_2\leq0\). Reversing the order gives \(z-2x_1-x_2\leq0\). Both inequalities are valid for \(X\), but their coefficient vectors differ, so the two lifting steps do not commute.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A four-point set yields coefficients minus one and minus two in one order, but minus two and minus one in the reverse order.
knowledge_statements.title: Commutativity Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four-point computation is internally correct and a counterexample is appropriate for the failure-boundary leaf, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable evidence source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric maximal-coefficient lifting function for a binary extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The maximal lifting function associated with the base inequality is the map \(\lambda:R\to\mathbb{R}\) defined by
\[
\lambda(r)=\beta-\sup\{a^\top u:(u,1)\in X_r\}.
\]
For each \(r\), the inequality \(a^\top u+\lambda(r)z\leq\beta\) is valid for \(X_r\). Moreover, if \(\gamma>\lambda(r)\), then \(a^\top u+\gamma z\leq\beta\) is not valid whenever the displayed supremum is attained. Thus \(\lambda(r)\) records the strongest coefficient obtainable from the one-variable lifting subproblem for parameter \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifting function maps each variable type to the largest coefficient allowed by optimization over the slice where that binary variable equals one.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifting Functions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lifting function and superadditivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional representation of lifting coefficients for a full-dimensional binary packing set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax\le b\}\), with \(A\ge0\) and \(\dim(S)=n\). Let \(C\subset N\), and suppose \(\sum_{i\in C}\alpha_ix_i\le\beta\) is valid on the face where \(x_j=0\) for all \(j\in N\setminus C\). Writing \(a^j\) for column \(j\) of \(A\), define, for \(z\in[0,b]\), \[f(z):=\beta-\max\left\{\sum_{i\in C}\alpha_ix_i:\sum_{i\in C}a^ix_i\le b-z,\ x_i\in\{0,1\}\text{ for }i\in C\right\}.\] The function \(f\) is the lifting function of the base inequality, and every lifting satisfies \(\alpha_j\le f(a^j)\) for \(j\in N\setminus C\). A function \(g:U\to\mathbb R\) is superadditive if \(g(u+v)\ge g(u)+g(v)\) whenever \(u,v,u+v\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lifting function gives the base right-hand side minus the best base-variable value available after reserving resource vector z. Every lifted coefficient is bounded above by the function evaluated at its column. Superadditivity requires the value at a feasible sum to be at least the sum of the separate values.
assumptions_latex: \sum_{i\in C}\alpha_ix_i\le\beta\text{ is valid when }x_j=0\ \forall j\in N\setminus C
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(z)=\beta-\max\left\{\sum_{i\in C}\alpha_ix_i:\sum_{i\in C}a^ix_i\le b-z,\ x_i\in\{0,1\}\right\},\quad \alpha_j\le f(a^j)\ (j\notin C),\quad g\text{ is superadditive when }g(u+v)\ge g(u)+g(v).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered-monoid form of reusable superadditive coefficient lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Repeated superadditivity gives
\[
\sum_{j=1}^n g(a_j)x_j\leq g\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^n a_jx_j\right).
\]
Order preservation and \(\sum_j a_jx_j\preceq b\) then give
\[
\sum_{j=1}^n g(a_j)x_j\leq g(b).
\]
Consequently \(g(a_j)\) are valid coefficients for all resource-feasible nonnegative integer vectors. If a new variable of type \(r\in M\) is introduced, assigning coefficient \(g(r)\) preserves the same certificate whenever the augmented resource inequality remains satisfied. This makes \(g\) a reusable superadditive lifting rule rather than a coefficient computed for only one formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-preserving superadditive function converts additive resource types into valid coefficients and can lift any new variable by evaluating its type.
knowledge_statements.title: Superadditive Lifting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordered-monoid claim is mathematically coherent and principle fits the superadditive-lifting leaf, but this generalized reusable lifting formulation lacks a source. The displayed derivation is proof text and should not appear in the final statement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity and uniqueness from a superadditive lifting function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous lifting through superadditive minorants of the lifting function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the lifting-function setup, let \(f:[0,b]\to\mathbb R\) be the lifting function of \(\sum_{j\in C}\alpha_jx_j\le\beta\). If \(g:[0,b]\to\mathbb R\) is superadditive and \(g(z)\le f(z)\) for every \(z\in[0,b]\), then \[\sum_{j\in C}\alpha_jx_j+\sum_{j\in N\setminus C}g(a^j)x_j\le\beta\] is valid for \(S\). In particular, if \(f\) is superadditive, then \[\sum_{j\in C}\alpha_jx_j+\sum_{j\in N\setminus C}f(a^j)x_j\le\beta\] is the unique maximal lifting of the base inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any superadditive function lying pointwise below the lifting function supplies jointly valid coefficients for all omitted variables. If the lifting function itself is superadditive, its values give the unique maximal lifting.
assumptions_latex: f:[0,b]\to\mathbb R\text{ is the lifting function of }\sum_{j\in C}\alpha_jx_j\le\beta
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j\in C}\alpha_jx_j+\sum_{j\notin C}g(a^j)x_j\le\beta\text{ is valid for }S;\quad f\text{ superadditive}\Rightarrow\sum_{j\in C}\alpha_jx_j+\sum_{j\notin C}f(a^j)x_j\le\beta\text{ is the unique maximal lifting.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb Z_+\), and suppose \(\alpha^Tx\le\beta\) is valid for every \((x,0)\in S\). Define the lifting-coefficient subproblem by \[\gamma^*:=\inf\left\{\frac{\beta-\alpha^Tx}{y}:(x,y)\in S,\ y>0\right\}.\] If this set is nonempty and \(\gamma^*\) is finite, then \(\gamma^*\) is the largest coefficient for which \(\alpha^Tx+\gamma y\le\beta\) is valid on \(S\). An exact solution returns \(\gamma^*\); any certified value \(\gamma\le\gamma^*\) is a valid approximate coefficient, while restricting the infimum requires a separately certified bound before validity can be asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximal coefficient for a lifted nonnegative integer variable is an infimum of residual slack divided by the variable value; certified lower coefficients remain valid.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tableau-pivot algorithm for quasi-optimal lift-and-project cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative CGLP-related tableau pivoting from a fractional row; the cut characterization is conditional on termination and does not assert finite termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve \(\mathrm{LP}\), let \(\bar x\) be an optimal solution, and choose \(k\) with \(0<\bar x_k<1\). In each current simplex basis, let \(J\) index the nonbasic variables. For every row \(i\ne k\), compute \(r_{u_i}\) using \(M_1=\{j\in J:\bar a_{kj}<0\ \vee\ (\bar a_{kj}=0\wedge\bar a_{ij}>0)\}\) and compute \(r_{v_i}\) using \(M_1=\{j\in J:\bar a_{kj}<0\ \vee\ (\bar a_{kj}=0\wedge\bar a_{ij}<0)\}\), in both cases taking \(M_2=J\setminus M_1\) and applying (9.6). If no row has \(r_{u_i}<0\) or \(r_{v_i}<0\), stop. Otherwise choose such a row \(i_*\), minimize \(f^+(\gamma_j)\) over \(j\in J\) with \(\gamma_j>0\) and \(f^-(\gamma_j)\) over \(j\in J\) with \(\gamma_j<0\), select the column \(j_*\) corresponding to the more negative minimum, pivot on \(\bar a_{i_*j_*}\), and repeat. Upon termination, the simple disjunctive cut from transformed row \(k\) is a quasi-optimal lift-and-project cut, and the mixed-integer Gomory cut from row \(k\) is a quasi-optimal strengthened lift-and-project cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from an optimal LP solution having a fractional component k. For each other tableau row, compute the two prescribed reduced costs. If either is negative for some row, choose such a row, select its most improving eligible pivot column using the stated positive- and negative-gamma minimizations, pivot, and repeat. Stop when no qualifying negative reduced cost remains. Conditional on termination, the transformed row-k disjunctive cut is a quasi-optimal lift-and-project cut, and its mixed-integer Gomory cut is a quasi-optimal strengthened lift-and-project cut.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\text{ is an optimal solution of }\mathrm{LP}.
J\text{ indexes the nonbasic variables in the current simplex basis}.
r_{u_i},r_{v_i},f^+,f^-,\gamma_j\text{ and the reduced-cost calculation (9.6) are defined by the associated CGLP tableau formulation}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{If the procedure terminates, the row-}k\text{ simple disjunctive cut is a quasi-optimal lift-and-project cut, and the row-}k\text{ GMI cut is a quasi-optimal strengthened lift-and-project cut.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tableau pivot regime that replaces a fractional primal pivot by a rounded cut having unit entering-variable coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an integral tableau basis $x_{B_i}+\sum_{j\in H}\bar a_{ij}x_j=\bar a_{i0}$ with an integral current basic solution. Choose $k\in H$ with $\bar a_{0k}<0$ and a ratio-test row $r\in\arg\min\{\bar a_{i0}/\bar a_{ik}:\bar a_{ik}>0\}$. If $\bar a_{rk}=1$, pivoting on row $r$ preserves integrality. If $\bar a_{rk}\ne1$, add the equation $x_{n+1}+x_k+\sum_{j\in H\setminus\{k\}}\left\lfloor\bar a_{rj}/\bar a_{rk}\right\rfloor x_j=\left\lfloor\bar a_{r0}/\bar a_{rk}\right\rfloor$, where $x_{n+1}\in\mathbb Z_+$, and pivot on this row; the resulting basic solution remains integral.

Otherwise, a ratio-scaled and rounded Chvátal–Gomory cut supplies a row with unit entering-variable coefficient, so pivoting on that row preserves integrality.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a basis \(B\), write the tableau equations as \(x_B=\bar b-\bar A x_N\), with \(x_N\ge0\), and let \(I_B\subseteq B\) index basic variables required to be integral. The associated corner relaxation is
\[R_B=\{(x_B,x_N):x_B=\bar b-\bar A x_N,\ x_N\ge0,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }i\in I_B\}.\]
Corner-relaxation generation constructs any inequality valid for \(R_B\), commonly from a fractional tableau row or a disjunction implied by its integrality condition, and adds its expression in the original variables to the current linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A corner relaxation retains tableau equations, nonbasic nonnegativity, and selected basic integrality; any inequality valid for it supplies a valid tableau-based cut.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a basis of a rational linear relaxation.
Variables indexed by \(I_B\) are integer constrained in the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality valid for \(R_B\) is valid for the original mixed-integer feasible points contained in \(R_B\).

notation.meaning: corner relaxation associated with basis B

children.title: Disjunctive Projection Calculus
children.top_down_role: Cuts generated by convexifying unions in original or lifted spaces.

children.title: Termwise Disjunctive Generation
children.top_down_role: Cut generation from validity across each term of a union.

knowledge_statements.title: Termwise Disjunctive Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity test for a finite union of polyhedral disjunctive terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=\bigcup_{t=1}^T P_t\), where each \(P_t\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron. An inequality \(\alpha^Tx\le\beta\) is valid for the disjunctive set \(D\) if and only if it is valid termwise:
\[\sup_{x\in P_t}\alpha^Tx\le\beta\qquad(t=1,\ldots,T).\]
When \(P_t=\{x:A^t x\le b^t\}\), termwise validity can be certified by multipliers \(\lambda^t\ge0\) satisfying \((A^t)^T\lambda^t=\alpha\) and \((b^t)^T\lambda^t\le\beta\) for every term, whenever the corresponding linear-programming dual certificates exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality is valid for a finite disjunction exactly when it is valid for every term; nonnegative multipliers can certify each term.
assumptions_latex: For the multiplier form, each term has the displayed inequality representation and finite support value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^Tx\le\beta\) is valid on \(D\) exactly when it is valid on every \(P_t\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative validity multiplier for term t

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Valid Inequalities for Disjunctive Sets p. 9

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Valid Inequalities for Disjunctive Sets p. 9

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Farkas Characterization of Valid Inequalities for a Finite Disjunction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes validity over a finite union of polyhedra through a separate nonnegative Farkas certificate for every nonempty term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be finite and \(F=\bigcup_{h\in Q}P_h\), where \(P_h=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A^h x\ge b^h\}\), \(A^h\in\mathbb R^{m_h\times n}\), and \(b^h\in\mathbb R^{m_h}\). Define \(Q^*=\{h\in Q:P_h\ne\varnothing\}\). For \(\alpha\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\alpha_0\in\mathbb R\), the inequality \(\alpha^\top x\ge\alpha_0\) is valid for every \(x\in F\) if and only if, for every \(h\in Q^*\), there exists \(u^h\in\mathbb R^{m_h}_+\) such that \(\alpha^\top=(u^h)^\top A^h\) and \(\alpha_0\le (u^h)^\top b^h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality is valid on a finite union of polyhedra exactly when every nonempty polyhedral term has a nonnegative Farkas multiplier that generates the inequality's coefficient vector and certifies its right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: P_h=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A^h x\ge b^h\},\quad A^h\in\mathbb R^{m_h\times n},\quad b^h\in\mathbb R^{m_h}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall x\in F,\ \alpha^\top x\ge\alpha_0)\iff(\forall h\in Q^*,\ \exists u^h\in\mathbb R^{m_h}_+:\ \alpha^\top=(u^h)^\top A^h\ \land\ \alpha_0\le (u^h)^\top b^h).

children.title: Lifted-Hull Generation
children.top_down_role: Generation in auxiliary-variable convex-hull representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Hull Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended convex-hull formulation for a finite union of polyhedra having a common recession cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_t=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A^t x\le b^t\}\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\), where the nonempty polyhedra \(P_t\) have a common recession cone. Define
\[Q=\left\{(x,x^1,\ldots,x^T,\lambda):x=\sum_{t=1}^T x^t,\ A^t x^t\le b^t\lambda_t\ (t=1,\ldots,T),\ \lambda\ge0,\ \sum_{t=1}^T\lambda_t=1\right\}.\]
Then \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{t=1}^T P_t)\). Consequently, eliminating \((x^1,\ldots,x^T,\lambda)\) from valid inequalities for \(Q\) generates valid inequalities for the disjunctive hull, while valid inequalities involving only \(x\) transfer directly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonempty polyhedra with a common recession cone, disaggregated copies and convex weights give an extended formulation whose x-projection is the convex hull of their union.
assumptions_latex: The polyhedra \(P_t\) have a common recession cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{t=1}^T P_t)\).

notation.meaning: disaggregated variable associated with term t
convex weight associated with term t

children.title: Projection of Lifted Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Transfer of extended-space inequalities into original-variable space.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection of Lifted Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier elimination of auxiliary variables in a polyhedral extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{n+m}:Ax+By\le d\}\) and \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\). For any multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \(B^T\lambda=0\), aggregation of the lifted inequalities eliminates \(y\) and gives
\[(A^T\lambda)^Tx\le d^T\lambda,\]
which is valid for \(P\). Conversely, every inequality \(\alpha^Tx\le\beta\) valid for a nonempty \(P\) admits such a multiplier with \(A^T\lambda=\alpha\) and \(d^T\lambda\le\beta\), subject to the standard polyhedral Farkas representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative aggregation projects a lifted system when auxiliary-variable coefficients cancel; under polyhedral Farkas conditions, every projected valid inequality has such a certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\) is represented by eliminating unrestricted auxiliary variables \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(B^T\lambda=0\) imply validity of \((A^T\lambda)^Tx\le d^T\lambda\) on \(P\).

children.title: Facet Transfer
children.top_down_role: Preservation or transformation of facet status across representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Facet Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension criterion for an x-only lifted supporting inequality to remain facet-defining after projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\) be a polyhedron, let \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\), and suppose the valid lifted inequality \(\alpha^T x\le\beta\), which has no auxiliary-variable coefficient, defines the face \(F_Q=Q\cap\{(x,y):\alpha^T x=\beta\}\). Its projection is
\[F_P=P\cap\{x:\alpha^T x=\beta\}=\operatorname{proj}_x(F_Q).\]
The inequality defines a facet of \(P\) if and only if \(\dim(F_P)=\dim(P)-1\), where dimension is taken in the affine hull of \(P\). In particular, if \(P\) is full-dimensional in \(\mathbb R^n\), this condition is \(\dim(F_P)=n-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An x-only valid inequality from a lifted polyhedron remains facet-defining after projection exactly when its projected equality face has codimension one in the projected polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha^T x\le\beta\) is valid for \(Q\) and has no auxiliary-variable coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality defines a facet of \(P\) if and only if \(\dim(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_Q))=\dim(P)-1\).

notation.meaning: equality face of the lifted polyhedron

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Rank Facet and Cone Extreme-Ray Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Under full dimensionality of the projected set and the stated rank condition on B, characterizes projected facets directly through extreme rays of the coefficient cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{Proj}_x(Q)\) is full dimensional and \(\operatorname{rank}(B)=m\), then \(vx\leq v_0\) defines a facet of \(\operatorname{Proj}_x(Q)\) if and only if \((v,v_0)\) is an extreme ray of \(\widetilde W\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: vx\leq v_0\text{ defines a facet of }\operatorname{Proj}_x(Q)\iff (v,v_0)\text{ is an extreme ray of }\widetilde W.

children.title: Facial Strength Loss Under Projection
children.top_down_role: Geometric circumstances where projection weakens facial status.

knowledge_statements.title: Facial Strength Loss Under Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A lifted facet may project onto the entire projected polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[Q=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:0\le x\le1,\ 0\le y\le x\}\]
and its projection \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=[0,1]\). The inequality \(y\ge0\) defines the facet \(F_Q=\{(x,0):0\le x\le1\}\) of the two-dimensional polyhedron \(Q\). Nevertheless, \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_Q)=[0,1]=P\). Hence this lifted facet yields no proper face and no nontrivial valid inequality in the projected space. Facet status is therefore not preserved by projection without an additional projected-dimension condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The facet y ≥ 0 of a triangular lifted polyhedron projects onto the whole interval, demonstrating complete loss of facial strength.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_Q\) is a facet of \(Q\), but \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_Q)=P\), so its projection is not a proper face.

notation.meaning: facet of Q defined by y equal to zero

children.title: Coefficient-Bound Strengthening Calculus
children.top_down_role: Post-generation improvement using integrality, complements, and variable bounds.

children.title: Coefficient Improvement Methods
children.top_down_role: Direct improvement of coefficients on discrete variables.

children.title: Coefficient Reduction
children.top_down_role: Decreases in discrete-variable coefficients that preserve validity while reducing excess magnitude.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe reduction of one coefficient in a valid covering-form inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\), and suppose \(a^T x\ge b\) is valid for \(X\). Fix \(j\) and define
\[a_j^*=\sup_{\substack{x\in X\\x_j>0}}\frac{b-\sum_{i\ne j}a_i x_i}{x_j},\]
using the convention \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\), and require separately that \(\sum_{i\ne j}a_i x_i\ge b\) for every \(x\in X\) with \(x_j=0\). Replacing \(a_j\) by any finite \(\widehat a_j\ge a_j^*\) preserves validity. If \(a_j^*\le\widehat a_j<a_j\), the new covering inequality dominates the original on \(\mathbb R_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a valid covering inequality over nonnegative variables, a coefficient can be reduced to any finite value not below its pointwise validity threshold, producing a dominating valid inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(a_j^*\le\widehat a_j<a_j\), then \(\sum_{i\ne j}a_i x_i+\widehat a_jx_j\ge b\) is valid for \(X\) and dominates the original inequality on \(\mathbb R_+^n\).

notation.meaning: pointwise validity threshold for the coefficient of variable j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the threshold follows directly from pointwise validity on the nonnegative domain
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Coefficient Tightening
children.top_down_role: Adjustments that improve inequality strength through discrete-variable structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe increase of one coefficient in a valid packing-form inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\), and suppose \(a^T x\le b\) is valid for \(X\). Fix \(j\) and define
\[a_j^*=\inf_{\substack{x\in X\\x_j>0}}\frac{b-\sum_{i\ne j}a_i x_i}{x_j},\]
using the convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Replacing \(a_j\) by any finite \(\widehat a_j\le a_j^*\) preserves validity. If \(a_j<\widehat a_j\le a_j^*\), then, because \(x_j\ge0\), the new packing inequality dominates the original on \(\mathbb R_+^n\). Dominance relative to a relaxation is strict exactly when the corresponding halfspace inclusion is proper.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a valid packing inequality over nonnegative variables, a coefficient can be increased to any finite value not above its pointwise validity ceiling, producing a dominating valid inequality; strictness requires proper containment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(a_j<\widehat a_j\le a_j^*\), then \(\sum_{i\ne j}a_i x_i+\widehat a_jx_j\le b\) is valid for \(X\) and dominates the original inequality on \(\mathbb R_+^n\).

notation.meaning: pointwise validity ceiling for the coefficient of variable j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the ceiling follows directly from pointwise validity on the nonnegative domain
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Dominance Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Strength comparisons between original inequalities and coefficient-improved variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise criterion for dominance between same-sense linear inequalities on a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(I_1\) and \(I_2\) be inequalities with feasible halfspaces \(H_1\) and \(H_2\). Relative to \(R\), \(I_1\) dominates \(I_2\) precisely when
\[R\cap H_1\subseteq R\cap H_2.\]
Dominance is strict when this inclusion is proper. In particular, on \(R\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\), reducing a coefficient in a covering inequality \(a^Tx\ge b\), or increasing a coefficient in a packing inequality \(a^Tx\le b\), yields a dominating inequality whenever validity is preserved. Equality of the intersections gives an equivalent, not strictly stronger, outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One inequality dominates another when its accepted points within the relaxation form a subset; coefficient improvement gives strict dominance only if that subset is proper.
assumptions_latex: Both inequalities are valid for the intended discrete feasible set.
Dominance is assessed relative to the same relaxation \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_1\) dominates \(I_2\) if and only if \(R\cap H_1\subseteq R\cap H_2\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dominance is defined by containment of relaxation intersections
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Variable Complementation
children.top_down_role: Alternative binary representations used before rounding and strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Complementation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact affine complementation of a binary variable before cut derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a binary variable \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\), define its complement \(z_j=1-x_j\). Then \(z_j\in\{0,1\}\), the transformation is bijective, and a linear inequality
\[a_jx_j+\sum_{i\ne j}a_i x_i\le b\]
is equivalently represented as
\[-a_jz_j+\sum_{i\ne j}a_i x_i\le b-a_j.\]
A valid inequality derived after complementation remains valid after substituting \(z_j=1-x_j\) back. Although the represented binary feasible set is unchanged, rounding or coefficient-strengthening operations need not be invariant under this alternative representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing a binary variable by one minus a new binary variable is exact, but subsequent rounding or strengthening may produce different cuts.
assumptions_latex: Complementation is followed by the inverse substitution when returning to the original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maps \(x_j\mapsto z_j=1-x_j\) and \(z_j\mapsto x_j=1-z_j\) preserve the binary feasible set and validity.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: binary complementation is an exact affine bijection
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine complementation and transformed inequality are correct, but the claim that subsequent rounding or strengthening need not be invariant depends on the operation used and needs a specific source or qualified example.

children.title: Variable-Bound Substitution Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Strengthening based on known or inferred variable bounds.

children.title: Explicit-Bound Substitution
children.top_down_role: Strengthening based on variable bounds stated directly in the formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit-Bound Substitution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact slack substitutions derived from stated finite variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a variable satisfy the explicit bounds \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\), with finite \(\ell_j<u_j\). Its lower-bound and upper-bound substitutions are
\[x_j=\ell_j+s_j^L,\qquad s_j^L\ge0,\]
and
\[x_j=u_j-s_j^U,\qquad s_j^U\ge0.\]
Each substitution is an exact affine reparameterization when the complementary upper restriction \(s_j^L\le u_j-\ell_j\), respectively \(s_j^U\le u_j-\ell_j\), is retained. Substituting either expression into a valid inequality and later eliminating the bound slack by the inverse identity preserves validity; the chosen orientation changes the coefficient sign exposed to rounding or strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely bounded variable can be expressed exactly as lower bound plus slack or upper bound minus slack, exposing different coefficient signs for strengthening.
assumptions_latex: Both explicit bounds remain enforced after substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either bounded-slack substitution gives a bijective representation of \(x_j\in[\ell_j,u_j]\) and preserves inequality validity under inverse substitution.

notation.meaning: nonnegative slack above the explicit lower bound
nonnegative slack below the explicit upper bound

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit-bound slack substitutions are exact affine identities
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Implied-Bound Substitution
children.top_down_role: Strengthening based on variable bounds inferred from other constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Implied-Bound Substitution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination substitution using globally valid, model-implied affine bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^{1+q}\) satisfy the valid row \(a x+r^\top z\ge b\). If \(a>0\) and \(x\le U(z)\) is valid for every \((x,z)\in S\), then replacing \(x\) by its implied upper bound yields the valid inequality \(aU(z)+r^\top z\ge b\). If \(a<0\) and \(x\ge L(z)\) is valid on \(S\), the analogous substitution gives \(aL(z)+r^\top z\ge b\). When \(L\) or \(U\) is affine, the substituted relation is a linear valid inequality in \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable may be eliminated from a valid row by substituting a globally valid implied bound selected according to the coefficient’s sign.
assumptions_latex: \(a x+r^\top z\ge b\) is valid for \(S\).
The substituted bound holds globally on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(aU(z)+r^\top z\ge b\) for \(a>0\), or \(aL(z)+r^\top z\ge b\) for \(a<0\), is valid for \(S\).

notation.meaning: Valid implied lower and upper bounds on the substituted variable.

children.title: Bound-Quality Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits caused by weak, invalid, or representation-sensitive bound information.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Quality Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and strength limits for bound substitution in a greater-than row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid row \(a x+r^\top z\ge b\) with \(a>0\), a globally valid upper bound guarantees valid upper-bound substitution. If \(U_1(z)\le U_2(z)\) on the relevant domain, the inequality obtained from \(U_1\) dominates the one obtained from \(U_2\); hence looser bounds weaken substitution. A finite substitution is unavailable when no finite valid upper bound exists. An upper bound that is not valid can destroy validity: for \(S=\{(1,0)\}\), the valid row \(x+z\ge1\) combined with the false bound \(x\le0\) produces \(z\ge1\), which is violated on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally valid tighter bounds provide stronger substituted cuts; absent finite bounds prevent finite substitution, and an invalid bound may produce an invalid cut.
assumptions_latex: \(a>0\) in the valid row \(a x+r^\top z\ge b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global validity of the substituted upper bound guarantees validity, tighter upper bounds give stronger substituted inequalities, and a nonvalid bound does not provide a validity guarantee.

notation.meaning: Candidate upper-bound functions with the first no larger than the second.
Feasible set used in the counterexample.

knowledge_statements.title: Chvátal–Gomory Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one aggregation-and-rounding form for a pure-integer linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), and \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\). For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) such that \(c=A^\top\lambda\in\mathbb Z^n\), the inequality \[c^\top x\le\lfloor\lambda^\top b\rfloor\] is a rank-one Chvátal–Gomory inequality for \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\). The intersection of \(P\) with all halfspaces obtained in this way is the rank-one Chvátal–Gomory closure of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-one Chvátal–Gomory inequality is obtained by nonnegative row aggregation with integral resulting coefficients and rounding down the aggregated right-hand side; intersecting all such halfspaces with the relaxation gives the rank-one closure.
assumptions_latex: The target solutions belong to \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) with \(A^\top\lambda\in\mathbb Z^n\), the inequality \((A^\top\lambda)^\top x\le\lfloor\lambda^\top b\rfloor\) is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\).

notation.meaning: Integral coefficient vector of the aggregated row.
