knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chvátal inequalities and the Chvátal closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition, validity, multiplier characterization, closure representation, and immediate inclusion properties in the mixed-integer setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\), \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(C=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus I\), and \(S=\{x\in P:x_j\in\mathbb Z\ (j\in I)\}\). For a split \((\pi,\pi_0)\), the inequality \(\pi x\le\pi_0\) is a Chvátal inequality if \(P\cap\{x:\pi x\ge\pi_0+1\}=\varnothing\). It is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\) and is a split inequality. If \(\delta=\max_{x\in P}\pi x\) and \(\pi_0=\lfloor\delta\rfloor\), it cuts off part of \(P\) if and only if \(\delta\notin\mathbb Z\). For a primitive split normal \(\pi\), \(\operatorname{conv}\{x\in\mathbb Z^I\times\mathbb R^C:\pi x\le\delta\}=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\pi x\le\lfloor\delta\rfloor\}\). If \(P\ne\varnothing\), then \(\pi x\le\pi_0\) is Chvátal if and only if there is \(u\ge0\) with \(uA=\pi\) and \(\pi_0\ge\lfloor ub\rfloor\). Moreover, \(P^{Ch}=\{x\in P:(uA)x\le\lfloor ub\rfloor\text{ for every }u\ge0\text{ with }uA_I\in\mathbb Z^I,\ uA_C=0\}\), and \(S\subseteq P^{\mathrm{split}}\subseteq P^{Ch}\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split inequality is Chvátal when the opposite side of its unit-width split contains no point of the relaxation. It is valid for the mixed-integer hull and has an aggregation-and-rounding characterization. Imposing all such inequalities defines the Chvátal closure, which contains the split closure and lies inside the original relaxation.
assumptions_latex: P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\},\quad I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\},\quad C=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus I.
(\pi,\pi_0)\text{ is a split for the integer variables, with }\pi_I\in\mathbb Z^I,\ \pi_C=0,\ \pi_0\in\mathbb Z.
\delta=\max\{\pi x:x\in P\}\text{ is finite and attained in the maximum-based assertions; the convex-hull assertion additionally uses a primitive }\pi.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi x\le\pi_0\text{ is Chvátal}\iff P\cap\{x:\pi x\ge\pi_0+1\}=\varnothing;\quad P^{Ch}=\{x\in P:(uA)x\le\lfloor ub\rfloor\ \forall u\ge0,\ uA_I\in\mathbb Z^I,\ uA_C=0\},\quad S\subseteq P^{\mathrm{split}}\subseteq P^{Ch}\subseteq P.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chvátal–Gomory Valid-Inequality Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation and coefficient/right-hand-side flooring for a nonnegative integer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax\le b\}, let A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_n]\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}, let X=P\cap\mathbb Z^n, and choose u\in\mathbb R_+^m. Then \sum_{j=1}^n(ua_j)x_j\le ub is valid for P. Because x\ge0, \sum_{j=1}^n\lfloor ua_j\rfloor x_j\le ub is valid for P. Because the latter left-hand side is integral on X, \sum_{j=1}^n\lfloor ua_j\rfloor x_j\le\lfloor ub\rfloor is valid for X.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate Ax ≤ b with nonnegative multipliers, floor the aggregated coefficients using variable nonnegativity, and floor the right-hand side using integrality. The resulting Chvátal–Gomory inequality is valid for X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j=1}^n\lfloor ua_j\rfloor x_j\le\lfloor ub\rfloor\quad\text{is valid for }X

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extension of a face cut to the ambient polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A Chvátal–Gomory cut for a face of a rational polytope has an ambient-polytope Chvátal–Gomory cut with the same restriction to that face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $F$ be a face of a rational polytope $P$. If $c^Tx\le\lfloor d\rfloor$ is a Chvátal--Gomory cut for $F$, then there exists a Chvátal--Gomory cut $(c')^Tx\le\lfloor d'\rfloor$ for $P$ such that $F\cap\{x:(c')^Tx\le\lfloor d'\rfloor\}=F\cap\{x:c^Tx\le\lfloor d\rfloor\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every Chvátal–Gomory cut for a face of a rational polytope can be matched by a Chvátal–Gomory cut for the whole polytope that has exactly the same effect on the face.
assumptions_latex: c^Tx\le\lfloor d\rfloor\text{ is a Chvátal--Gomory cut for }F
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(c',d'):\ (c')^Tx\le\lfloor d'\rfloor\text{ is a Chvátal--Gomory cut for }P\text{ and }F\cap\{x:(c')^Tx\le\lfloor d'\rfloor\}=F\cap\{x:c^Tx\le\lfloor d\rfloor\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chvátal–Gomory inequality by aggregation and rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the pure-integer aggregation-and-rounding cut and its equivalent valid-inequality formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $a_i^Tx\le b_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,m$ and $y_i\ge0$, set $c=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i a_i$ and $d=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i b_i$. Every solution of the system satisfies $c^Tx\le d$. If $c\in\mathbb Z^n$, every integral solution satisfies the Chvátal--Gomory inequality $c^Tx\le\lfloor d\rfloor$. Equivalently, if $c^Tx\le d$ is valid for a polyhedron $P$ and $c\in\mathbb Z^n$, then $c^Tx\le\lfloor d\rfloor$ is valid for $P\cap\mathbb Z^n$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative aggregation of a linear inequality system gives a valid inequality. If its coefficient vector is integral, rounding the right-hand side down yields a Chvátal–Gomory inequality valid for every integral feasible vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in\mathbb Z^n,\ a_i^Tx\le b_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\implies c^Tx\le\lfloor d\rfloor

children.top_down_role: Chvátal–Gomory cuts represented through multipliers on a linear system.

knowledge_statements.title: System-Form Chvátal–Gomory Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier representation relative to a displayed inequality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the displayed formulation \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\), its system-form rank-one Chvátal–Gomory family is \[\mathcal C(A,b)=\left\{(A^\top\lambda)^\top x\le\lfloor b^\top\lambda\rfloor:\lambda\ge0,\ A^\top\lambda\in\mathbb Z^n\right\}.\] Thus separation in system form searches directly over nonnegative row multipliers. The corresponding closure is \(P_{CG}(A,b)=P\cap\bigcap_{H\in\mathcal C(A,b)}H\), where each member of \(\mathcal C(A,b)\) is interpreted as its defining halfspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: System-form CG cuts are generated directly from nonnegative multipliers of the rows in a particular linear inequality formulation.
assumptions_latex: The variables \(x\) are integer in the target set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every member of \(\mathcal C(A,b)\) is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\).

notation.meaning: Intersection of the formulation with its rank-one CG cuts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: System-form representations of mixed-integer Chvátal inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relevant or irredundant multiplier-and-rounding forms for nonnegative mixed-integer systems written using inequalities or equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \begin{aligned}P_{\le}&=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\},\\ P_{=}&=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax=b\},\qquad C=[n]\setminus I.\end{aligned}\quad\begin{cases}\text{For }P_{\le},\text{ the relevant inequalities may be taken as }\displaystyle\sum_{j\in I}\lfloor(uA)_j\rfloor x_j\le\lfloor ub\rfloor,\quad u\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ uA_C\ge0.\\\text{For }P_{=},\text{ every irredundant Chvátal inequality has this form for some }u\in\mathbb R^m\text{ satisfying }uA_C\ge0\text{ and }ub\notin\mathbb Z.\end{cases}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let I index the integer-constrained variables and let C be its complement. For a nonnegative inequality-form system, the relevant Chvátal inequalities may be restricted to rounded multiplier inequalities with a nonnegative multiplier and uA_C nonnegative. For a nonnegative equality-form system, every irredundant Chvátal inequality has the same rounded form for an unrestricted multiplier satisfying uA_C nonnegative and ub nonintegral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j\in I}\lfloor(uA)_j\rfloor x_j\le\lfloor ub\rfloor\quad\text{under the corresponding multiplier conditions}

children.title: Projected Chvátal–Gomory Cuts
children.top_down_role: Chvátal–Gomory cuts transferred from an extended or alternative formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Chvátal–Gomory Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CG aggregation in an extended system followed by elimination of auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{n+p}:Ax+By\le b\}\), with \((x,y)\) required integral, and let \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\). If \(\lambda\ge0\), \(A^\top\lambda\in\mathbb Z^n\), and \(B^\top\lambda=0\), then the extended-system CG inequality contains no auxiliary variables and projects directly to \[(A^\top\lambda)^\top x\le\lfloor b^\top\lambda\rfloor.\] This inequality is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\). More generally, projected CG relaxations are obtained by taking the \(x\)-projection after imposing CG inequalities in the extended space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CG cut derived in an extended formulation becomes an original-space cut when its auxiliary-variable coefficients vanish, or after projecting the strengthened extension.
assumptions_latex: Both original and auxiliary variables are integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((A^\top\lambda)^\top x\le\lfloor b^\top\lambda\rfloor\) is valid for \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q\cap\mathbb Z^{n+p})\).

notation.meaning: Extended formulation in original and auxiliary variables.
Projection of the extended formulation onto the original variables.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied. Moreover, the body claims validity for \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\), while the conclusion correctly limits validity to \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q\cap\mathbb Z^{n+p})\); these sets need not coincide because an integer projected point may lack an integer auxiliary lift.

children.title: Formulation-Dependence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Variation in available cuts caused by system representation or projection choice.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation-Dependence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes intrinsic CG closure from extended-formulation projection effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed nonempty rational polyhedron \(P\), the full rank-one Chvátal–Gomory closure is intrinsic: replacing one exact rational inequality description of \(P\) by another does not change that closure. This invariance does not imply commutation with extended-space projection. For an integral-variable extension \(Q\) with \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\), one has \[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{CG})\subseteq P_{CG},\] because every CG inequality of \(P\) lifts to a valid zero-auxiliary-coefficient CG inequality for \(Q\). The inclusion can be strict, so rank and one-round strength may depend on the chosen extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CG closure is independent of an exact inequality description in fixed space, but adding integer auxiliary variables and projecting can strengthen one-round closure.
assumptions_latex: The extension uses integer auxiliary variables and satisfies \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{CG})\subseteq P_{CG}\), potentially strictly.

notation.meaning: Rank-one CG closure in the original space.
Rank-one CG closure of the extended formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-space invariance and projected-closure inclusion are plausible standard claims, but the potentially strict inclusion and its extension assumptions require an authoritative locator and an inspectable supporting example.

children.title: Strong Chvátal–Gomory Cuts
children.top_down_role: Strengthened rounding cuts used in general-purpose separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Chvátal–Gomory Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance-based interpretation within the rank-one CG family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be rational and let \(\mathcal H_{CG}(P)\) denote its rank-one Chvátal–Gomory halfspaces. A member \(H\in\mathcal H_{CG}(P)\) is strong, in the dominance sense, if there is no \(H'\in\mathcal H_{CG}(P)\) such that \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\subseteq H'\subsetneq H\). Equivalently, the defining CG inequality is undominated within the chosen rank-one family. General-purpose separation may therefore discard a generated CG inequality whenever another available CG inequality defines a strictly smaller valid halfspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the dominance sense, a strong CG cut is a rank-one CG inequality not strictly dominated by another cut from the same family.
assumptions_latex: Dominance is compared within a fixed rank-one CG family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A strong CG halfspace is inclusion-minimal among CG halfspaces containing \(P\cap\mathbb Z^n\).

notation.meaning: Rank-one CG halfspaces associated with the polyhedron.
Candidate valid halfspaces compared by inclusion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The title may denote a specific coefficient-strengthened CG family rather than merely undominated rank-one cuts. In addition, global halfspace inclusion is narrower than common dominance relative to a relaxation. An authoritative definition is required before fixing the mathematical version.

children.title: Gomory Fractional Cut Family
children.top_down_role: Pure-integer tableau cuts and their arithmetic algorithmic regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity of the Gomory fractional-cut equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer tableau-row representation of a Gomory fractional cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\bar a_{i0}\notin\mathbb Z\), define \(f_{ij}=\bar a_{ij}-\lfloor\bar a_{ij}\rfloor\) for \(j\in H\) and \(f_{i0}=\bar a_{i0}-\lfloor\bar a_{i0}\rfloor\). Then \[\sum_{j\in H}f_{ij}x_j=f_{i0}+x_{n+1},\qquad x_{n+1}\in\mathbb Z_+,\] is a valid equality for \(S^0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a tableau row with fractional right-hand side, its fractional parts yield a valid equality for the pure-integer feasible set after introducing a nonnegative integer slack variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j\in H}f_{ij}x_j=f_{i0}+x_{n+1},\quad x_{n+1}\in\mathbb Z_+,\text{ is valid for }S^0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gomory fractional cuts are Chvátal–Gomory inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of an aggregated-row Gomory fractional cut with a Chvátal–Gomory inequality for an integral pure-integer system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S=\{x\in\mathbb Z_+^n:Ax\le b\}, where (A,b) is an integral m\times(n+1) matrix. For any \lambda\in\mathbb R^m, the Gomory fractional cut derived from the aggregated equality \lambda(A,I)x=\lambda b is a Chv\'atal\text{--}Gomory inequality for S obtained with weights u_i=\lambda_i-\lfloor\lambda_i\rfloor for every i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integral nonnegative pure-integer system, the Gomory fractional cut obtained from a weighted aggregation of the equality-form constraints is a Chvátal–Gomory inequality whose weights are the fractional parts of the aggregation weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The associated Gomory fractional cut is a Chv\'atal\text{--}Gomory inequality for }S\text{ with }u_i=\lambda_i-\lfloor\lambda_i\rfloor\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gomory fractional-cut construction from a fractional optimal tableau row
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer tableau-row cut construction, dual-simplex reoptimization, and the failure of unrestricted basis and row choices to ensure finite convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Given an optimal tableau row }x_h+\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_{hj}x_j=\bar b_h\text{ with }\bar b_h\notin\mathbb Z,\quad x_h+\sum_{j\in N}\lfloor\bar a_{hj}\rfloor x_j\le\lfloor\bar b_h\rfloor\text{ is valid for }P\cap\mathbb Z^n\text{ and excludes the current LP optimum. Setting }f_j=\bar a_{hj}-\lfloor\bar a_{hj}\rfloor\text{ and }f_0=\bar b_h-\lfloor\bar b_h\rfloor\text{ gives }\sum_{j\in N}-f_jx_j+x_{n+1}=-f_0.\text{ The augmented tableau is dual feasible and primal infeasible, permitting dual-simplex reoptimization; unrestricted repetition is not guaranteed to terminate finitely.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a pure integer program in nonnegative equality form, a fractional basic row of an optimal LP tableau yields a rounded inequality valid for every integer solution and violated by the current LP optimum. Subtracting the row produces the Gomory fractional-cut equation with an integer slack variable. The augmented tableau may be reoptimized by dual simplex, but arbitrary basis and source-row choices do not guarantee finite convergence.
assumptions_latex: B\text{ is an optimal basis of the LP relaxation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_h+\sum_{j\in N}\lfloor\bar a_{hj}\rfloor x_j\le\lfloor\bar b_h\rfloor,\qquad \sum_{j\in N}-f_jx_j+x_{n+1}=-f_0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gomory fractional cut from an aggregated equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer nonnegative systems put into equality form using nonnegative integer slack variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S=\{x\in\mathbb Z_+^n:Ax\le b\}, where (A,b) is integral, and let S^e=\{x\in\mathbb Z_+^{n+m}:(A,I)x=b\}. For \lambda\in\mathbb R^m, define \bar a_j=\lambda a_j, \bar b=\lambda b, f_j=\bar a_j-\lfloor\bar a_j\rfloor, g_i=\lambda_i-\lfloor\lambda_i\rfloor, and f_0=\bar b-\lfloor\bar b\rfloor. The valid inequality \sum_{j=1}^n f_jx_j+\sum_{i=1}^m g_ix_{n+i}\ge f_0 is the Gomory fractional cut derived from \lambda(A,I)x=\lambda b.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integral pure-integer system in equality form, take a weighted aggregation of the equations. The inequality formed from the fractional parts of the aggregated original-variable coefficients, slack-variable coefficients, and right-hand side is valid and is called the corresponding Gomory fractional cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j=1}^n(\lambda a_j-\lfloor\lambda a_j\rfloor)x_j+\sum_{i=1}^m(\lambda_i-\lfloor\lambda_i\rfloor)x_{n+i}\ge \lambda b-\lfloor\lambda b\rfloor\text{ is a valid Gomory fractional cut for }S^e.

children.title: Single-Row Fractional Cuts
children.top_down_role: Fractional cuts associated with individual pure-integer tableau rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Row Fractional Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Gomory fractional cut from one pure-integer tableau row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a tableau row \(x_B=\bar b-\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_jx_j\), where \(x_B\) and all \(x_j\) are nonnegative integer variables and \(f_0=\bar b-\lfloor\bar b\rfloor\) satisfies \(0<f_0<1\). Writing \(f_j=\bar a_j-\lfloor\bar a_j\rfloor\), the associated single-row Gomory fractional cut is \[\sum_{j\in N}f_jx_j\ge f_0.\] It is valid for every integer solution satisfying the tableau row and cuts off the current basic solution with \(x_j=0\) for all \(j\in N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional parts of one pure-integer tableau row define a valid cut violated by the current fractional basic solution.
assumptions_latex: The tableau row contains only integer-constrained variables.
The row right-hand side is fractional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j\in N}f_jx_j\ge f_0\) is valid and excludes the current tableau solution.

notation.meaning: Fractional part of the tableau right-hand side.
Fractional part of tableau coefficient \(\bar a_j\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity of the single-row Gomory fractional cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded validity statement for a pure-integer single equation with nonnegative variables and a fractional right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_n,a_0\in\mathbb R\), with \(a_0\notin\mathbb Z\). If \(x\in\mathbb Z_+^n\) satisfies \(\sum_{j=1}^n a_jx_j=a_0\), then the Gomory fractional inequality \[\sum_{j=1}^n\bigl(a_j-\lfloor a_j\rfloor\bigr)x_j\geq a_0-\lfloor a_0\rfloor\] is valid for every such \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative integer variables satisfying one linear equation with a nonintegral right-hand side, the fractional parts of the coefficients, weighted by the variables, sum to at least the fractional part of the right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j=1}^n\left(a_j-\lfloor a_j\rfloor\right)x_j\geq a_0-\lfloor a_0\rfloor.

knowledge_statements.title: All-Integer Tableau Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residue-cut tableau scheme using integer numerators and denominators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a rational pure-integer program and maintain each tableau row in integer form \(d x_B+\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j=r\), where \(d>0\) and \(a_j,r\in\mathbb Z\). If \(d\nmid r\), set \(r_0=r\bmod d\) and \(r_j=a_j\bmod d\), using residues in \(\{0,\ldots,d-1\}\), and append \[\sum_{j\in N}r_jx_j\ge r_0.\] Introduce an integer slack and update the tableau by integer-preserving pivots or fraction-free row operations. Stop when every basic integer variable is integral, or when the tableau certifies infeasibility or unboundedness; output the resulting integer solution or certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All-integer tableau methods store scaled integer rows, generate modular residue cuts from nondivisible right-hand sides, and update through integer-preserving pivots.
assumptions_latex: All structural variables are nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each residue cut is valid and excludes the current row solution whenever \(0<r_0<d\).

notation.meaning: Positive row denominator or scaling factor.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The modular residue cut is plausible, but the claimed tableau update, stopping conditions, and certificate outputs combine variant-specific algorithmic assertions without a cited pivot rule or termination theorem.

children.title: Lexicographic Gomory Methods
children.top_down_role: Lexicographic variants supporting finite progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Gomory Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pure-integer cutting-plane method with lexicographic progress control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a bounded rational pure-integer linear program, impose a symbolic lexicographic perturbation of the objective and right-hand sides and solve the perturbed relaxation exactly. If the lexicographically optimal basic solution is integral, return it. Otherwise select the first fractional basic integer row in the prescribed lexicographic order, append its Gomory fractional cut, and restore lexicographic optimality by lexicographic dual-simplex pivots. Repeat. Under the classical pure-integer assumptions and exact lexicographic pivot rule, successive tableaux make strict lexicographic progress, so the method terminates finitely with an optimal integer solution or an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographic perturbation, ordered fractional-row cuts, and lexicographic dual-simplex pivots prevent cycling and give finite progress for bounded pure-integer programs.
assumptions_latex: The program is rational, bounded, and purely integer.
Pivots and perturbations are handled exactly.
The classical lexicographic row and pivot rules are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cutting-plane sequence terminates finitely with an optimal integer solution or an infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: Fixed lexicographic ordering used for progress and pivot selection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Finite termination depends on the exact classical lexicographic perturbation, row-selection, and pivot rules. Those rules are not specified sufficiently or supported by a theorem locator.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Section 8.7.2: The Mixed Integer Rounding Inequality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed-integer rounding inequalities and their closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the basic mixed-set inequality, its aggregation-based extension, and the induced closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=\beta-\lfloor\beta\rfloor\). For \(M=\{(\xi,v)\in\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R_+:\xi-v\leq\beta\}\), \(\operatorname{conv}(M)\) is described by \(v\geq0\), \(\xi-v\leq\beta\), and \(\xi-\frac{1}{1-f}v\leq\lfloor\beta\rfloor\). More generally, let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b\}\), and suppose a valid inequality for \(P\) is written as \(\pi x-(\gamma-cx)\leq\beta\), where \(\pi_I\in\mathbb Z^I\), \(\pi_C=0\), and \(cx\leq\gamma\) is valid for \(P\). Then
\[\pi x-\frac{1}{1-f}(\gamma-cx)\leq\lfloor\beta\rfloor\]
is a mixed-integer rounding inequality. MIR inequalities are equivalent to split inequalities. The MIR closure is \(P^{\mathrm{MIR}}=\{x\in P:x\text{ satisfies every MIR inequality}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of the basic one-row mixed set is obtained by adding its simple rounding inequality. Replacing the integer variable by an integral aggregation and the nonnegative continuous variable by a valid slack yields the general MIR inequality. MIR inequalities are equivalent to split inequalities, and the MIR closure consists of points satisfying every MIR inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi x-\frac{\gamma-cx}{1-f}\leq\lfloor\beta\rfloor\text{ is an MIR inequality, and }P^{\mathrm{MIR}}=\{x\in P:x\text{ satisfies every MIR inequality}\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Mixed-Integer Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical one-integer, one-continuous-variable set underlying basic MIR validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(b\in\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Z\), let \(f=b-\lfloor b\rfloor\in(0,1)\). The basic mixed-integer set is \[S(b)=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R_+:x+s\ge b\}.\] Its basic mixed-integer rounding inequality is \[x+\frac{s}{f}\ge\lceil b\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The basic mixed-integer set consists of an integer variable and a nonnegative continuous slack satisfying one lower-bound row; its MIR inequality rounds the integer threshold while scaling the slack by the fractional part of the right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(x+s/f\ge\lceil b\rceil\) is valid for \(S(b)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded MIR Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic MIR inequality with explicit finite bounds on the integer variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L,U\in\mathbb Z\), \(L\le U\), and \(b\notin\mathbb Z\), with \(f=b-\lfloor b\rfloor\). For the bounded basic set \[S_{L,U}(b)=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R_+:L\le x\le U,\ x+s\ge b\},\] the bounded MIR form is \[x+\frac{s}{f}\ge\lceil b\rceil,\qquad L\le x\le U,\qquad s\ge0.\] If \(U<\lceil b\rceil\), the same inequality remains valid and enforces the positive slack requirement \(s\ge f(\lceil b\rceil-x)\). Bounds may subsequently support complementing or coefficient strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding finite integer bounds to the basic MIR set preserves the MIR inequality and can expose additional slack requirements or strengthening opportunities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x+s/f\ge\lceil b\rceil\) is valid for \(S_{L,U}(b)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Complemented MIR Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MIR construction after complementing integer variables having finite integral upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^q\) be a mixed-integer set, and let \(a^{\mathsf T}x+d^{\mathsf T}y\le b\) be valid for \(S\). For an index set \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\), assume \(0\le x_j\le u_j\) with \(u_j\in\mathbb Z_+\), and introduce \(z_j=u_j-x_j\) for every \(j\in J\). Rewrite the row in \((x_{\bar J},z_J,y)\). If that transformed row satisfies the hypotheses of the selected validity-preserving MIR operator, apply the operator and substitute \(z_j=u_j-x_j\) back. The resulting complemented MIR inequality is valid for \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complement integer variables using finite integral upper bounds, apply a valid MIR rule to the transformed row, and substitute back; the pulled-back inequality is valid for the original set.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^q\), and \(a^{\mathsf T}x+d^{\mathsf T}y\le b\) is valid for \(S\).
\(0\le x_j\le u_j\) and \(u_j\in\mathbb Z_+\) for every \(j\in J\).
The transformed row satisfies the hypotheses of the selected MIR operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality obtained after substituting \(z_j=u_j-x_j\) into the transformed MIR inequality is valid for \(S\).

children.title: Bound–Complement Representation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between bound-based and complemented representations of MIR cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound–Complement Representation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity equivalence under the affine substitution induced by finite integral bounds on integer variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^q\), fix \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and assume \(0\le x_j\le u_j\) with \(u_j\in\mathbb Z_+\) for every \(j\in J\). Let \(T_J\) replace each \(x_j\) by \(z_j=u_j-x_j\), and set \(S^J=T_J(S)\). Then \(T_J:S\to S^J\) is an affine bijection with inverse given by \(x_j=u_j-z_j\). Consequently, an inequality is valid for \(S\) if and only if its literal transport through \(T_J\) is valid for \(S^J\). In particular, a MIR inequality derived in either representation and then literally transported has identical pointwise slack at corresponding points; this does not assert that independent MIR applications commute with complementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integral upper-bound complementation is an affine bijection. It preserves validity and the slack of an inequality transported between the two representations, but independent MIR applications need not generate the same cut.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le x_j\le u_j\) and \(u_j\in\mathbb Z_+\) for every \(j\in J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An inequality is valid for \(S\) if and only if its literal image under \(T_J\) is valid for \(S^J=T_J(S)\).

notation.meaning: upper-bound complementation map on indices J
image of the original feasible set under complementation
finite integral upper bound of x_j

children.title: Aggregated MIR Cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregated MIR Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-row MIR cuts obtained from nonnegative aggregation of valid constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given valid rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+d_i^{\mathsf T}y\le b_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), choose multipliers \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\). Form the valid aggregate \((\sum_i\lambda_i a_i)^{\mathsf T}x+(\sum_i\lambda_i d_i)^{\mathsf T}y\le\sum_i\lambda_i b_i\), normalize it according to the selected MIR convention, and apply \(\operatorname{MIR}\). Output the resulting inequality if its fractional datum is nonzero and it separates the point under consideration; otherwise output no cut. Every emitted inequality is valid because nonnegative aggregation preserves validity before rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegatively combine valid rows, normalize the aggregate, apply MIR, and retain the cut when it is defined and separating.
assumptions_latex: Each row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+d_i^{\mathsf T}y\le b_i\) is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality emitted by \(\operatorname{MIR}(\sum_i\lambda_i(a_i,d_i,b_i))\) is valid for the common mixed-integer feasible set.

children.title: Multirow MIR Cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Multirow MIR Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MIR-type inequalities using several tableau rows jointly rather than one fixed aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_B=f+Rs\) be a subsystem of \(k\ge2\) tableau rows, where designated components of \(x_B\) are integer and \(s\ge0\) contains nonbasic variables with specified integrality. A multirow MIR cut is a valid inequality \(\pi^{\mathsf T}s\ge1\) derived from the joint lattice-free or disjunctive relaxation of these \(k\) rows. Its coefficients depend on the column vectors \(R_{ullet j}\), not merely on one scalar aggregation \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}R_{ullet j}\); consequently, a multirow cut need not be representable as MIR applied to a single aggregated row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multirow MIR cut uses several tableau equations jointly, and its columnwise coefficients need not arise from any single row aggregation.
assumptions_latex: The integrality designations of \(x_B\) and \(s\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The joint relaxation yields a valid inequality \(\pi^{\mathsf T}s\ge1\), potentially outside the family of single-aggregate MIR cuts.

notation.meaning: column of tableau coefficients for nonbasic variable j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement contains malformed occurrences of the tableau column notation and conflates multirow MIR cuts with general lattice-free or disjunctive cuts. An authoritative definition and a source for the asserted failure of single-aggregate representation are required.

children.title: MIR Row-Combination Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: MIR Row-Combination Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes single-row, aggregated-row, and genuinely joint multirow MIR constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For valid rows indexed by \(I\), three regimes are distinguished. Selecting one row \(i\in I\) and applying MIR is the single-row regime. Choosing \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^I\), forming \(\sum_i\lambda_i r_i\), and applying MIR once is the aggregated-row regime. Retaining at least two rows as a vector system and deriving coefficients from their joint disjunction is the multirow regime. Every single-row cut is aggregated with a unit multiplier, whereas a multirow cut belongs to the aggregated regime only when some \(\lambda\) reproduces all of its coefficients after MIR normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MIR constructions separate into single-row, nonnegative aggregated-row, and genuinely joint multirow regimes; only the first is always a special aggregate.
assumptions_latex: All input rows are valid for the same mixed-integer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{single}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\mathrm{aggregate}}\), while \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{multi}}\) is not generally contained in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{aggregate}}\).

notation.meaning: the i-th valid row, including its right-hand side
cut families generated in the three regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The single-row inclusion is plausible, but the asserted noncontainment depends on precise definitions of the aggregate and multirow families. No source is supplied for that substantive family relation.

knowledge_statements.title: MIR Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized MIR coefficient representation for a fractional mixed-integer tableau row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_B=b-\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j\), where \(x_B\) is integer, \(x_j\ge0\), and \(f_0=b-\lfloor b\rfloor\in(0,1)\). For integer nonbasic indices \(I\), set \(f_j=a_j-\lfloor a_j\rfloor\). The normalized MIR representation has coefficients \(f_j/f_0\) when \(j\in I\) and \(f_j\le f_0\), \((1-f_j)/(1-f_0)\) when \(j\in I\) and \(f_j>f_0\), \(a_j/f_0\) when \(j\notin I\) and \(a_j\ge0\), and \(-a_j/(1-f_0)\) otherwise; their weighted sum is at least \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized MIR representation assigns piecewise coefficients determined by row fractions, integrality, sign, and the fractional basic value.
assumptions_latex: \(x_B=b-\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j\) is a valid tableau row.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\sum_{j\in N}\pi_jx_j\ge1\), with the stated coefficients \(\pi_j\), is valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Split-Cut Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-row cut represented by the split disjunction on the integer basic variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the tableau row \(x_B=b-\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j\) with \(x_B\in\mathbb Z\) and \(f_0=b-\lfloor b\rfloor\in(0,1)\), every feasible point satisfies the split disjunction \(x_B\le\lfloor b\rfloor\) or \(x_B\ge\lceil b\rceil\). Intersecting the nonnegative tableau cone with the two boundary hyperplanes and expressing the resulting intersection inequality in the nonbasic variables gives \(\sum_{j\in N}\pi_jx_j\ge1\), where the ray coefficient \(\pi_j\) is the reciprocal of the first intersection distance with either side of the split.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fractional tableau row induces an integer split; intersecting each tableau ray with its two boundaries yields the normalized split cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The intersection inequality \(\sum_{j\in N}\pi_jx_j\ge1\) is valid for the split-disjunctive relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: GMI Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical normalized GMI inequality from one fractional integer-basic tableau row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_B=b-\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j\), with \(x_B\in\mathbb Z\), \(x_j\ge0\), and \(f_0=b-\lfloor b\rfloor\in(0,1)\). For integer nonbasic variables define \(f_j=a_j-\lfloor a_j\rfloor\). The GMI inequality is \[\sum_{j\in I:f_j\le f_0}\frac{f_j}{f_0}x_j+\sum_{j\in I:f_j>f_0}\frac{1-f_j}{1-f_0}x_j+\sum_{j\notin I:a_j\ge0}\frac{a_j}{f_0}x_j+\sum_{j\notin I:a_j<0}\frac{-a_j}{1-f_0}x_j\ge1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The single-row GMI inequality has piecewise coefficients based on integer coefficient fractions and continuous coefficient signs.

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Family Correspondence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-row correspondence among MIR, GMI, and the appropriately strengthened split-cut representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_B=b-\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j\) be a tableau row with \(x_B\in\mathbb Z\), \(x_j\ge0\), fixed nonbasic-variable integrality, and \(b\notin\mathbb Z\). Apply the MIR and GMI constructions using the same tableau sign convention and normalization. For the split \(x_B\le\lfloor b\rfloor\) or \(x_B\ge\lceil b\rceil\), use the split intersection inequality strengthened by integer modularization on every integer nonbasic variable. The three normalized inequalities then have identical coefficients. Without this strengthening, the raw split intersection coefficients can differ from the MIR and GMI coefficients when integer nonbasic variables are present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one fractional tableau row, normalized MIR and GMI coincide with the split intersection cut after the required integer-variable strengthening; the raw split cut need not coincide when integer nonbasic variables are present.
assumptions_latex: All three constructions use the same tableau representation and normalization.
The split intersection inequality is strengthened by integer modularization for integer nonbasic variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi^{\mathrm{MIR}}=\pi^{\mathrm{GMI}}=\pi^{\mathrm{split,str}}\) for the compatible strengthened single-row representations.

children.title: Gomory Mixed-Integer Cut Family
children.top_down_role: Mixed-integer tableau cuts and their generation from simplex representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Single-row Gomory mixed-integer inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the GMI inequality obtained from a simplex-tableau row whose basic variable is integer-constrained and whose right-hand side is fractional, and records exclusion of the associated basic solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax=b\}\), let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index the integer-constrained variables, and let \(C=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus I\). For a feasible basis \(B\), consider a tableau row \(x_i+\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_{ij}x_j=\bar b_i\), where \(i\in B\cap I\). Define \(f_0=\bar b_i-\lfloor\bar b_i\rfloor\in(0,1)\) and \(f_j=\bar a_{ij}-\lfloor\bar a_{ij}\rfloor\) for \(j\in N\). The associated Gomory mixed-integer inequality is
\[
\sum_{\substack{j\in N\cap I\\ f_j\le f_0}}\frac{f_j}{f_0}x_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in N\cap I\\ f_j>f_0}}\frac{1-f_j}{1-f_0}x_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in N\cap C\\ \bar a_{ij}\ge0}}\frac{\bar a_{ij}}{f_0}x_j-\sum_{\substack{j\in N\cap C\\ \bar a_{ij}<0}}\frac{\bar a_{ij}}{1-f_0}x_j\ge1.
\]
The basic solution associated with \(B\), satisfying \(x_j^*=0\) for every \(j\in N\), violates this inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible simplex-tableau row with an integer-constrained basic variable and a fractional right-hand side, the displayed coefficient rule gives the Gomory mixed-integer inequality. It cuts off the associated basic solution because every nonbasic variable is zero there, making the left-hand side zero.
assumptions_latex: P=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax=b\}\text{ is a rational polyhedron}
B\text{ is a feasible basis with tableau row }x_i+\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_{ij}x_j=\bar b_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{\substack{j\in N\cap I\\ f_j\le f_0}}\frac{f_j}{f_0}x_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in N\cap I\\ f_j>f_0}}\frac{1-f_j}{1-f_0}x_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in N\cap C\\ \bar a_{ij}\ge0}}\frac{\bar a_{ij}}{f_0}x_j-\sum_{\substack{j\in N\cap C\\ \bar a_{ij}<0}}\frac{\bar a_{ij}}{1-f_0}x_j\ge1,\qquad x^*\text{ violates the inequality}

children.title: Single-Row GMI Cuts
children.top_down_role: GMI cuts derived from individual mixed-integer tableau rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Row GMI Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generation of one exact normalized GMI cut from an eligible fractional tableau row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a simplex-tableau row \(x_B=b-\sum_{j\in N}a_jx_j\) whose basic variable satisfies \(x_B\in\mathbb Z\), with every nonbasic variable satisfying \(x_j\ge0\). Set \(f_0=b-\lfloor b\rfloor\). If \(f_0=0\), output no cut. Otherwise, for each integer nonbasic index \(j\in I\), set \(f_j=a_j-\lfloor a_j\rfloor\), assign the normalized GMI coefficients by the standard four cases based on \(j\in I\), \(f_j\le f_0\), and the sign of \(a_j\), and output the exact inequality \(\sum_{j\in N}\pi_jx_j\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a fractional integer-basic tableau row, compute the exact four-case normalized GMI coefficients, and output the resulting inequality without uncertified coefficient deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(0<f_0<1\), the algorithm outputs the valid GMI inequality \(\sum_{j\in N}\pi_jx_j\ge1\); if \(f_0=0\), it outputs no cut.

notation.meaning: fractional part of the tableau right-hand side
fractional part of an integer nonbasic coefficient

children.title: GMI Tableau Selection Interface
children.top_down_role: Selection of tableau representations for GMI generation.

children.title: GMI Row Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection of fractional tableau rows for GMI cut generation.

knowledge_statements.title: GMI Row Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection among eligible fractional integer-basic tableau rows by normalized efficacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an LP solution \(\bar x\), form the eligible set \(R\) of tableau rows whose basic variable is integer constrained and has fractional value. For each \(r\in R\), generate the normalized GMI inequality \(\pi_r^{\mathsf T}x\ge1\) and compute its efficacy \(e_r=(1-\pi_r^{\mathsf T}\bar x)/\lVert\pi_r\rVert_2\), discarding rows with nonpositive violation or unacceptable numerical conditioning. Select any \(r^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{r\in R}e_r\), or the highest-scoring prescribed subset, and return the corresponding GMI cuts. If \(R\) is empty, return no cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate candidates from fractional integer-basic rows and select the numerically acceptable cuts with greatest normalized violation.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is the current LP solution.
Candidate rows have integer-constrained basic variables and nonzero fractional right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected row maximizes \(e_r\) over the retained eligible candidates, and its generated GMI inequality is valid.

notation.meaning: Euclidean-normalized cut violation for row r

children.title: GMI Basis Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection among alternative bases representing the same relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: GMI Basis Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of an LP basis whose tableau yields a preferred GMI candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B(\bar x)\) be a prescribed finite collection of feasible LP bases representing the same solution \(\bar x\). For each \(B\in\mathcal B(\bar x)\), construct its tableau, generate GMI candidates from all fractional integer-basic rows, and assign each candidate a fixed score such as efficacy \((1-\pi^{\mathsf T}\bar x)/\lVert\pi\rVert_2\). Discard numerically unstable candidates, select a basis and row attaining the largest remaining score, and output that cut. Different bases may produce different valid GMI inequalities even when they represent the same LP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare GMI candidates from alternative feasible bases and choose the stable basis-row pair with the best fixed separation score.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B(\bar x)\) is finite and every \(B\in\mathcal B(\bar x)\) represents \(\bar x\).
The same scoring and numerical-acceptance rules are used for every basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned pair \((B^\star,r^\star)\) maximizes the chosen score among retained basis-row candidates, and its GMI cut is valid.

notation.meaning: candidate feasible bases representing the current LP solution

children.title: Representation Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Variation in GMI cuts caused by row or basis choice.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of generated GMI cuts on the chosen formulation, basis, and tableau row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a mixed-integer relaxation, and let two extended formulations have the same projection onto the original variables. Applying the GMI formula to tableau rows of independently chosen bases can produce inequalities \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta\) and \(\tilde a^{\mathsf T}x\geq\tilde\beta\) whose projected halfspaces differ. Each cut remains valid when its generating tableau row is valid and its declared basic variable is integer, but formulation equivalence alone does not imply equality or mutual dominance of the resulting cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent formulations or different bases can yield distinct GMI cuts. Validity is retained, but equality or dominance of their projected inequalities is not guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) has the prescribed mixed-integer variable domain.
Each selected tableau row is exact and has an integer-constrained basic variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equivalent representations need not generate identical or mutually dominating GMI cuts.

notation.meaning: mixed-integer relaxation in the original variables
a GMI cut projected to the original variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the Representation Sensitivity leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no source is supplied for the representation-, basis-, and row-dependence claim or its projected non-dominance conclusion.

children.title: GMI Postprocessing Calculus
children.top_down_role: Strengthening, sparsification, scaling, and numerical treatment of GMI cuts.

children.title: GMI Coefficient Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Improvement of GMI coefficients using discrete-variable structure.

knowledge_statements.title: GMI Coefficient Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance-preserving coefficient replacement for a generated GMI inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a relaxation \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n_+\), let \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta\) be a valid GMI cut. A coefficient vector \(a'\) is a GMI coefficient strengthening on \(R\) if \(a'^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta\) is valid for every mixed-integer feasible point and \(a'\leq a\) componentwise. Then every \(x\in R\) satisfying the strengthened inequality also satisfies the original inequality. The strengthening is strict when some feasible point of \(R\) satisfies the original cut but violates the strengthened cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative variables, a valid componentwise coefficient reduction strengthens a GMI cut; it is strict if it excludes a relaxation point retained by the original.
assumptions_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta\) is a valid GMI inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity and \(a'\leq a\) imply that \(a'^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta\) dominates \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta\) on \(R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise dominance statement is correct for nonnegative variables, but it is a generic definition of coefficient strengthening rather than a sourced GMI-specific strengthening rule. An authoritative source identifying the applicable GMI operation is required.

children.title: GMI Sparsification
children.top_down_role: Reduction of GMI support while controlling validity and strength.

knowledge_statements.title: GMI Sparsification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity limitation for deleting small coefficients from a GMI cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Coefficient deletion is not validity preserving in general. On the binary set \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^2:x_1+x_2\geq1\}\), the valid inequality \(x_1+x_2\geq1\) becomes \(x_1\geq1\) after deleting the coefficient of \(x_2\); the point \((0,1)\in X\) violates the sparsified inequality. Consequently, a GMI coefficient may be set to zero only when validity is separately certified, for example by a dominance argument using variable bounds or other valid constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blindly deleting small GMI coefficients can invalidate a cut. Every deletion requires a separate validity or dominance certificate.
assumptions_latex: Sparsification means replacing at least one cut coefficient by zero without otherwise changing the inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uncertified coefficient deletion does not preserve validity, even for binary feasible sets.

notation.meaning: binary feasible set used in the counterexample

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary counterexample correctly shows that arbitrary coefficient deletion can destroy validity, and failure_boundary is an appropriate role. However, the example is not identified as a GMI-derived inequality, and no source supports the stated GMI postprocessing boundary.

children.title: GMI Scaling
children.top_down_role: Equivalent rescaling choices used for solver-facing representations.

knowledge_statements.title: GMI Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive rescaling and normalization of a GMI inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any GMI inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta\) and scalar \(\lambda>0\), the inequality \((\lambda a)^{\mathsf T}x\geq\lambda\beta\) defines exactly the same halfspace. If \((a,\beta)\neq0\), a canonical numerical normalization may divide all coefficients and the right-hand side by \(s=\max\{|\beta|,\|a\|_\infty\}>0\). Negative scaling is excluded because it reverses the inequality direction unless that direction is also reversed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplication by a positive scalar preserves a GMI cut exactly. Normalization can bound coefficient magnitudes without changing the represented halfspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta\}=\{x:(\lambda a)^{\mathsf T}x\geq\lambda\beta\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Positive scaling and the proposed infinity-norm normalization preserve the represented halfspace, and representation fits the leaf. The record nevertheless has neither a cited source nor an explicit standard-field rationale permitted by the evidence contract.

children.title: GMI Numerical Treatment
children.top_down_role: Tolerance, coefficient-range, and stability concerns in processed GMI cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: GMI Numerical Treatment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerically safe acceptance procedure for a floating-point GMI candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a floating-point tableau row, the integrality labels, and tolerances. First reject a row whose basic variable is not integer-constrained or whose residual exceeds the row-feasibility tolerance. Rationally reconstruct or otherwise certify the row data, then recompute the GMI coefficients from the certified row. Remove or round a coefficient only through a validity-preserving rule, apply positive normalization, and accept the cut only after checking its certified derivation and violation at the candidate relaxation point. Without certified row data, output the inequality as heuristic rather than valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruct and certify the tableau row, recompute the cut, normalize it, and verify violation. Floating-point output without certified derivation remains heuristic.
assumptions_latex: The input identifies the basic variable and all integer-constrained nonbasic variables.
Exact or certified rational reconstruction is available for accepted cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs either a derivationally certified GMI cut or an explicitly heuristic candidate.

notation.meaning: chosen family of numerical feasibility and integrality tolerances

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role for this procedure, but the conditions under which rational reconstruction certifies the tableau row and the resulting GMI cut are not specified precisely enough to establish the conclusion. An authoritative numerical GMI source is required.

children.title: Modular Cut Families
children.top_down_role: Low-modulus and congruence-based specializations of rounding cuts.

children.title: Zero-Half Cuts
children.top_down_role: Half-integral Chvátal–Gomory cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Half Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Half-integral Chvátal–Gomory cuts for a pure-integer nonnegative system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n_+:Ax\leq b\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\), and require \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\). For any multiplier \(u\in\{0,\tfrac12\}^m\), the zero-half cut associated with \(u\) is \[\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}A\rfloor x\leq\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}b\rfloor,\] where the floor is componentwise on \(u^{\mathsf T}A\). It is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\) because \(x\geq0\), the aggregated inequality is valid, and its rounded left side is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-half cut is the Chvátal–Gomory rounding of an aggregation whose row multipliers are zero or one-half.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}A\rfloor x\leq\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}b\rfloor\) is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed half-integral Chvatal-Gomory formula is plausible under the stated nonnegativity and integrality assumptions, but no authoritative zero-half-cut source is cited. The final causal clause also constitutes proof-style justification and should be removed once the sourced statement is revised.

children.title: Modular Group-Cut Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Higher-modulus and finite-group extensions of modular cut generation.

children.title: Mod-k Cuts
children.top_down_role: Modular cuts associated with integer moduli beyond the zero-half case.

knowledge_statements.title: Mod-k Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chvátal–Gomory cuts generated by multipliers with denominator dividing \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an integer \(k\geq2\). For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n_+:Ax\leq b\}\) with integral \(A,b\) and integer variables \(x\), choose \(u\in\{0,\tfrac1k,\ldots,\tfrac{k-1}{k}\}^m\). The associated mod-\(k\) cut is \[\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}A\rfloor x\leq\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}b\rfloor.\] This inequality is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\). Its fractional aggregation data depend only on the relevant integer residues modulo \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mod-k cut rounds an aggregation whose multipliers are nonnegative residue fractions with denominator k; the resulting inequality is valid for nonnegative integer points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}A\rfloor x\leq\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}b\rfloor\) is a valid mod-\(k\) inequality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula is a coherent denominator-k Chvatal-Gomory construction for a nonnegative pure-integer system, but the exact use of the name mod-k and the residue-dependence assertion require an authoritative source.

children.title: Finite-Group Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts organized through finite-group relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Group Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid-function representation for a finite abelian group relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a finite abelian group, let \(b\in G\setminus\{0\}\), and define \(Y_b=\{y\in\mathbb{Z}_+^G:\sum_{g\in G}g y_g=b\}\). If \(\pi:G\to\mathbb{R}_+\) satisfies \(\pi(0)=0\), subadditivity \(\pi(g+h)\leq\pi(g)+\pi(h)\), and symmetry \(\pi(g)+\pi(b-g)=1\), then \[\sum_{g\in G}\pi(g)y_g\geq1\] is valid for \(Y_b\). Such inequalities are finite-group cuts; different valid functions describe different members of the family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative, subadditive, symmetric function on a finite abelian group yields a valid inequality for its group relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite abelian group and \(b\neq0\).
\(\pi\) is nonnegative, normalized, subadditive, and symmetric as stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{g\in G}\pi(g)y_g\geq1\) is valid for \(Y_b\).

notation.meaning: finite-group relaxation with right-hand side b

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-group valid-function statement is internally consistent and representation is an appropriate content kind, but no source is supplied for the normalization, subadditivity, and symmetry characterization.

children.title: Modulus–Group Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between residue-class constructions and finite-group representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Modulus–Group Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of denominator-\(k\) modular data with the cyclic group \(\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\geq2\), the map \(\varphi:r/k+\mathbb{Z}\mapsto r+k\mathbb{Z}\) is a group isomorphism from the subgroup \((\tfrac1k\mathbb{Z})/\mathbb{Z}\) of \(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}\) onto the cyclic group \(\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}\). Hence an integer congruence \(\sum_j r_j y_j\equiv r_0\pmod{k}\) is equivalent to the finite-group equation \(\sum_j(r_j+k\mathbb{Z})y_j=r_0+k\mathbb{Z}\). Mod-\(k\) cut coefficients can therefore be represented by valid functions on this cyclic group.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractions with denominator k modulo integers form the cyclic group of residues modulo k, translating modular congruences into finite-group equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\tfrac1k\mathbb{Z})/\mathbb{Z}\cong\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}\), and the corresponding modular and group equations are equivalent.

notation.meaning: cyclic residue group of modulus k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cyclic-group isomorphism and congruence translation are mathematically standard, but the record supplies neither a source nor an explicit standard-field rationale. The further claim about representing mod-k cut coefficients by valid functions also needs cut-theoretic support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional strict domination of the GMI cut by simple split cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two independent sufficient conditions for strict domination by the positive and negative cuts from the simple split-disjunction construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((\forall j\in J_1,\ a_j\ge a_0-1)\land(J_1^+\ne\varnothing)\), then \(\alpha^+x\ge 1\) strictly dominates the GMI cut. If \((\forall j\in J_1,\ a_j\le a_0)\land(J_1^-\ne\varnothing)\), then \(\alpha^-x\ge 1\) strictly dominates the GMI cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the first sufficient condition, the positive simple-split cut strictly dominates the GMI cut. Independently, under the second sufficient condition, the negative simple-split cut strictly dominates the GMI cut.

children.title: Single-Variable Split Cuts
children.top_down_role: Split cuts induced by an individual integer variable.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality valid for the displayed disjunctive hull is valid for all mixed-integer feasible points in \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Split cuts obtained from one integer-constrained coordinate.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. The Correspondence Between Lift-and-Project Cuts and Simple Disjunctive Cuts p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a relaxation whose coordinate \(x_i\) is required to be integer, and choose \(k\in\mathbb{Z}\). The single-variable split disjunction is \(x_i\leq k\) or \(x_i\geq k+1\). A single-variable split cut is any linear inequality valid for \[\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\cap\{x:x_i\leq k\})\cup(P\cap\{x:x_i\geq k+1\})\bigr).\] Every such inequality is valid for the mixed-integer feasible points of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-variable split cut is valid for the convex hull obtained by imposing either side of the unit gap around an integer-constrained coordinate, and hence for the mixed-integer feasible set.

children.title: General Integral Split Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Split cuts induced by integral linear forms.

knowledge_statements.title: General Integral Split Disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Split disjunctions defined by an integral linear form in integer-constrained variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(I\) index integer-constrained coordinates, choose \(\pi\in\mathbb{Z}^{I}\setminus\{0\}\), and let \(k\in\mathbb{Z}\). The integral split disjunction is \(\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\leq k\) or \(\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\geq k+1\). Its split hull is the convex hull of the union of the two intersections with \(P\). A general integral split cut is any linear inequality valid for this split hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integral split uses any nonzero integer linear form of the integer variables and excludes the open slab between consecutive integer levels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every general integral split cut is valid for the mixed-integer feasible points of \(P\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Split Cut Induced by an Integral Linear Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition for a mixed-integer set obtained by intersecting a polyhedron with integrality restrictions on x.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X=P\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^p). An inequality cx+hy\leq c_0 is a split cut for X if there exists (\pi,\pi_0)\in\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb Z such that cx+hy\leq c_0 is valid for both P\cap\{(x,y):\pi x\leq\pi_0\} and P\cap\{(x,y):\pi x\geq\pi_0+1\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality is a split cut when an integral linear form defines two complementary branches and the inequality is valid on the polyhedron restricted to each branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: cx+hy\leq c_0\text{ is a split cut for }X\iff cx+hy\leq c_0\text{ is valid for both }P\cap\{\pi x\leq\pi_0\}\text{ and }P\cap\{\pi x\geq\pi_0+1\}\text{ for some }(\pi,\pi_0)\in\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb Z.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity of the normalized multiplier split inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of the normalized multiplier inequality for the single-split convexification induced by its integral linear form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}. Suppose u\in\mathbb R^m satisfies uA_I\in\mathbb Z^{|I|}, uA_C=0, and ub\notin\mathbb Z. Define \pi=uA, \pi_0=\lfloor ub\rfloor, and f=ub-\lfloor ub\rfloor. Then \frac{u^+(b-Ax)}{f}+\frac{u^-(b-Ax)}{1-f}\ge1 is valid for P^{(\pi,\pi_0)} and hence is a split inequality for P.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized multiplier inequality generated by a multiplier integral on the integer columns, zero on the continuous columns, and fractional on the right-hand side is valid for the convexification induced by the corresponding split and therefore is a split inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{u^+(b-Ax)}{f}+\frac{u^-(b-Ax)}{1-f}\ge1\text{ is valid for }P^{(\pi,\pi_0)}\text{ and is a split inequality for }P.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Split cuts from general integral split disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines split cuts for a mixed-integer polyhedron, including the support restriction on the integral linear form and the elementary or rank-one designation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\geq b\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), and let \(N_1\subseteq N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index the integer-constrained variables. Define \(P_I=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in P:x_j\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }j\in N_1\}\). For \((\pi,\pi_0)\in\mathbb Z^{n+1}\) with \(\pi_j=0\) for \(j\in N\setminus N_1\), a split cut is any inequality valid for \(P_I\) derived from \((Ax\geq b,\ \pi x\leq\pi_0)\ \vee\ (Ax\geq b,\ \pi x\geq\pi_0+1)\). Split cuts derived directly from one such disjunction without iterating the cut-generation procedure are elementary, or rank-one, split cuts. The closure obtained from all elementary split cuts is the elementary split closure of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rational mixed-integer relaxation, an integral linear form supported only on integer-constrained variables yields a split disjunction between two consecutive integer levels. Valid inequalities derived from this disjunction are split cuts. Directly derived cuts are elementary or rank one, and all elementary split cuts determine the elementary split closure.
assumptions_latex: N_1\subseteq N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\text{ indexes the integer-constrained variables}
Ax\geq b\text{ includes }x\geq0\text{ and the stated upper bounds on }x_j\text{ for }j\in N_1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Direct cuts from }\pi x\leq\pi_0\ \vee\ \pi x\geq\pi_0+1\text{ are elementary (rank-one) split cuts, and all such cuts define the elementary split closure of }P.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of the normalized multiplier expression; validity as a split inequality is not asserted in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}, with A_I and A_C denoting the columns indexed by the integer and continuous variables. For u\in\mathbb R^m, define u_i^+=\max\{0,u_i\} and u^-=(-u)^+. If uA_I is integral, uA_C=0, and ub\notin\mathbb Z, set f=ub-\lfloor ub\rfloor\in(0,1). The associated normalized multiplier inequality is \frac{u^+(b-Ax)}{f}+\frac{u^-(b-Ax)}{1-f}\ge1.

This extract defines the form but does not yet establish its validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{u^+(b-Ax)}{f}+\frac{u^-(b-Ax)}{1-f}\ge1\quad\text{is the associated normalized multiplier inequality}.

knowledge_statements.title: Split-Disjunction Validity Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity transfer from both terms of a split disjunction to their convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(D_1=\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\leq k\}\), and let \(D_2=\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\geq k+1\}\), where \(x_I\) is integer and \(\pi,k\) are integral. If \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for both \(P\cap D_1\) and \(P\cap D_2\), then it is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}((P\cap D_1)\cup(P\cap D_2))\), and therefore for every mixed-integer feasible point of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality valid on both sides of an integral split is valid on their convex hull and hence on the mixed-integer feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid on both disjunctive terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}((P\cap D_1)\cup(P\cap D_2))\) and for the mixed-integer feasible set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\ge3\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and, for each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), let \(D^i\in\mathbb R^{p_i\times n}\) and \(d^i\in\mathbb R^{p_i}\). Define \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\}\) and the nonempty polyhedron \(P_i=P\cap\{x\in\mathbb R^n:D^ix\ge d^i\}\). For \(\alpha\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), the inequality \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\) is valid for \(\bigcup_{i=1}^qP_i\) if and only if, for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), there exist \(u^i\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(v^i\in\mathbb R_+^{p_i}\) such that \[\alpha=A^\top u^i+(D^i)^\top v^i,\qquad \beta\le b^\top u^i+(d^i)^\top v^i.\] Thus the common inequality is represented by a separate nonnegative aggregation for every term of the disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a union of at least three nonempty polyhedra sharing a common relaxation, an inequality is valid for the union exactly when it has a separate nonnegative multiplier representation for every disjunctive term.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Disjunctive Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity relative to the CGLP–simplex-basis correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a polyhedral relaxation \(P\), a finite disjunction, and a normalized cut-generating linear program (CGLP). A disjunctive cut \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\) is regular if it has an optimal basic CGLP representation whose positive multipliers on rows of \(P\) select rows compatible with some nonsingular simplex basis of \(P\), and the same inequality, up to positive scaling, is generated from that basis and the disjunction. Regularity is therefore existential: a cut remains regular when one basis-compatible representation exists, even if it also possesses other degenerate or non-basis-compatible CGLP representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disjunctive cut is regular when at least one basic CGLP representation corresponds to a simplex basis of the underlying relaxation.
assumptions_latex: A particular relaxation, disjunction, and CGLP normalization are fixed.
Cut inequalities are identified up to positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut belongs to the regular class exactly when a basis-compatible CGLP representation exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Irregular Disjunctive Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complement of regularity for a fixed relaxation, disjunction, and CGLP formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a polyhedral relaxation \(P\), a finite disjunction, and a normalized CGLP. A generated inequality \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\) is an irregular disjunctive cut if no optimal basic CGLP representation of that inequality is compatible with any nonsingular simplex basis of \(P\). Equivalently, although the CGLP multipliers certify validity for every disjunctive term, every representation of the cut fails the row-selection and tableau conditions required by the CGLP–LP-basis correspondence. Irregularity concerns representability, not validity: an irregular cut is still valid for the disjunctive union.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An irregular cut is CGLP-valid but has no representation corresponding to a simplex basis of the underlying relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation, disjunction, normalization, and basis-correspondence criterion are fixed.
All CGLP representations producing the same positively scaled inequality are considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut is irregular precisely when it has no basis-compatible CGLP representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient condition for irregularity of an L&P cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition involving a corner point and the support of positive CGLP multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a basic feasible solution of the LP relaxation, with \(J\) the index set of nonbasic variables, and let \((\bar\alpha,\bar\beta,\{\bar u^t,\bar v^t\}_{t\in T})\) be a basic feasible solution of (11.8) such that \(\bar\alpha x\geq\bar\beta\) cuts off \(\bar x\). Suppose there exist \(\bar y\in\operatorname{corner}(J)\setminus P\) and \(t^*\in T\) such that \(\bar v^{t^*}D^{t^*}\bar y=\bar v^{t^*}d^{t^*}\). If \(\{i:\bar u_i^{t^*}>0\}\) can be partitioned as \(F^+\mathbin{\dot\cup}F^-\), where \(F^-\neq\varnothing\) and \(F^+\) may be empty, such that \(\widetilde A_i\bar y=\widetilde b_i\) for every \(i\in F^+\) and \(\widetilde A_i\bar y<\widetilde b_i\) for every \(i\in F^-\), then \(\bar\alpha x\geq\bar\beta\) is an irregular L\&P cut and cuts off \(\bar y\) from \(\operatorname{corner}(J)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a corner point outside P lies on the specified disjunctive boundary, and the positive-multiplier constraints split into constraints satisfied at equality and a nonempty set violated by that point, then the L&P cut is irregular and cuts off the corner point.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\text{ is a basic feasible solution of the LP relaxation, and }J\text{ indexes its nonbasic variables.}
(\bar\alpha,\bar\beta,\{\bar u^t,\bar v^t\}_{t\in T})\text{ is a basic feasible solution of (11.8), and }\bar\alpha x\geq\bar\beta\text{ cuts off }\bar x.
\exists\bar y\in\operatorname{corner}(J)\setminus P,\ \exists t^*\in T:\ \bar v^{t^*}D^{t^*}\bar y=\bar v^{t^*}d^{t^*}.
\widetilde A_i\bar y=\widetilde b_i\ \forall i\in F^+,\qquad \widetilde A_i\bar y<\widetilde b_i\ \forall i\in F^-.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar\alpha x\geq\bar\beta\text{ is an irregular L\&P cut, and }\bar\alpha\bar y<\bar\beta\text{ for }\bar y\in\operatorname{corner}(J).

children.title: Regularity Classification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Representation-sensitive distinctions separating regular from irregular cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Classification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions limiting inference of regularity from one CGLP solution or one LP basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Regularity cannot generally be inferred from an arbitrary CGLP representation. Degeneracy may give one inequality several multiplier vectors or several optimal CGLP bases, some basis-compatible and others incompatible. Consequently, observing an incompatible representation does not establish irregularity; irregularity requires exclusion of every basis-compatible representation of the same cut, modulo positive scaling. Conversely, correspondence with one LP basis establishes regularity only relative to the fixed relaxation, disjunction, normalization, and admissible basis class. Changing any of these data can change the classification without changing the geometric halfspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degeneracy and alternative representations prevent classifying a cut from one CGLP basis; irregularity requires ruling out every compatible LP-basis representation.
assumptions_latex: CGLP solutions and inequalities are distinguished, with inequalities identified up to positive scaling.
The classification is relative to fixed formulation data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single incompatible representation is insufficient to certify irregularity, whereas one compatible representation suffices for regularity.

notation.meaning: Halfspace coefficients considered up to positive scaling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct content kind, but the specialized claims about degeneracy, universal exclusion of compatible representations, and classification changes under reformulation have no cited source. Their validity also depends on the unresolved definition of regularity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-row-rank characterization of CGLP regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An if-and-only-if rank criterion for regularity of a CGLP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:=\{j\in Q:\bar u_j^t>0\text{ for some }t\in T\}\), and let \(\widetilde A_R\) be the \(|R|\times n\) submatrix of \(\widetilde A\) whose rows are indexed by \(R\). Then \(\bar w\) is a regular solution to the CGLP if and only if \(\widetilde A_R\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CGLP solution is regular exactly when the submatrix consisting of rows assigned a positive multiplier in at least one disjunctive term has full row rank.
assumptions_latex: R:=\{j\in Q:\exists t\in T\text{ such that }\bar u_j^t>0\}.
\widetilde A_R\in\mathbb R^{|R|\times n}\text{ consists of the rows of }\widetilde A\text{ indexed by }R.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar w\text{ is a regular CGLP solution}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{rank}(\widetilde A_R)=|R|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular and irregular CGLP bases, solutions, and cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes regularity of a CGLP representation from regularity of the represented cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible basis for CGLP system (11.6), respectively (11.8), and its associated solution are regular if the cut they define is equivalent to an intersection cut, that is, if the condition of Theorem 11.9, respectively Theorem 11.10, holds; otherwise they are irregular. A cut defined by an irregular solution \(w\) is irregular unless there exists a regular solution \(w'\) with the same \((\alpha,\beta)\)-component as \(w\), in which case the cut is regular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible CGLP basis and its associated solution are regular when their cut is equivalent to an intersection cut, and irregular otherwise. An irregular representation can nevertheless define a regular cut if the same coefficient pair has another, regular CGLP representation.
assumptions_latex: w\text{ is a feasible basis or associated solution of CGLP system (11.6) or (11.8)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w\text{ is regular}\iff\operatorname{cut}(w)\text{ is equivalent to an intersection cut};\quad w\text{ irregular}\Longrightarrow\bigl(\operatorname{cut}(w)\text{ is regular}\iff\exists\text{ regular }w'\text{ with }(\alpha',\beta')=(\alpha,\beta)\bigr).
