knowledge_statements.title: V-Polyhedral Cut Generators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity characterization using finite vertex-and-ray descriptions of all disjunctive terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(i=1,\ldots,q\), let \(P_i=\operatorname{conv}(V_i)+\operatorname{cone}(R_i)\), where \(V_i\) and \(R_i\) are finite. Then \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\) is valid for \(\bigcup_{i=1}^qP_i\) if and only if \[\alpha^\top v\ge\beta\quad(v\in V_i),\qquad \alpha^\top r\ge0\quad(r\in R_i),\qquad i=1,\ldots,q.\] Hence a V-polyhedral cut generator searches over \((\alpha,\beta)\) subject to these finite constraints and a scale normalization, usually optimizing separation of a prescribed relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With vertex-and-ray descriptions, cut validity is equivalent to testing every listed vertex and requiring nonnegative value on every recession ray.

Every nonempty term has at least one listed vertex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite vertex and ray inequalities characterize validity for the entire disjunctive union.

knowledge_statements.title: CGLP Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-space formulation of validity for a finite union of polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A^ix\ge b^i\}\), for \(i=1,\ldots,q\). A CGLP representation of a common valid inequality consists of \((\alpha,\beta)\) and multipliers \(u^i\ge0\) satisfying \[\alpha=(A^i)^\top u^i,\qquad \beta\le(b^i)^\top u^i\quad(i=1,\ldots,q),\] together with a normalization excluding the zero solution. For a point \(\bar x\), minimizing \(\alpha^\top\bar x-\beta\) over this system either produces a separating inequality when the optimum is negative or finds no separator within the normalized represented family when it is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CGLP represents one inequality through separate nonnegative validity multipliers for every polyhedron and optimizes its separation of a chosen point.
assumptions_latex: A normalization fixes positive scaling and makes the chosen optimization well posed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible nonzero CGLP point defines an inequality valid for \(\bigcup_{i=1}^qP_i\).

notation.meaning: Validity multiplier for disjunctive term i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bonami LP and membership-LP dual for the normalized split CGLP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-equivalent LP and dual representations for the split CGLP under the disjunction-multiplier normalization, with the distinct consequences of the two stated normalization regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\max\{cx:Ax=b,\ x\in\mathbb Z_+^p\times\mathbb R_+^{n-p}\}\), let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax=b\}\), and let \(\widehat x\) be optimal for its linear relaxation. For \(k\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\) with \(\lfloor\widehat x_k\rfloor<\widehat x_k<\lceil\widehat x_k\rceil\), the CGLP associated with \(x_k\leq\lfloor\widehat x_k\rfloor\vee x_k\geq\lceil\widehat x_k\rceil\) generates a lift-and-project cut. Under \(ue+ve+se+te+u_0+v_0=1\), an optimal CGLP solution defines a cut maximally violated by \(\widehat x\) in the stated normalized sense. Under \(u_0+v_0=1\), it defines the simple disjunctive cut obtained from the optimal simplex-tableau row for \(x_k\). Writing \(\widehat f_k=\widehat x_k-\lfloor\widehat x_k\rfloor\), the latter CGLP is cut-equivalent to \[\min_{\lambda,s,t}\ \widehat f_k b^T\lambda+\widehat x^Ts-\widehat f_k\lceil\widehat x_k\rceil\quad\text{s.t.}\quad A^T\lambda+s-t=e_k,\quad \lambda\in\mathbb R^m,\quad s,t\in\mathbb R_+^n.\] Its dual, called the membership LP, is \[\max_y\ y_k-\widehat f_k\lceil\widehat x_k\rceil\quad\text{s.t.}\quad Ay=b\widehat f_k,\quad 0\leq y\leq\widehat x,\quad y\in\mathbb R^n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fractional integer coordinate of an optimal MILP-relaxation solution, the associated split CGLP generates a lift-and-project cut. Normalizing all listed multipliers and slacks to sum to one yields a maximally violated cut in the stated normalized sense. Normalizing only the two disjunction multipliers yields the simple tableau disjunctive cut; this normalized CGLP has Bonami's cut-equivalent LP formulation, whose dual is called the membership LP.
assumptions_latex: P=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax=b\}\text{ is the relaxation of }\max\{cx:Ax=b,\ x\in\mathbb Z_+^p\times\mathbb R_+^{n-p}\}.
\widehat x\in P\text{ is an optimal relaxation solution}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{CGLP}_k^{(10.12)}\text{ is cut-equivalent to Bonami's LP, whose dual is the membership LP; }\mathrm{CGLP}_k^{(10.11)}\text{ yields a maximally violated cut, whereas }\mathrm{CGLP}_k^{(10.12)}\text{ yields the simple tableau disjunctive cut.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: CGLP membership and separation certificate for a disjunctive hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A normalized cut-generating linear program characterizes membership in the closed convex hull of a finite polyhedral disjunction and produces a separating inequality when membership fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax\ge b\}\), let \(D=\bigvee_{k=1}^q(D_kx\ge d_k)\), let \(\widehat x\in P\), and define \(Q=\operatorname{clconv}\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^q\{x\in P:D_kx\ge d_k\}\right)\). For conformable normalization vectors satisfying \(\xi\ge0\) and \(\xi_k>0\) for every \(k\), consider the CGLP minimizing \(\alpha^T\widehat x-\beta\) subject to \(A^Tu^k+D_k^Tv^k=\alpha\), \(b^Tu^k+d_k^Tv^k\ge\beta\), and \(u^k,v^k\ge0\) for every \(k\), together with \(\sum_{k=1}^q(\xi^Tu^k+\xi_k^Tv^k)=1\). Then \(\widehat x\in Q\) if and only if the CGLP optimal value is nonnegative. If the optimal value is negative and \((\alpha,\beta)\) is part of an optimal solution, then \(\alpha^Tx\ge\beta\) is valid for \(Q\) and cuts off \(\widehat x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedron subject to a finite disjunction, the normalized cut-generating linear program tests whether a specified point lies in the closed disjunctive hull. Membership holds exactly when the optimal value is nonnegative. A negative optimum supplies a valid inequality that separates the point from the hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x\in Q\iff \operatorname{val}(\mathrm{CGLP})\ge0;\quad \operatorname{val}(\mathrm{CGLP})<0\Rightarrow \alpha^Tx\ge\beta\text{ is valid for }Q\text{ and cuts off }\widehat x

children.title: LP-Basis Representations
children.top_down_role: Basis-based tableau representations associated with candidate cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: LP-Basis Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tableau-cone representation used to derive basis-dependent intersection or disjunctive cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be the basic solution associated with an LP basis and let its translated tableau cone be \(C=\{\bar x+Rs:s\ge0\}\), with ray columns \(r^j\). If a closed convex set \(S\) contains \(\bar x\) in its interior and has no feasible integer point in its interior, define \(\lambda_j=\sup\{\lambda\ge0:\bar x+\lambda r^j\in S\}\). When \(0<\lambda_j<\infty\), the basis representation of the intersection cut is \[\sum_j\frac{s_j}{\lambda_j}\ge1.\] Substitution of the tableau equations converts this inequality into the original \(x\)-space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP basis supplies a cone of tableau rays; their first boundary intersections with a forbidden convex set give the intersection-cut coefficients.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}(S)\) and \(\operatorname{int}(S)\) contains no feasible integer point.
Every retained tableau ray has a finite positive boundary distance \(\lambda_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_j s_j/\lambda_j\ge1\) is valid for points of the tableau cone lying outside \(\operatorname{int}(S)\).

children.title: Basis Correspondence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing whether a CGLP solution admits an LP-basis interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Correspondence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of identifying CGLP solutions with cuts derived from one simplex tableau.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A CGLP cut has an LP-basis representation only when its active multiplier rows can be organized into the nonsingular row system of an admissible LP basis and the resulting tableau construction reproduces the same halfspace up to positive scaling. The correspondence can fail for a nonbasic CGLP solution, an irregular basic solution, rank-deficient active rows, or formulation rows that cannot coexist in one LP basis. Degeneracy also destroys one-to-one correspondence: distinct CGLP bases or LP bases may generate the same inequality, and one inequality may possess both compatible and incompatible multiplier representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CGLP and LP-basis representations correspond only under rank and compatibility conditions; degeneracy can make the mapping nonunique.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation, disjunction, normalization, and admissible LP bases are fixed.
Inequalities differing by positive scaling are identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither arbitrary CGLP feasibility nor CGLP basicness alone guarantees an LP-basis representation.

children.title: CGLP Normalization Families
children.top_down_role: Normalization regimes controlling boundedness and generated-cut geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: CGLP Normalization Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-homogeneous cross-sections that remove the scale invariance of CGLP cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be the homogeneous CGLP feasibility cone in variables \(z=(\alpha,\beta,u^1,\ldots,u^q)\). Because \(tz\in K\) for every \(z\in K\) and \(t>0\), optimization requires a normalization \(h(z)=1\), where \(h\) is nonnegative and positively homogeneous. Multiplier normalizations use a weighted sum of components of \(u^i\); coefficient normalizations use a norm or weighted gauge of \((\alpha,\beta)\). The normalized feasible set is bounded precisely when no nonzero recession direction of \(K\) has zero gauge, namely \(\operatorname{rec}(K)\cap\{z:h(z)=0\}=\{0\}\). Different cross-sections can select different representatives and cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CGLP normalizations intersect the scale-invariant feasibility cone with a gauge cross-section; boundedness requires the gauge to detect every recession direction.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is finite, nonnegative, continuous, and positively homogeneous on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The section \(K\cap\{z:h(z)=1\}\) is bounded if and only if \(\operatorname{rec}(K)\cap\ker h=\{0\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is a plausible kind for this normalization-family leaf, but no source supports the proposed taxonomy or boundedness criterion. Moreover, the statement that different complete gauge cross-sections select different cuts is ambiguous: cross-sections select different representatives of the same rays, while different optimization outcomes require additional conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Minimum Criterion for a Directionally Normalized CGLP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness criterion for a feasible directional-normalization variant of a cut-generating linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(CGLP)^y$ be feasible. Then $(CGLP)^y$ has a finite minimum if and only if $\bar{x}+y\lambda\in P_D$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the directionally normalized CGLP is feasible, it has a finite minimum exactly when the affine line through the reference point in direction y intersects P_D.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (CGLP)^y\text{ has a finite minimum}\iff\exists\lambda\in\mathbb{R}:\bar{x}+y\lambda\in P_D

knowledge_statements.statement_title: CGLP boundedness through normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncation of the homogeneous cut-generating cone for a binary split and the dependence of the generated cut on the chosen normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be an optimal solution of the current LP relaxation, and suppose the homogeneous CGLP constraints define a cone of feasible cut coefficients and multipliers. If there exists a feasible cut with \(\alpha^T\bar x-\beta<0\), then the unnormalized problem \(\min(\alpha^T\bar x-\beta)\) is unbounded below by positive scaling. For the disjunction \(x_k\le 0\vee x_k\ge 1\), imposing \(ue+u_0+ve+v_0=1\) yields the normalized CGLP \[\min\ \alpha^T\bar x-\beta\] subject to \[\alpha-u\widetilde A+u_0e_k=0,\qquad \alpha-v\widetilde A-v_0e_k=0,\] \[-\beta+u\widetilde b=0,\qquad -\beta+v\widetilde b+v_0=0,\] \[ue+u_0+ve+v_0=1,\qquad u,u_0,v,v_0\ge0.\] Other truncating normalizations may constrain \(\beta\), the components or a norm of \(\alpha\), or impose \(u_0+v_0=1\). The normalization can materially change the resulting cut. In particular, \(u_0+v_0=1\) yields a cut equivalent to the intersection cut associated with \(S=\{x:0\le x_k\le1\}\); although the multiplier-sum normalization is reported as empirically advantageous, it is not asserted to dominate the alternatives in a well-defined sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the homogeneous CGLP cone contains a cut that strictly separates the LP optimum, scaling that cut makes the unnormalized minimization unbounded below. A normalization truncates this scaling. For the binary split, the displayed multiplier-sum normalization defines a bounded linear CGLP. The normalization choice can substantially change the generated cut: the trivial normalization recovers the associated intersection cut, while the empirically favored multiplier-sum normalization has no stated general dominance guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is an optimal solution of the current LP relaxation.
The CGLP constraint system is homogeneous and therefore defines a cone.
There exists a feasible cut satisfying \(\alpha^T\bar x-\beta<0\) for the unboundedness conclusion.
\(e\) is the all-ones summation vector and \(e_k\) is the \(k\)-th unit vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A truncating normalization removes the CGLP's improving scaling ray, and different normalizations may produce materially different cuts; specifically, \(u_0+v_0=1\) recovers the associated intersection cut.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional-Membership Interpretation of a CGLP Optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value and contact-point characterization for an optimal directionally normalized CGLP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If $(CGLP)^y$ has an optimal solution $(\widetilde{\alpha},\widetilde{\beta})$, then
\[
\bar{x}^{T}\widetilde{\alpha}-\widetilde{\beta}=\lambda^*:=\min\{\lambda:\bar{x}+y\lambda\in P_D\},
\]
and
\[
(\bar{x}+y\lambda^*)^{T}\widetilde{\alpha}=\widetilde{\beta}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an optimal solution of the directionally normalized CGLP, the objective value equals the minimum parameter for which the directed affine line reaches P_D, and the corresponding point lies on the generated hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar{x}^{T}\widetilde{\alpha}-\widetilde{\beta}=\lambda^*:=\min\{\lambda:\bar{x}+y\lambda\in P_D\},\qquad(\bar{x}+y\lambda^*)^{T}\widetilde{\alpha}=\widetilde{\beta}

children.title: Violation Objectives
children.top_down_role: CGLP objectives prioritizing separation of a specified relaxation point.

knowledge_statements.title: Violation Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CGLP separation by maximizing signed violation at a prescribed relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a point \(\bar x\), a CGLP feasible cone \(K\), and a normalization \(h(z)=1\). Solve \[\max\{\beta-\alpha^\top\bar x:z=(\alpha,\beta,u^1,\ldots,u^q)\in K,\ h(z)=1\}.\] If the optimum \(\delta^*>0\), output \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\), which cuts off \(\bar x\) by amount \(\delta^*\). If \(\delta^*\le0\), report that no inequality in the selected normalized CGLP family strictly separates \(\bar x\). The numerical value depends on the normalization, although positivity of violation is invariant under positive rescaling of a fixed inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize a normalized cut's violation at the candidate point; a positive optimum yields a separating valid inequality.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible nonzero point of \(K\) represents a valid inequality.
The normalized optimization problem attains a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta^*>0\) yields a valid cut excluding \(\bar x\); \(\delta^*\le0\) excludes separation only within the modeled family.

children.title: Cut-Depth Objectives
children.top_down_role: CGLP objectives prioritizing geometric depth or related strength measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Depth Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-invariant separation depth measured in a chosen norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on coefficient space and a point \(\bar x\). For a nonconstant valid inequality \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\), its cut depth at \(\bar x\) is \[d(\bar x;\alpha,\beta)=\frac{\max\{0,\beta-\alpha^\top\bar x\}}{\|\alpha\|_*},\] where \(\|\cdot\|_*\) is the dual norm. A cut-depth objective maximizes this quantity over the represented cut family; equivalently, it maximizes \(\beta-\alpha^\top\bar x\) under \(\|\alpha\|_*=1\). The quotient is invariant under positive scaling and equals the norm-distance from \(\bar x\) to the boundary hyperplane when the inequality is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut depth divides violation by the dual norm of the cut normal, producing a scale-invariant distance to the cut hyperplane.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient norm and its dual are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(\bar x;t\alpha,t\beta)=d(\bar x;\alpha,\beta)\) for every \(t>0\).

notation.meaning: Dual norm used for the cut normal.
Point at which depth is evaluated.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind is plausible, but cut-depth conventions vary and no source is supplied. The statement should also specify that the primal norm is on the ambient point space and that its dual norm acts on the cut normal; describing the initial norm as being on coefficient space makes the distance interpretation ambiguous.

children.title: Closure Membership Models
children.top_down_role: Optimization models assessing membership in a cut closure.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Membership Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Membership test for the intersection of all halfspaces represented by a normalized CGLP family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a family of valid inequalities and define its closure \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal F}=\bigcap_{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal F}\{x:\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\}\). Suppose a normalization chooses at least one positive representative of every inequality ray in \(\mathcal F\), and let \(K_N\) be the resulting coefficient set. Then \[\bar x\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal F}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \inf_{(\alpha,\beta)\in K_N}(\alpha^\top\bar x-\beta)\ge0.\] A negative optimum supplies a separating cut. A nonnegative optimum certifies membership only when \(K_N\) represents the entire intended family and the infimum problem is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point belongs to a cut closure exactly when every represented inequality has nonnegative slack there; a negative minimum returns a separator.
assumptions_latex: \(K_N\) contains a positive normalized representative of every inequality ray in \(\mathcal F\).
The infimum is evaluated globally over the complete represented family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal F}\) if and only if the minimum represented slack is nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Normalized coefficient representation of the family.

children.title: Mixed-Binary Disjunction Geometry
children.top_down_role: Disjunctive structure induced by binary variables within mixed-variable formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Binary Disjunction Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate disjunction for one binary variable in a mixed-binary relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^p\times[0,1]^q\) be a polyhedron with variables \((y,x)\), and fix \(k\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\). Define \(P_k^0=P\cap\{x_k=0\}\) and \(P_k^1=P\cap\{x_k=1\}\). The disjunctive hull associated with binary coordinate \(k\) is
\[D_k(P)=\operatorname{conv}(P_k^0\cup P_k^1).\]
Every mixed-binary feasible point of \(P\) belongs to \(D_k(P)\), while any point of \(P\setminus D_k(P)\) can be separated by a valid lift-and-project inequality for this disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary-coordinate disjunction partitions the relaxation into its zero and one faces; their convex hull contains every mixed-binary feasible point and excludes points cut by lift-and-project inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(x_k\) is required to be binary in the mixed-binary model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\cap(\mathbb R^p\times\{0,1\}^q)\subseteq D_k(P)=\operatorname{conv}(P_k^0\cup P_k^1)\subseteq P\).

notation.meaning: Face of P obtained by fixing binary coordinate k to t.
Convex hull of the two disjunctive faces.

children.title: Mixed-Binary Lifted Convexification
children.top_down_role: Extended-space convexification specialized to mixed-binary feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Binary Lifted Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenized two-branch formulation of a coordinate-disjunctive hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Az\le b\}\), and let coordinate \(z_k\) satisfy \(0\le z_k\le1\). Introduce \(z^0,z^1\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda_0,\lambda_1\ge0\). Then the lifted set
\[Q_k=\{(z,z^0,z^1,\lambda):z=z^0+z^1,\ Az^t\le b\lambda_t\ (t=0,1),\ z_k^0=0,\ z_k^1=\lambda_1,\ \lambda_0+\lambda_1=1\}\]
is an extended formulation of the convex hull of the branches \(P\cap\{z_k=0\}\) and \(P\cap\{z_k=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled copies of the zero and one branches, joined by convex-combination weights, form an extended formulation of the binary-disjunctive hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_z(Q_k)=\operatorname{conv}((P\cap\{z_k=0\})\cup(P\cap\{z_k=1\}))\).

notation.meaning: Homogenized branch copies of the original variables.

children.title: Projection to Mixed-Binary Model Space
children.top_down_role: Transfer of lifted inequalities into the original mixed-binary formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection to Mixed-Binary Model Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection property of the lifted coordinate-disjunction formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the lifted convexification \(Q_k\), eliminating \(z^0,z^1,\lambda_0,\lambda_1\) yields precisely the coordinate-disjunctive hull in the original model space. Consequently, an inequality \(\alpha^\top z\ge\beta\) is valid for \(\operatorname{proj}_z(Q_k)\) if and only if it is valid on both \(P\cap\{z_k=0\}\) and \(P\cap\{z_k=1\}\). Any such inequality is valid for every mixed-binary feasible point of \(P\), and it is a cut whenever the current relaxation point violates it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the lifted variables gives exactly the original-space disjunctive hull; its inequalities are precisely those valid on both binary branches.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_k\) is the homogenized two-branch formulation of the preceding record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^\top z\ge\beta\text{ is valid for }\operatorname{proj}_z(Q_k)\iff\alpha^\top z\ge\beta\text{ is valid for each branch}.\)

notation.meaning: Projection onto the original mixed-binary model variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex-Tableau Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tableau implementation of a fixed-disjunction lift-and-project separation step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a standard-form relaxation \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), a simplex basis \(B\), a fractional basic variable \(x_k\), and its split \(x_k\le\lfloor\bar x_k\rfloor\) or \(x_k\ge\lceil\bar x_k\rceil\). Express the associated tableau row and rays from the basic solution \(\bar x\); compute where each ray first meets either boundary of the split; form the resulting intersection inequality in nonbasic variables; then substitute the tableau equations to obtain an original-space inequality. Output it if violated by \(\bar x\); otherwise report no cut from this row and basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: From a fractional tableau row, intersect the basis cone’s rays with the two split boundaries, form the intersection inequality, and translate it back to original variables.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) has a feasible simplex basis.
\(x_k\) is integer-constrained and fractional at the basic solution.
The selected rays meet the split boundary or receive the standard zero coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output inequality is valid for \(P\cap(\{x_k\le\lfloor\bar x_k\rfloor\}\cup\{x_k\ge\lceil\bar x_k\rceil\})\).

children.title: Cut-Generating Linear Programs
children.top_down_role: CGLP formulations used to generate lift–project cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Generating Linear Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized multiplier formulation for separating a two-term split disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\}\), let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index the integer-constrained variables, and choose \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^n\) and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\) such that \(\pi_j=0\) for every \(j\notin I\). Consider the split \(\pi^\top x\le\pi_0\) or \(\pi^\top x\ge\pi_0+1\). For a point \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), solve
\[\min\ \alpha^\top\bar x-\beta\]
subject to
\[\alpha=u^\top A-u_0\pi=v^\top A+v_0\pi,\qquad \beta=u^\top b-u_0\pi_0=v^\top b+v_0(\pi_0+1),\]
with \(u,v\ge0\), \(u_0,v_0\ge0\), and the normalization \(\mathbf1^\top u+u_0+\mathbf1^\top v+v_0=1\). If the optimum is negative, output \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized linear program combines nonnegative implication multipliers from both branches of a valid mixed-integer split; a negative optimum gives an inequality that is valid on both branches and violated by the candidate point.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^n\), \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\), and \(\pi_j=0\) for all \(j\notin I\).
The normalized CGLP has an attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative optimum certifies that \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\) is valid for both disjunctive branches and separates \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative implication multipliers for the two branches.
Generated inequality coefficients and right-hand side.

knowledge_statements.title: Tableau–CGLP Representation Links
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of tableau intersection inequalities and normalized CGLP inequalities for a fixed split.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a split disjunction and a feasible simplex basis of \(P\). The intersection inequality obtained by applying the split to the corresponding tableau cone admits nonnegative branch multipliers satisfying the CGLP equations, hence is a CGLP-feasible lift-and-project cut after scaling. Conversely, a basic normalized CGLP solution whose active multiplier constraints determine a regular basis induces the same ray-boundary coefficients as the intersection cut from that basis. Thus tableau generation and the CGLP give primal-geometric and multiplier representations of the same fixed-disjunction inequality family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed split, tableau intersection cuts yield feasible CGLP multipliers, while regular basic CGLP solutions recover the corresponding tableau ray coefficients.
assumptions_latex: A split disjunction and a feasible simplex basis are fixed.
The converse is restricted to regular basic CGLP solutions admitting the associated tableau basis.
Inequalities are identified up to positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{tableau}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\mathrm{CGLP}}\), with equality for the regular basis-generated members described above.

notation.meaning: Cuts obtained from tableau cones for the fixed split.
Cuts represented by feasible normalized CGLP solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: CGLP basic solution yields an equivalent simple disjunctive cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward correspondence from a suitably structured basic feasible CGLP solution to the cut derived from its associated simplex-tableau row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha x\geq\beta\) be the lift-and-project cut associated with a basic feasible solution \((\alpha,\beta,u,u_0,v,v_0)\) of \((\mathrm{CGLP})_k\), where \(u_0,v_0>0\), every component of \((\alpha,\beta)\) is basic, and \(M_1,M_2\) index the basic components of \(u,v\), respectively. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated basic-feasibility, positivity, and basis assumptions, the lift-and-project cut represented by the CGLP solution is equivalent to the simple disjunctive cut from the associated tableau row.

\pi s_J\geq\pi_0\text{ is obtained by applying }x_k\leq0\vee x_k\geq1\text{ to tableau row (8.5) defined by }J

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LP-tableau pivots and equivalent CGLP basic solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between a combined source-row lift-and-project cut and a CGLP basis reached by an explicitly prescribed pivot sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose $(10.1)_{\gamma_{j_t}}$ is the combined source row obtained by pivoting on $\bar a_{ij_t}$, and $\pi x\geq\pi_0$ is the cut from $x_k+\gamma_{j_t}x_i\leq0\ \vee\ x_k+\gamma_{j_t}x_i\geq1$. The equivalent lift-and-project cut $\alpha x\geq\beta$ corresponds to a basic feasible solution of $(\mathrm{CGLP})_k$ reached by $t$ pivots: first, introduce $u_i$ or $v_i$, whichever has negative reduced cost, and remove the corresponding $u_{j_1}$ or $v_{j_1}$; for $h=2,\ldots,t-1$, exchange $u_{j_h}$ with $u_{j_{h+1}}$ when $\bar a_{kj_h}$ changes from positive to negative as $\gamma$ passes $\gamma_{j_h}$, or exchange $v_{j_h}$ with $v_{j_{h+1}}$ when it changes from negative to positive; finally, exchange $u_{j_{t-1}}$ with $u_{j_t}$, or $v_{j_{t-1}}$ with $v_{j_t}$. The transition from $\gamma_{j_h}$ to $\gamma_{j_{h+1}}$ is nondegenerate if and only if $\gamma_{j_h}\neq\gamma_{j_{h+1}}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A combined-source-row lift-and-project cut has an equivalent CGLP basic feasible solution obtained through a specified sequence of variable exchanges reflecting sign changes in the parameterized LP tableau. Each transition pivot is nondegenerate exactly when its consecutive gamma values differ.
assumptions_latex: (10.1)_{\gamma_{j_t}}\text{ is the combined source row obtained by pivoting on }\bar a_{ij_t}.
\alpha x\geq\beta\text{ is the lift-and-project cut equivalent to }\pi x\geq\pi_0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha x\geq\beta\text{ corresponds to a basic feasible solution of }(\mathrm{CGLP})_k\text{ reached by the prescribed }t\text{-pivot sequence, and a transition }h\text{ is nondegenerate}\iff\gamma_{j_h}\neq\gamma_{j_{h+1}}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converse correspondence from a nonsingular tableau basis and sign-compatible partition to the specified basic feasible CGLP representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat A\) be an \(n\times n\) nonsingular submatrix of \(\widetilde A\), let \(\widehat b\) be the corresponding subvector of \(\widetilde b\), and suppose \(0<e_k\widehat A^{-1}\widehat b<1\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: CGLP reduced costs from simplex-tableau data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit reduced-cost formulas for nonbasic CGLP multiplier columns obtained from simplex-tableau coefficients and surplus values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\alpha,\beta,u,u_0,v,v_0)\) be a basic feasible solution of (8.1), with \(u_0,v_0>0\), all components of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) basic, and the basic components of \(u\) and \(v\) indexed by \(M_1\) and \(M_2\), respectively. Let \(\bar s\) be the surplus vector of \(\widetilde A x\geq\widetilde b\) corresponding to \(\bar x\). For every \(i\notin J\cup\{k\}\), \[r_{u_i}=\sigma\left(-\sum_{j\in M_1}\bar a_{ij}+\sum_{j\in M_2}\bar a_{ij}-1\right)-\sum_{j\in M_2}\bar a_{ij}\bar s_j+\bar a_{i0}(1-\bar x_k),\] \[r_{v_i}=\sigma\left(\sum_{j\in M_1}\bar a_{ij}-\sum_{j\in M_2}\bar a_{ij}-1\right)-\sum_{j\in M_1}\bar a_{ij}\bar s_j+\bar a_{i0}\bar x_k,\] where \[\sigma=\frac{\sum_{j\in M_2}\bar a_{kj}\bar s_j-\bar a_{k0}(1-\bar x_k)}{1+\sum_{j\in J}|\bar a_{kj}|}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the specified CGLP basis conditions, the reduced costs of the indicated nonbasic u and v multiplier columns are given by the stated formulas in the simplex-tableau coefficients, surplus values, the value of the distinguished variable, and sigma.

Every component of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) is basic.
\(M_1\) and \(M_2\) index the basic components of \(u\) and \(v\), respectively.
\(\bar s\) is the surplus vector of \(\widetilde A x\geq\widetilde b\) corresponding to \(\bar x\).

children.title: Lift–Project Coefficient Lifting
children.top_down_role: Coefficient extensions for generated lift–project inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Project Coefficient Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal sequential lifting coefficient for a binary variable initially fixed to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\{0,1\}\), set \(S_t=\{x:(x,t)\in S\}\), and suppose \(a^\top x\ge b\) is valid for \(S_0\). If \(\inf_{x\in S_1}a^\top x\) is finite, then
\[a^\top x+\lambda z\ge b\]
is valid for \(S\) exactly when \(\lambda\ge b-\inf_{x\in S_1}a^\top x\). Therefore \(\lambda^*=b-\inf_{x\in S_1}a^\top x\) is the smallest valid lifting coefficient under the greater-than-or-equal convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary variable fixed during cut derivation can be restored using the smallest coefficient that covers the worst point on its opposite binary face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^*=b-\inf_{x\in S_1}a^\top x\) is the minimal valid lifting coefficient.

notation.meaning: Projection of the face with binary variable fixed to t.
Minimal coefficient lifting the inequality to both binary faces.

children.title: Lift–Project Modularization
children.top_down_role: Modular transformations used to improve cut coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Project Modularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Congruence-based strengthening of tableau coefficients belonging to integer variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an integer tableau equation
\[x_B=f+\sum_{j\in I}r_jx_j+\sum_{j\notin I}r_jx_j,\]
where \(x_B\) and \(x_j\) for \(j\in I\) are integer, choose integers \(m_j\) and rewrite it as
\[x_B-\sum_{j\in I}m_jx_j=f+\sum_{j\in I}(r_j-m_j)x_j+\sum_{j\notin I}r_jx_j.\]
Apply the same split or lift-and-project cut formula to the modified row, and select the admissible \(m_j\) minimizing the resulting cut coefficients. Output the strongest valid candidate found; congruence preserves the integer feasible points represented by the row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtract integer multiples of integer-variable columns from an integer tableau row, then apply the cut formula to coefficient representatives chosen for strength.
assumptions_latex: \(x_B\) and every \(x_j\) indexed by \(I\) are integer-constrained.
The subsequent cut formula is valid for the rewritten split row.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The modularized row has the same integer solutions as the original row and may yield a dominating lift-and-project cut.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iterative disjunctive modularization of a source row
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines source-row modularization for lift–project cut strengthening, its validity, and its repeated application after tableau pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k=\bar a_{k0}-\sum_{j\in J}\bar a_{kj}s_j\), where \(x_k\) is integer-constrained, \(J_1:=J\cap\{1,\ldots,p\}\) indexes the integer-constrained components, and \(J_2:=J\setminus J_1\). Set \(J_1^+:=\{j\in J_1:\bar a_{kj}-\lfloor\bar a_{kj}\rfloor\leq\bar a_{k0}\}\) and \(J_1^-:=J_1\setminus J_1^+\). Disjunctive modularization replaces the source row by \(y_k=\varphi_{k0}-\sum_{j\in J}\varphi_{kj}s_j\), where \(y_k\) is a new unrestricted-sign integer variable, \(\varphi_{k0}=\bar a_{k0}\), and \(\varphi_{kj}=\bar a_{kj}-\lfloor\bar a_{kj}\rfloor\) for \(j\in J_1^+\), \(\varphi_{kj}=\bar a_{kj}-\lceil\bar a_{kj}\rceil\) for \(j\in J_1^-\), and \(\varphi_{kj}=\bar a_{kj}\) for \(j\in J_2\). Every assignment satisfying the original row with integral \(x_k\) satisfies the modularized row with integral \(y_k\). The intersection cut obtained from the modularized row is the strengthened intersection cut, or MIG cut, obtained from the original row and dominates the corresponding unmodularized cut. In iterative disjunctive modularization, the modularized row remains the source row throughout the pivot sequence and is modularized again after each pivot using the same rule on its transformed coefficients; every such iteration improves the cut obtainable from the source row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an intersection-cut or MIG-cut tableau source row with an integer basic variable, modularization replaces coefficients associated with integer-constrained components by fractional-part or ceiling-residual coefficients according to the stated threshold, while leaving the other coefficients unchanged. The resulting row is valid whenever the original row has an integral basic variable. Its intersection cut is the strengthened intersection, or MIG, cut and dominates the cut from the unmodularized row. Reapplying modularization to the transformed source row after every pivot improves the cut obtainable from that row.
assumptions_latex: J_1=J\cap\{1,\ldots,p\}\text{ indexes integer-constrained components and }J_2=J\setminus J_1
\text{The row is used as a source row for an intersection cut or MIG cut.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The modularized row is valid, yields the strengthened intersection/MIG cut, dominates the unmodularized-row cut, and repeated post-pivot modularization improves the obtainable cut.}

knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Project Dominance Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance criterion for strengthened cuts on a nonnegative formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\), and suppose \(a^\top x\ge1\) and \(a'^\top x\ge1\) are valid for \(X\). If \(a'\le a\) componentwise, then the inequality with coefficient vector \(a'\) dominates the one with coefficient vector \(a\): every nonnegative point satisfying \(a'^\top x\ge1\) also satisfies \(a^\top x\ge1\). Hence valid lifting, modularization, or multiplier choices that decrease coefficients componentwise without changing the normalized right-hand side produce a no-weaker lift-and-project cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With nonnegative variables and equal normalized right-hand sides, a valid cut with componentwise smaller coefficients dominates the original cut.
assumptions_latex: Both inequalities are valid for \(X\) and normalized to right-hand side one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\ge0:a'^\top x\ge1\}\subseteq\{x\ge0:a^\top x\ge1\}\).

notation.meaning: Target mixed-integer feasible set in nonnegative variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Split-Cut Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate lift-and-project cuts as split-disjunctive valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^p\times[0,1]^q\), and let \(x_k\) be binary. The coordinate split is \(x_k\le0\) or \(x_k\ge1\). Its split hull is
\[S_k(P)=\operatorname{conv}((P\cap\{x_k\le0\})\cup(P\cap\{x_k\ge1\})).\]
Because \(0\le x_k\le1\) on \(P\), this equals \(\operatorname{conv}((P\cap\{x_k=0\})\cup(P\cap\{x_k=1\}))\), the coordinate lift-and-project hull. Consequently, inequalities obtained by projecting the lifted two-branch formulation are exactly the valid inequalities of this coordinate split hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded binary coordinate, its zero-or-one lift-and-project hull is exactly the hull generated by the coordinate split disjunction.
assumptions_latex: Coordinate \(x_k\) is binary in the target model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_k(P)=D_k(P)\), so coordinate lift-and-project inequalities are coordinate split cuts.

notation.meaning: Split hull for the coordinate split on x_k.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection-Cut Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between basis-cone intersection cuts and basis-generated lift-and-project cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar x\) be a basic feasible solution of a polyhedron \(P\), and let \(C=\bar x+\operatorname{cone}\{r^1,\ldots,r^m\}\) be its simplicial tableau cone. For a split whose interior contains \(\bar x\), let \(t_j>0\) be the first parameter for which \(\bar x+t_jr^j\) reaches a split boundary. The intersection inequality
\[\sum_{j=1}^m s_j/t_j\ge1\qquad\text{for }x=\bar x+\sum_{j=1}^m r^js_j,\ s\ge0\]
is the tableau representation of the lift-and-project inequality generated from the same basis and split, up to positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting each tableau-cone ray with a split boundary produces the same basis-dependent inequality as lift-and-project generation for that split.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a simplicial tableau cone at \(\bar x\).
Every relevant ray reaches a split boundary at finite positive parameter \(t_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The split intersection cut and the basis-generated lift-and-project cut coincide up to positive scaling.

notation.meaning: Extreme ray of the tableau cone.
First split-boundary intersection parameter on ray j.

knowledge_statements.title: GMI-Cut Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: GMI cuts as split intersection cuts and tableau-generated lift-and-project cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a simplex row
\[x_B=\bar x_B-\sum_{j\in N}a_js_j,\qquad s_j\ge0,\]
where \(x_B\) is integer-constrained and \(f=\bar x_B-\lfloor\bar x_B\rfloor\in(0,1)\). Applying the split \(x_B\le\lfloor\bar x_B\rfloor\) or \(x_B\ge\lceil\bar x_B\rceil\) to the tableau cone yields its intersection cut. After modular strengthening of coefficients associated with integer nonbasic variables, this inequality is the mixed-integer Gomory cut from the row. It is therefore a tableau-generated lift-and-project cut for the same split, up to positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The GMI cut from a fractional integer tableau row is the modularly strengthened intersection cut, hence a lift-and-project cut for the row’s split.
assumptions_latex: Integer nonbasic coefficients receive the standard modular strengthening.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{GMI row cut}=\text{strengthened split intersection cut}=\text{tableau lift-and-project cut}\) up to scaling.

notation.meaning: Fractional part of the basic value.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integer hull, corner polyhedron, and free-set construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational definitions and geometric construction for intersection cuts from an LP basis cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\} have rational data, and let P_I=P\cap\{x:x_j\in\mathbb Z,\ j\in N'\}. The integer hull is \operatorname{conv}(P_I). For a basic solution \bar x with associated LP cone C(J), the corner polyhedron is the convex hull of the integer-feasible points in C(J), denoted \operatorname{corner}(J). The containments are C(J)\supseteq P\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(P_I) and C(J)\supseteq\operatorname{corner}(J)\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(P_I). A convex set S is P_I\text{-free} when \operatorname{int}(S)\cap P_I=\varnothing. If \bar x\in\operatorname{int}(S), then P\cap\operatorname{int}(S) contains no feasible mixed-integer point. When the extreme rays of C(J) meet \operatorname{bd}(S), their boundary intersections determine the intersection-cut hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integer hull is the convex hull of the feasible mixed-integer points, while the corner polyhedron is the convex hull of the integer-feasible points in the LP basis cone. A convex set is P_I-free if its interior contains no feasible mixed-integer point. If such a set contains the current fractional basic solution in its interior, that interior can be excluded; intersections of the basis-cone rays with its boundary provide the intersection-cut construction.
assumptions_latex: P=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\text{ has rational data}
\bar x\text{ is an LP basic solution with associated cone }C(J)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C(J)\supseteq P\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(P_I),\quad C(J)\supseteq\operatorname{corner}(J)\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(P_I),\quad P\cap\operatorname{int}(S)\cap P_I=\varnothing;\text{ when the required ray-boundary intersections exist, they define the intersection-cut construction.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ray-Length Formula for Parametric Multirow Intersection-Cut Coefficients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses each coefficient of the intersection cut from a normalized parametric cross-polytope as the reciprocal of the corresponding ray's boundary distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widetilde K^*(v)\) be the parametric cross-polytope in \(x\)-space associated with admissible parameters \(v\), and substitute
\[
x=f-\sum_{j\in J}\bar a_j s_j,\qquad s_j\ge 0,
\]
to obtain its representation \(\widetilde K^{*(n)}(v)\) in \(s\)-space. For each \(j\in J\), let
\[
s_j^*=\max\{t\ge 0:f-\bar a_j t\in\widetilde K^*(v)\}.
\]
Then the intersection cut generated from \(\widetilde K^{*(n)}(v)\) is
\[
\sum_{j\in J}\widetilde\alpha_j s_j\ge 1,
\qquad
\widetilde\alpha_j=\frac{1}{s_j^*}\quad(j\in J).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pull the normalized parametric cross-polytope back through the nonnegative tableau-ray representation. The coefficient for each ray in the resulting intersection cut equals the reciprocal of the distance from f to the cross-polytope boundary along that ray.
assumptions_latex: v\text{ satisfies the defining nonnegativity and normalization conditions for }\widetilde K^*(v)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j\in J}\widetilde\alpha_j s_j\ge 1,\qquad \widetilde\alpha_j=(s_j^*)^{-1}\quad(j\in J).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Standard versus restricted intersection cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the two free-set regimes and records their inclusion, possible strength difference, and nonbasic-coefficient sign distinction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C(J) be the LP cone associated with an optimal LP cobasis J. A standard intersection cut (SIC) is obtained by intersecting the extreme rays of C(J) with the boundary of a convex P_I-free set S, meaning \operatorname{int}(S)\cap P_I=\varnothing. A restricted intersection cut (RIC) instead uses a convex lattice-free set S', meaning \operatorname{int}(S')\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing. Hence every RIC is an SIC, but SICs may also arise from P_I-free sets that are not lattice-free. If a facet of S' has only infeasible integer points in its relative interior, replacing S' by a larger P_I-free set may yield a stronger cut. RIC coefficients in the nonbasic variables are nonnegative, whereas SIC coefficients may be negative. For a P_I-free polyhedron with facets \sum_{j\in J}d_{ij}x_j\le d_{i0},\ i\in Q, under the facet normalization d_{i0}>0, the associated disjunctive-cut coefficients satisfy \delta_j=\max_{i\in Q}d_{ij}/d_{i0}; therefore, if d_{ij}<0 for every i\in Q, then \delta_j<0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard intersection cuts use convex sets whose interiors contain no feasible integer point, whereas restricted intersection cuts use convex sets whose interiors contain no integer point at all. Thus restricted cuts form a subclass of standard cuts. Enlarging a lattice-free set to a feasible-integer-point-free set may produce a stronger cut when a facet has only infeasible integer points in its relative interior. Restricted cuts have nonnegative coefficients in the nonbasic variables, while standard cuts may have negative coefficients; with positively normalized facet right-hand sides, a coefficient is negative when all its corresponding facet coefficients are negative.
assumptions_latex: C(J)\text{ is the LP cone associated with an optimal LP cobasis }J.
S=\left\{x:\sum_{j\in J}d_{ij}x_j\le d_{i0},\ i\in Q\right\},\quad d_{i0}>0\text{ for the coefficient-sign implication}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{RIC}\subseteq\mathrm{SIC},\qquad \delta_j=\max_{i\in Q}\frac{d_{ij}}{d_{i0}},\qquad \left(\forall i\in Q,\ d_{ij}<0\right)\Rightarrow\delta_j<0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity of the standard intersection cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and separation guarantee for the full-ray intersection cut generated from a convex P_I-free set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Standard intersection cut from a mixed-integer-free convex set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the ray-intersection parameters and associated cut, including finite boundary intersections and recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be closed and convex, with \bar{x}\in\operatorname{int}(C) and \operatorname{int}(C)\cap(\mathbb{Z}^p\times\mathbb{R}^{n-p})=\varnothing. For each extreme ray \bar r^j of \operatorname{corner}(B), define the extended-real parameter \alpha_j:=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:\bar{x}+\alpha\bar r^j\in C\}\in(0,+\infty]. If \alpha_j<+\infty, then \bar{x}+\alpha_j\bar r^j\in\partial C and \bar{x}+\alpha\bar r^j\in\operatorname{int}(C) for 0\leq\alpha<\alpha_j. If \bar r^j\in\operatorname{rec}(C), then \alpha_j=+\infty. With 1/(+\infty):=0, the inequality \sum_{j\in N}x_j/\alpha_j\geq1 is the intersection cut defined by C for \operatorname{corner}(B).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect every corner ray with the boundary of a closed convex mixed-integer-free set containing the corner apex. Reciprocal intersection distances give the cut coefficients, while recession directions receive coefficient zero.
assumptions_latex: \{\bar r^j:j\in N\}\text{ are the extreme rays of }\operatorname{corner}(B)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_j:=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:\bar{x}+\alpha\bar r^j\in C\},\quad \frac{1}{+\infty}:=0,\qquad \sum_{j\in N}\frac{x_j}{\alpha_j}\geq1\text{ is the intersection cut defined by }C.

children.title: Restricted Intersection Cuts

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is an admissible open convex \(S\)-free set containing \(\bar x\), selected from a prescribed restricted class \(\mathcal C_R\).

notation.meaning: Permitted restricted family of convex forbidden sets.
Ray exit parameter for the selected set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic restriction-by-admissible-family sense; the navigation context does not specify a particular restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a prescribed family \(\mathcal C_R\) of admissible open convex \(S\)-free sets containing \(\bar x\), a restricted intersection cut is an inequality obtained from some \(C\in\mathcal C_R\): \[\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{s_j}{t_j(C)}\ge1,\qquad t_j(C)=\sup\{t\ge0:\bar x+t r^j\in C\}.\] The restriction concerns which forbidden sets or ray intersections may be used; it does not alter the validity argument for an admitted \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted intersection cut uses the usual ray-exit formula but permits only forbidden sets from a specified subclass, potentially limiting the strongest available cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Intersection Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic definition is plausible, but the immutable context does not identify what restriction defines this taxonomy leaf. An authoritative source specifying the intended admissible family or restriction regime is required before the local mathematical sense can be verified.

children.title: Restriction Strength Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Strength consequences of limiting rays or relaxation portions.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C_1\subseteq\mathcal C_2\) are admissible families of open convex \(S\)-free sets containing the same cone apex.
\(V(\mathcal C)\) denotes all intersection cuts generated from members of \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(\mathcal C_1)\subseteq V(\mathcal C_2)\), so restricting the admissible family cannot improve the best attainable dominance bound.

notation.meaning: Cuts obtainable from an admissible family.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion boundary for restriction; no quantitative approximation factor is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because every \(C\in\mathcal C_1\) also belongs to \(\mathcal C_2\), the generated cut families satisfy \[V(\mathcal C_1)\subseteq V(\mathcal C_2).\] Hence restriction can preserve the unrestricted strength only if the restricted family contains a cut matching or dominating an unrestricted optimum under the chosen strength criterion. If no such member exists, the restriction necessarily loses attainable strength; no universal quantitative loss follows from family inclusion alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller admissible family produces no more cuts than a larger one. It matches unrestricted strength only when it contains an equally strong or dominating cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Restriction Strength Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Family inclusion does imply inclusion of generated cuts, but the statements about matching an unrestricted optimum depend on an introduced strength criterion and existence or attainment assumptions. No source establishes that this is the intended restriction-strength boundary for the leaf.

children.title: Generalized Intersection Cuts

assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) contains \(\bar x\) in its interior and satisfies \(D\cap S=\varnothing\).
Every ray has a well-defined first exit parameter \(t_j\in(0,\infty]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever the stated ray-covering conditions hold, \(\sum_j s_j/t_j\ge1\) is valid for \(Q\cap S\).

notation.meaning: Possibly nonstandard forbidden region used by the generalized construction.
First parameter at which ray j exits D.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract ray-exit extension; additional hypotheses depend on the intended generalized-intersection-cut theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generalized ray-exit construction assigns \(t_j=\inf\{t>0:\bar x+t r^j\notin D\}\) and proposes \[\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{s_j}{t_j}\ge1.\] Validity requires the generalized forbidden region and exit rule to ensure that every \(s\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\) with \(\bar x+\sum_j r^j s_j\in S\) has weighted ray usage at least one. Convex \(D\) recovers the standard intersection-cut construction; broader choices require separately stated covering conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized intersection cuts retain a ray-exit inequality beyond the standard corner-cone setting, but validity requires an explicit condition ensuring every feasible ray combination exits the forbidden region.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Intersection Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a nonconvex or otherwise generalized region, first ray exits alone do not establish the displayed inequality. The stated covering condition largely restates the desired validity conclusion, and no authoritative source identifies the intended generalized-intersection-cut framework or sufficient hypotheses.

children.title: Finite Group Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Group problems over finite residue structures.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite abelian group with identity \(0\), and \(b\in G\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(G,b)=\operatorname{conv}\{y\in\mathbb{Z}_+^G:\sum_{g\in G}g y_g=b\text{ in }G\}\) is the finite group polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer finite abelian group model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The finite group relaxation for residue \(b\) has feasible set \[Y(G,b)=\left\{y\in\mathbb{Z}_+^G:\sum_{g\in G}g y_g=b\text{ in }G\right\}.\] Its finite group polyhedron is \(P(G,b)=\operatorname{conv}Y(G,b)\). A linear inequality \(\sum_{g
e0}\pi(g)y_g\ge1\) is valid precisely when its coefficient function gives at least one on every nonnegative integer combination having group sum \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite group relaxation selects nonnegative integer multiplicities of group elements whose residue sum equals a prescribed nonzero group element.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Group Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite abelian group formulation is mathematically standard and the definition content kind fits, but the record supplies no citation with an inspectable locator. Source support is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis-Form Integer Program Equivalent to the Group Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent integer-program representation induced by an optimal basis of the LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(A_B\) is an optimal basis matrix for the linear-programming relaxation of the integer program, then the associated group problem is equivalent to
\[z_{A_B}(b)=\max\left\{c_Bx_B+c_Nx_N:A_Bx_B+A_Nx_N=b,\ x_B\in\mathbb Z^m,\ x_N\in\mathbb Z_+^{n-m}\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an optimal LP basis, the associated group problem is equivalent to an integer program with unrestricted-in-sign integer basic variables and nonnegative integer nonbasic variables.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{GP}\equiv\max\left\{c_Bx_B+c_Nx_N:A_Bx_B+A_Nx_N=b,\ x_B\in\mathbb Z^m,\ x_N\in\mathbb Z_+^{n-m}\right\}

children.title: Lattice-Free Geometry

children.title: Maximal Lattice-Free Sets
children.top_down_role: Maximal forbidden-interior regions supporting strong cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Lattice-Free Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean lattice-free convexity with respect to the standard integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A closed convex set \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is lattice-free if \(\operatorname{int}(B)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n=\varnothing\), where the interior is taken in \(\mathbb{R}^n\). It is maximal lattice-free if it is lattice-free and, for every closed convex lattice-free set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(B\subseteq C\), one has \(C=B\). Thus maximality is inclusion-maximality among closed convex sets whose ordinary interior contains no integer point; it does not mean maximal volume or maximal dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximal lattice-free set is a closed convex region with no interior integer point that admits no proper closed convex lattice-free enlargement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\text{ is maximal lattice-free}\iff \operatorname{int}(B)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n=\varnothing\text{ and no proper closed convex lattice-free superset contains }B\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically precise and fits the container, but it has no citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Lattice-Free Structural Type Taxonomy

children.title: Split Lattice-Free Types
children.top_down_role: Maximal lattice-free regions having split geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Split Lattice-Free Types
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard split sets for the integer lattice in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a primitive vector \(a\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), meaning that the greatest common divisor of its coordinates is one, and an integer \(\beta\in\mathbb{Z}\), the split determined by \((a,\beta)\) is
\[S(a,\beta)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\beta\le a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta+1\}.\]
Its interior contains no point of \(\mathbb{Z}^n\), because \(a^{\mathsf T}z\) is integral for every \(z\in\mathbb{Z}^n\). The primitivity of \(a\) makes both boundary hyperplanes contain integer points and makes \(S(a,\beta)\) maximal lattice-free.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split is the unit-width slab between two consecutive integer hyperplanes having a primitive integral normal; it is maximal lattice-free.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(a,\beta)\) is maximal lattice-free in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: split slab defined by consecutive lattice hyperplanes
scalar product of a and x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The split definition and maximality claim are standard, but no source supports them. The explanatory sentence beginning “because” is proof-like and should be removed when the record is sourced.

children.title: Polyhedral Lattice-Free Types
children.top_down_role: Maximal lattice-free regions with nonsplit polyhedral geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Lattice-Free Types
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet characterization of full-dimensional maximal lattice-free convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a full-dimensional closed convex set with \(\operatorname{int}(B)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n=\varnothing\). Then \(B\) is maximal lattice-free if and only if \(B\) is a polyhedron and the relative interior of every facet of \(B\) contains a point of \(\mathbb{Z}^n\). Moreover, every such polyhedron has at most \(2^n\) facets. Consequently, full-dimensional maximal lattice-free sets admit finite irredundant halfspace descriptions, with each defining facet anchored by an integer point in its relative interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-dimensional lattice-free convex set is maximal exactly when it is polyhedral and every facet contains an integer point in its relative interior; it has at most 2^n facets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\text{ is maximal lattice-free}\iff B\text{ is polyhedral and }\operatorname{relint}(F)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\ne\varnothing\text{ for every facet }F\), and \(B\) has at most \(2^n\) facets.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the polyhedral-types container, but the facet characterization and the bound of 2^n facets require an authoritative theorem locator.

children.title: Dimensional Type Regimes
children.top_down_role: Lattice-free type distinctions across ambient dimensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimensional Type Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension dichotomy for maximal lattice-free closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every maximal lattice-free closed convex set \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) lies in exactly one of two regimes. Either \(\dim(B)=n\), in which case \(B\) is a polyhedron whose every facet contains an integer point in its relative interior, or \(\dim(B)=n-1\), in which case \(B\) is an affine hyperplane whose direction space is not a rational subspace. No maximal lattice-free closed convex set has dimension below \(n-1\). Here a subspace is rational when it is generated by vectors in \(\mathbb{Q}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximal lattice-free sets are either full-dimensional facet-anchored polyhedra or irrational affine hyperplanes; lower-dimensional regimes cannot be maximal.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a maximal lattice-free closed convex set
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim(B)=n\) with the facet property, or \(\dim(B)=n-1\) and \(B\) is an irrational affine hyperplane.

notation.meaning: dimension of the affine hull of B

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dimensional dichotomy fits the container, but the precise characterization of the codimension-one regime and exclusion of lower dimensions require authoritative support.

children.title: Gauge Representations
children.top_down_role: Gauge-based representations of cuts from lattice-free regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge form of a closed convex neighborhood of the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}(K)\). Its gauge is
\[\gamma_K(r)=\inf\{\lambda>0:r\in\lambda K\}.\]
Then \(K=\{r\in\mathbb{R}^n:\gamma_K(r)\le1\}\), and \(\gamma_K\) is finite, nonnegative, positively homogeneous, and subadditive. If
\[K=\{r\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}r\le1,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},\]
then
\[\gamma_K(r)=\max\left\{0,\max_{1\le i\le m}a_i^{\mathsf T}r\right\}.\]
If this polyhedron is bounded, the zero term is redundant. For a lattice-free set \(B\) containing \(f\) in its interior, the representation applies to \(K=B-f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex neighborhood of the origin is the unit sublevel set of its gauge. For a polyhedron, the gauge is the maximum of zero and its normalized defining functionals; zero is redundant when the polyhedron is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=\{r\in\mathbb{R}^n:\gamma_K(r)\le1\}\), with \(\gamma_K(r)=\max\{0,\max_i a_i^{\mathsf T}r\}\) in the stated polyhedral case.

notation.meaning: normal of a normalized defining inequality

children.title: Blocking Representations

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blocking duality for nonnegative blocking polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty blocking polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\), define its blocker by
\[\operatorname{bl}(P)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:y^{\mathsf T}x\ge1\text{ for every }x\in P\}.\]
Then \(\operatorname{bl}(P)\) is a blocking polyhedron and
\[P=\operatorname{bl}(\operatorname{bl}(P))=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:y^{\mathsf T}x\ge1\text{ for every }y\in\operatorname{bl}(P)\}.\]
Thus the points of the blocker provide a complete, possibly redundant, inequality representation of \(P\), and its minimal points determine the undominated blocking inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A blocking polyhedron equals the blocker of its blocker, so points of its blocker give all normalized nonnegative inequalities defining it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{bl}(\operatorname{bl}(P))=P\).

children.title: Polarity Representations

knowledge_statements.title: Polarity Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar representation for closed convex neighborhoods of the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}(K)\), and define
\[K^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:y^{\mathsf T}x\le1\text{ for every }x\in K\}.\]
Then the bipolar identity gives
\[K=(K^\circ)^\circ=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:y^{\mathsf T}x\le1\text{ for every }y\in K^\circ\}.\]
Moreover, the gauge of \(K\) is the support function of its polar:
\[\gamma_K(x)=\sup_{y\in K^\circ}y^{\mathsf T}x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex neighborhood of zero is recovered from its polar, and its gauge equals the polar’s support function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=(K^\circ)^\circ\) and \(\gamma_K=\sigma_{K^\circ}\).

children.title: Representation Translations
children.top_down_role: Structural translations among gauge, blocking, and polar viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Translations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact translations among facet, gauge, polar, and blocking descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le1,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) is a polytope with \(0\in\operatorname{int}(K)\) and an irredundant normalized facet description. Then
\[K^\circ=\operatorname{conv}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\},\qquad \gamma_K(x)=\max_i a_i^{\mathsf T}x=\sup_{y\in K^\circ}y^{\mathsf T}x.\]
Thus normalized facet normals become vertices of the polar, and their maximum becomes the gauge. For a blocking polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\), reversing the inequality orientation yields the analogous recovery formula
\[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:y^{\mathsf T}x\ge1\text{ for every }y\in\operatorname{bl}(P)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized facets become polar vertices; maximizing their functionals gives the gauge, while blocker points analogously encode normalized lower inequalities.
assumptions_latex: the displayed facet description is normalized and irredundant
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K^\circ=\operatorname{conv}\{a_i\}_{i=1}^m\), \(\gamma_K=\sigma_{K^\circ}\), and \(P=\operatorname{bl}(\operatorname{bl}(P))\).

children.title: Pure-Integer Infinite Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Infinite relaxations with purely integer activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Pure-Integer Infinite Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support pure-integer group relaxation over the standard lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(f\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\mathbb{Z}^n\). The pure-integer infinite relaxation is
\[R_f^{\mathrm I}=\left\{y:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{Z}_+\text{ of finite support}:f+\sum_{r\in\mathbb{R}^n}r\,y(r)\in\mathbb{Z}^n\right\}.\]
A function \(\pi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) defines a normalized valid inequality when
\[\sum_{r\in\mathbb{R}^n}\pi(r)y(r)\ge1\qquad\text{for every }y\in R_f^{\mathrm I}.\]
All displayed sums are finite because every feasible activity function has finite support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pure-integer infinite relaxation uses finitely supported nonnegative integer multiplicities whose weighted displacement moves a fractional base point to the integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_f^{\mathrm I}=\{y:f+\sum_r r y(r)\in\mathbb{Z}^n,\ y(r)\in\mathbb{Z}_+,\ y\text{ has finite support}\}\).

notation.meaning: integer multiplicity assigned to direction r
coefficient function of a normalized valid inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-support pure-integer model is precise and fits the container, but neither its convention nor its normalized-validity formulation has a citation.

children.title: Continuous Infinite Relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Infinite Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support continuous infinite group relaxation at a fractional base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(f\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\mathbb{Z}^n\). The continuous infinite relaxation is
\[R_f^{\mathrm C}=\left\{s:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\text{ of finite support}:f+\sum_{r\in\mathbb{R}^n}r\,s(r)\in\mathbb{Z}^n\right\}.\]
A function \(\psi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) defines a normalized valid inequality if
\[\sum_{r\in\mathbb{R}^n}\psi(r)s(r)\ge1\qquad\text{for every }s\in R_f^{\mathrm C}.\]
Finite support makes both the lattice equation and inequality algebraically well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous infinite relaxation assigns finitely supported nonnegative real weights to directions so that the displaced fractional base point reaches the integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_f^{\mathrm C}=\{s:f+\sum_r r s(r)\in\mathbb{Z}^n,\ s(r)\in\mathbb{R}_+,\ s\text{ has finite support}\}\).

notation.meaning: continuous activity assigned to direction r
coefficient function of a normalized valid inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The continuous finite-support model is internally consistent and fits the container, but its exact infinite-relaxation convention requires an authoritative locator.

children.title: Mixed-Integer Infinite Relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Infinite Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support mixed infinite group relaxation with integer and continuous activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(f\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\mathbb{Z}^n\). The mixed-integer infinite relaxation is
\[R_f^{\mathrm{MI}}=\left\{(y,s):f+\sum_r r\,y(r)+\sum_r r\,s(r)\in\mathbb{Z}^n\right\},\]
where \(y:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{Z}_+\) and \(s:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\) have finite support. A pair \((\pi,\psi)\) defines a normalized valid inequality if
\[\sum_r\pi(r)y(r)+\sum_r\psi(r)s(r)\ge1\qquad\text{for every }(y,s)\in R_f^{\mathrm{MI}}.\]
The first coefficient function prices integer activity and the second prices continuous activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed infinite relaxation combines finitely supported integer and real nonnegative activities whose total displacement carries a fractional base point to the lattice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y,s)\in R_f^{\mathrm{MI}}\iff y\ge0\text{ is integer-valued},\ s\ge0,\text{ and }f+\sum_r r y(r)+\sum_r r s(r)\in\mathbb{Z}^n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mixed integer/continuous activity model is coherent and properly scoped, but its formulation and normalized inequality convention are unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Valid-Function Taxonomy

children.title: Minimal Valid Functions
children.top_down_role: Valid functions minimal under pointwise dominance.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Valid Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise minimality for normalized valid functions of the pure-integer infinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(f\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\mathbb{Z}^n\). A nonnegative function \(\pi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\) is valid for \(R_f^{\mathrm I}\) if
\[\sum_r\pi(r)y(r)\ge1\qquad\text{for every }y\in R_f^{\mathrm I}.\]
It is minimal valid if there is no distinct valid function \(\pi':\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\) satisfying \(\pi'(r)\le\pi(r)\) for every \(r\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Equivalently, no coefficient can be decreased, possibly together with other coefficients, while retaining validity throughout the infinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid function is minimal when no distinct valid function is pointwise smaller, so its normalized inequality is undominated within the same coefficient class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\text{ is minimal valid}\iff \nexists\,\pi'\ne\pi\text{ valid with }\pi'(r)\le\pi(r)\text{ for all }r\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise minimality definition is precise and appropriate for this container, but it requires an authoritative source tied to the stated pure-integer infinite relaxation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimality and Additivity Domains Under Valid Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex decompositions of a minimal valid function into valid functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi\) be a minimal valid function and suppose \(\pi=\tfrac12\pi_1+\tfrac12\pi_2\), where \(\pi_1\) and \(\pi_2\) are valid functions. Then \(\pi_1\) and \(\pi_2\) are minimal functions and \(E(\pi)\subseteq E(\pi_1)\cap E(\pi_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a minimal valid function is the average of two valid functions, both components are minimal, and every additivity relation of the average is an additivity relation of each component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi_1,\pi_2\text{ are minimal functions and }E(\pi)\subseteq E(\pi_1)\cap E(\pi_2).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of Minimal Valid Functions for the Infinite Group Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal valid functions for the infinite group relaxation G_f.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(\pi:\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}_+\) is minimal valid for \(G_f\) if and only if \(\pi(0)=0\), \(\pi\) is subadditive and periodic, and \(\pi\) satisfies the symmetry condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative function on R^q is minimal valid for G_f exactly when it vanishes at zero, is subadditive and periodic, and satisfies the symmetry condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi\text{ is minimal valid for }G_f\iff \pi(0)=0,\ \pi\text{ is subadditive and periodic, and }\pi\text{ satisfies the symmetry condition.}

children.title: Valid-Function Exposure Classes
children.top_down_role: Indecomposable and supporting functional structures.

children.title: Extreme Valid Functions
children.top_down_role: Indecomposable valid functions within the relevant convex family.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Valid Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme points of a convex, normalized valid-function class for a fixed relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal V\) be a convex set of valid functions for a fixed relaxation, contained in a real vector space of functions and subject to the same normalization. A function \(\pi\in\mathcal V\) is extreme in \(\mathcal V\) if, whenever \(\pi=\lambda\pi_1+(1-\lambda)\pi_2\) for some \(\pi_1,\pi_2\in\mathcal V\) and \(0<\lambda<1\), one has \(\pi_1=\pi_2=\pi\). Equivalently, \(\pi\) does not lie in any nontrivial open line segment contained in \(\mathcal V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid function is extreme when it cannot be expressed as a proper convex combination of two distinct normalized valid functions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal V\) is a convex class of valid functions with a fixed normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\in\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal V)\iff [\pi=\lambda\pi_1+(1-\lambda)\pi_2,\ 0<\lambda<1]\Rightarrow \pi_1=\pi_2=\pi.\)

notation.meaning: set of extreme elements of the class

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, and the mathematical statement is a standard extreme-point definition. However, the record supplies no citation, while the fixed valid-function class and normalization are framework-dependent. A source with a specific definition, section, theorem, or page locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Slope Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional minimal valid functions in the infinite-relaxation setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be a minimal valid function. If \(\pi|_{[0,1]}\) is continuous and piecewise linear with only two slopes, then \(\pi\) is extreme.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal valid function on the real line is extreme if its restriction to the unit interval is continuous, piecewise linear, and has only two slopes.
assumptions_latex: \pi|_{[0,1]}\text{ is continuous and piecewise linear with only two slopes}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi\text{ is extreme.}
