children.title: Exposed Valid Functions
children.top_down_role: Valid functions isolated by supporting functionals.

knowledge_statements.title: Exposed Valid Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exposure by a continuous linear functional on an ambient topological function space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a real locally convex topological vector space and let \(\mathcal V\subseteq E\) be a convex class of normalized valid functions. A function \(\pi\in\mathcal V\) is exposed in \(\mathcal V\) if there exists a continuous linear functional \(L:E\to\mathbb R\) such that \(L(\pi)<L(\varphi)\) for every \(\varphi\in\mathcal V\setminus\{\pi\}\). Thus \(\pi\) is the unique minimizer of \(L\) over \(\mathcal V\); changing the sign of \(L\) gives the equivalent unique-maximizer convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid function is exposed when some continuous linear functional uniquely optimizes at that function over the normalized valid-function class.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a real locally convex topological vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\in\operatorname{exp}(\mathcal V)\iff \exists L\in E'\ \forall\varphi\in\mathcal V\setminus\{\pi\}:L(\pi)<L(\varphi).\)

notation.meaning: continuous dual of the ambient space

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, and the minimizer and maximizer conventions are equivalent. The choice of a locally convex ambient space and continuous dual is nevertheless substantive and unsupported by any cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Extremality–Exposedness Gap
children.top_down_role: Regimes where extremality does not yield exposedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Extremality–Exposedness Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The general convex-geometric distinction between extreme and exposed valid functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any convex valid-function class \(\mathcal V\) in a real locally convex space, every exposed function is extreme: \(\operatorname{exp}(\mathcal V)\subseteq\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal V)\). The converse is not a consequence of convexity alone. The extremality–exposedness gap is the set \(\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal V)\setminus\operatorname{exp}(\mathcal V)\); it consists precisely of extreme valid functions for which no continuous linear functional has that function as its unique optimizer over \(\mathcal V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exposure implies extremality, but an extreme valid function need not be uniquely selected by any continuous linear functional.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal V\) is convex in a real locally convex topological vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{exp}(\mathcal V)\subseteq\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal V)\), while equality requires additional hypotheses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and exposed points are extreme under the stated definitions. But the record does not cite a source establishing that the possible strictness of the inclusion applies in the intended valid-function framework; general convex-geometric possibility alone does not establish a nonempty valid-function gap.

children.title: Piecewise-Linear Approximation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Finite-complexity function classes and approximation structures.

children.title: Piecewise-Linear Valid Functions
children.top_down_role: Valid functions represented by finitely many linear pieces.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Linear Valid Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional infinite-group relaxation with finitely many linear pieces per period.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(f\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\). A periodic function \(\pi:\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R\) is a piecewise-linear valid function if there are breakpoints \(0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_m=1\) such that a representative of \(\pi\) is affine on every \([t_{k-1},t_k]\), and if every finitely supported \(y:\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z_+\) satisfying \(\sum_r r y(r)=f\) in \(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) also satisfies \(\sum_r\pi(r)y(r)\ge 1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A piecewise-linear valid function has finitely many affine pieces per period and yields a valid inequality for every feasible group-relaxation vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_r r y(r)=f\Rightarrow\sum_r\pi(r)y(r)\ge1.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and consistently specifies the one-dimensional infinite-group model, finite support, periodic domain, and piecewise linearity. No cited source supports this exact group-relaxation convention or supplies a specific locator.

children.title: Valid-Function Approximation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Approximation structures for more general valid functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Valid-Function Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform approximation constrained to remain inside the valid-function class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal V\) be a class of bounded valid functions on a common domain \(D\), and let \(\mathcal V_m^{\mathrm{PL}}\subseteq\mathcal V\) contain functions having at most \(m\) affine pieces. A sequence \((\pi_m)\) is a uniform valid-function approximation of \(\pi\in\mathcal V\) if \(\pi_m\in\mathcal V_m^{\mathrm{PL}}\) and \(\|\pi_m-\pi\|_\infty\to0\). It is an outer approximation when additionally \(\pi_m\ge\pi\) pointwise, and an inner approximation when \(\pi_m\le\pi\) pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid-function approximation uses increasingly rich piecewise-linear valid functions, optionally preserving pointwise outer or inner dominance, with uniform error tending to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal V\) consists of bounded functions on a common domain \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_m\in\mathcal V_m^{\mathrm{PL}}\) and \(\|\pi_m-\pi\|_\infty\to0\).

notation.meaning: valid functions with at most m affine pieces
uniform norm on the common domain

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind is plausible for the leaf, but the proposed taxonomy of uniform, inner, and outer valid-function approximation is framework-dependent. No source establishes these conventions, the relevant common domain, or the existence and nesting behavior of the stated piecewise-linear subclasses.

children.title: Approximation Complexity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between representational complexity and approximation quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximation Complexity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best uniform error as a function of the permitted number of affine pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\pi\in\mathcal V\), define \(E_m(\pi)=\inf\{\|\varphi-\pi\|_\infty:\varphi\in\mathcal V_m^{\mathrm{PL}}\}\), where \(\mathcal V_m^{\mathrm{PL}}\subseteq\mathcal V_{m+1}^{\mathrm{PL}}\) is the class of valid functions with at most \(m\) affine pieces. Then \(E_{m+1}(\pi)\le E_m(\pi)\). The least piece complexity achieving tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) is \(M_\pi(\varepsilon)=\inf\{m:E_m(\pi)\le\varepsilon\}\). If \(\pi\) lies in the uniform closure of \(\bigcup_m\mathcal V_m^{\mathrm{PL}}\), then \(E_m(\pi)\to0\) and \(M_\pi(\varepsilon)<\infty\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best uniform error cannot increase with the allowed number of pieces; approximability guarantees finite piece complexity for every positive tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi\) lies in the uniform closure of \(\bigcup_m\mathcal V_m^{\mathrm{PL}}\) for the convergence conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{m+1}(\pi)\le E_m(\pi)\), and under the closure assumption \(E_m(\pi)\to0\).

notation.meaning: best uniform error using at most m pieces
least piece budget attaining tolerance epsilon

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is compatible with the terminal container, and the monotonicity and closure conclusions follow from the definitions. Nevertheless, the record gives only an abstract error-versus-piece-budget formulation, not a sourced approximation-complexity result or quantitative tradeoff for valid functions. A specific authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Lifting Multiplicity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Existence and multiplicity regimes for lifting valid functions.

children.title: Unique Lifting Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings in which a valid function admits a unique lifting.

knowledge_statements.title: Unique Lifting Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of integer-variable coefficients when a continuous-variable valid function is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(f\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\) and a valid function \(\pi\) for the continuous group relaxation. Let \(\mathcal L(\pi)\) be the set of functions \(\psi:\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R\) such that \(\sum_r\pi(r)s(r)+\sum_r\psi(r)y(r)\ge1\) whenever \(s\) and \(y\) have finite support, \(s(r)\in\mathbb R_+\), \(y(r)\in\mathbb Z_+\), and \(\sum_r r(s(r)+y(r))=f\). The lifting regime of \(\pi\) is unique exactly when \(\mathcal L(\pi)\) is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A base valid function has unique lifting when exactly one integer-variable coefficient function preserves validity for the mixed group relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\) has unique lifting \(\iff |\mathcal L(\pi)|=1\).

notation.meaning: set of valid liftings of the base function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but uniqueness in the established lifting literature commonly concerns a specified class such as minimal liftings. Defining the set as all validity-preserving coefficient functions can change or trivialize the uniqueness question. The intended convention and exact mixed-group model require a supporting source.

children.title: Nonunique Lifting Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings admitting multiple valid liftings.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Lifting Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity of valid integer-variable coefficient functions for a fixed base function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the mixed group relaxation, let \(\mathcal L(\pi)\) denote the set of lifting functions associated with a fixed continuous-variable valid function \(\pi\). The lifting regime is nonunique if there exist \(\psi_1,\psi_2\in\mathcal L(\pi)\) with \(\psi_1\ne\psi_2\); equivalently, there is some group element \(r\) for which \(\psi_1(r)\ne\psi_2(r)\). If only minimal liftings are under consideration, \(\mathcal L(\pi)\) is replaced throughout by its subset of pointwise-minimal valid liftings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifting is nonunique when two distinct valid coefficient functions extend the same base valid function; the convention may be restricted to minimal liftings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\) has nonunique lifting \(\iff\exists\psi_1,\psi_2\in\mathcal L(\pi):\psi_1\ne\psi_2.\)

notation.meaning: chosen class of valid liftings of pi

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, and distinct functions differ at some group element. However, the statement alternates between all valid liftings and pointwise-minimal liftings instead of fixing one mathematical class. A source is needed to determine the intended convention and formulate the terminal statement unambiguously.

children.title: Lifting Multiplicity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural transitions between unique and nonunique lifting behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifting Multiplicity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Envelope criterion separating unique from nonunique lifting for a nonempty lifting class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\mathcal L(\pi)\ne\varnothing\), and define pointwise envelopes \(\psi^-(r)=\inf_{\psi\in\mathcal L(\pi)}\psi(r)\) and \(\psi^+(r)=\sup_{\psi\in\mathcal L(\pi)}\psi(r)\). The lifting is unique if and only if \(\psi^-(r)=\psi^+(r)\) for every group element \(r\). It is nonunique if and only if there exists \(r\) with \(\psi^-(r)<\psi^+(r)\). Thus the multiplicity boundary is coordinatewise collapse versus positive width of the lifting envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unique lifting occurs exactly when the lower and upper coefficient envelopes coincide everywhere; any coordinate with positive envelope width certifies nonuniqueness.
assumptions_latex: The pointwise infima and suprema are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal L(\pi)|=1\iff\forall r,\ \psi^-(r)=\psi^+(r).\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the boundary leaf, and for a nonempty class of real-valued functions, coordinatewise equality of the infimum and supremum envelopes is equivalent to singleton membership. The result still depends on which lifting class is used, and neither that convention nor this envelope formulation has a supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covers, minimal covers, and cover inequalities for a 0–1 knapsack set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines covers and minimal covers, states cover-inequality validity, and records the dimension loss caused by items that individually exceed capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(b>0\), \(a_j>0\) for all \(j\in N\), and \(K:=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{j=1}^n a_jx_j\le b\}\). With \(J:=\{j\in N:a_j>b\}\), one has \(\dim(\operatorname{conv}(K))=n-|J|\). Thus, if \(a_j\le b\) for every \(j\in N\), then \(\operatorname{conv}(K)\) is full-dimensional. A subset \(C\subseteq N\) is a cover if \(\sum_{j\in C}a_j>b\), and it is minimal if \(\sum_{j\in C\setminus\{k\}}a_j\le b\) for every \(k\in C\). For every cover \(C\), the inequality \(\sum_{j\in C}x_j\le |C|-1\) is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a binary knapsack set with positive capacity and weights, the convex hull loses one dimension for each item that cannot fit by itself and is full-dimensional if every item fits individually. A cover has total weight exceeding capacity; it is minimal when removing any one item makes it feasible. Every cover permits at most |C|−1 of its items to be selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim(\operatorname{conv}(K))=n-|\{j\in N:a_j>b\}|,\qquad C\text{ a cover}\Longrightarrow \sum_{j\in C}x_j\le |C|-1\text{ is valid for }\operatorname{conv}(K).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cover and minimal cover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines covers and inclusion-minimal covers for a 0-1 knapsack constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq N\). The set \(C\) is a cover if \(\sum_{j\in C}a_j>b\). It is a minimal cover if it is a cover and \(C\setminus\{j\}\) is not a cover for every \(j\in C\); equivalently, \[\sum_{j\in C}a_j>b\quad\text{and}\quad \sum_{i\in C\setminus\{j\}}a_i\le b\quad\text{for every }j\in C.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cover is an item set whose total weight exceeds capacity. It is minimal when it is a cover but deleting any one item makes the remaining set fit within capacity.

children.title: Minimal Cover Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Cover cuts based on inclusion-minimal infeasible item sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Cover Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary single-row knapsack covers that are inclusion-minimal among infeasible item sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\}\), where \(a_i>0\). A set \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a cover if \(\sum_{i\in C}a_i>b\), and it is minimal if \(\sum_{i\in C\setminus\{j\}}a_i\le b\) for every \(j\in C\). Every feasible \(x\in X\) then satisfies the minimal cover inequality \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inclusion-minimal overweight item set defines a valid inequality forbidding selection of all its items simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\) for every \(x\in X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, and the binary-knapsack minimal-cover definition and resulting inequality are mathematically standard and internally precise. The supplied inventory contains no locator addressing cover inequalities, and the record itself cites no source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covers, Minimal Covers, and the Complete Minimal-Cover System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines covers and minimal covers for a positive-weight binary knapsack set and the binary set satisfying every minimal-cover inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b>0\), let \(a_i>0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), and define \(K:=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\}\). A set \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a cover for \(K\) if \(\sum_{i\in C}a_i>b\). It is a minimal cover if, additionally, \(\sum_{i\in C\setminus\{j\}}a_i\le b\) for every \(j\in C\). Define \(K^C:=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\text{ for every minimal cover }C\text{ of }K\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a binary knapsack set with positive capacity and weights, a cover has total weight exceeding capacity. It is minimal if deleting any one item makes its weight no greater than capacity. The set K^C contains the binary vectors satisfying the inequality associated with every minimal cover.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\text{ is a minimal cover}\iff \sum_{i\in C}a_i>b\ \text{ and }\ \sum_{i\in C\setminus\{j\}}a_i\le b\ \forall j\in C,\qquad K^C=\left\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\ \forall C\text{ minimal}\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal Cover and Decomposition of Nonminimal Cover Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimal dependent sets and the derivation of inequalities for nonminimal dependent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dependent set \(C\subseteq N\) is minimal if every proper subset of \(C\) is independent. If \(C\) is not minimal and \(C'\subset C\) is a minimal dependent set, then its inequality is obtained by adding the cover inequality for \(C'\) and the upper bounds for the remaining variables: \[\left(\sum_{j\in C'}x_j\le |C'|-1\right)+\sum_{j\in C\setminus C'}(x_j\le1)\;\Longrightarrow\;\sum_{j\in C}x_j\le |C|-1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal cover is a dependent item set whose proper subsets are all feasible. The inequality of a nonminimal dependent set follows from a contained minimal cover inequality and the upper bounds on the remaining variables.
assumptions_latex: C'\subset C\text{ is a minimal dependent set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\sum_{j\in C'}x_j\le |C'|-1\right)+\sum_{j\in C\setminus C'}(x_j\le1)\;\Longrightarrow\;\sum_{j\in C}x_j\le |C|-1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Facet criterion for a cover inequality on the cover-restricted knapsack polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes facet-defining cover inequalities after all variables outside the cover are fixed to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(b>0\), \(0<a_j\le b\) for every \(j\in N\), and \(K:=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{j=1}^n a_jx_j\le b\}\). Let \(C\subseteq N\) be a cover and define \(P_C:=\operatorname{conv}(K)\cap\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x_j=0\text{ for every }j\in N\setminus C\}\). Then \(\sum_{j\in C}x_j\le |C|-1\) is facet-defining for \(P_C\) if and only if \(C\) is a minimal cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assume every item has positive weight and can fit individually. For a cover C, fix all variables outside C to zero. Its cover inequality defines a facet of the resulting restricted knapsack polytope exactly when removing any one item from C makes the remaining set feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j\in C}x_j\le |C|-1\text{ is facet-defining for }P_C\iff \sum_{j\in C\setminus\{k\}}a_j\le b\quad\text{for every }k\in C.

children.title: Lifted Cover Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Cover inequalities strengthened by lifting variables outside a base cover.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Cover Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid strengthening obtained by assigning coefficients to variables outside a base cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a cover for the binary knapsack set \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i a_i x_i\le b\}\). A lifted cover inequality has the form \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{j\notin C}\alpha_jx_j\le |C|-1\), where the lifting coefficients \(\alpha_j\ge0\) are chosen so that the inequality holds for every \(x\in X\). It dominates the unlifted cover inequality whenever at least one coefficient \(\alpha_j\) is positive and the corresponding variable can occur in a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted cover inequality strengthens a base cover cut with valid nonnegative coefficients on variables outside the cover.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a cover for the binary knapsack set \(X\).
\(\alpha_j\ge0\) and the displayed inequality is valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{j\notin C}\alpha_jx_j\le |C|-1\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: lifting coefficient for an item outside the cover

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, and the displayed form is a validity-based description of a lifted cover inequality. However, merely requiring that a positive-coefficient variable occur in some feasible point does not establish strict dominance or strict strengthening relative to the base inequality. The lifting convention, coefficient construction, and dominance claim require a specific source.

children.title: Extended Cover Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Cover inequalities enlarged through dominance and coefficient structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Cover Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard coefficient-dominance extension of a minimal binary knapsack cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i a_i x_i\le b\}\) with \(a_i>0\), and let \(C\) be a minimal cover. Define \(E=C\cup\{j\notin C:a_j\ge\max_{i\in C}a_i\}\). Then every feasible point satisfies the extended cover inequality \(\sum_{j\in E}x_j\le |C|-1\). Indeed, the coefficient condition ensures that any selection of \(|C|\) members of \(E\) has total weight at least that of some \(|C|\)-member replacement of \(C\), and is therefore infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Items at least as heavy as the heaviest member of a minimal cover can be added to its cover inequality with unit coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j\in E}x_j\le |C|-1\) for every \(x\in X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the leaf, and the displayed coefficient-dominance extension is mathematically plausible for the stated binary knapsack model. The sentence beginning with “Indeed” is proof text, which is prohibited, and no source identifies this exact extended-cover variant or supplies an inspectable locator. The authoritative formulation must be established before revision.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity of the extended cover inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends a knapsack cover by including items at least as heavy as every item in the cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{j=1}^n a_jx_j\le b\}\), and let \(C\subseteq N\) be a cover. Define \[E(C)=C\cup\{j\in N:a_j\ge a_i\text{ for every }i\in C\}.\] Then \[\sum_{j\in E(C)}x_j\le |C|-1\] is valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cover can be extended by including every item whose weight is at least every cover-item weight. At most one fewer than the original cover size can be selected from the extended set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j\in E(C)}x_j\le |C|-1\quad\forall x\in X

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Conditions for an Extended Cover Facet
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four sufficient regimes under which an extended cover inequality defines a facet of the 0-1 knapsack polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{j_1,\ldots,j_r\}\) be a minimal dependent set with \(j_1<\cdots<j_r\), and let \(E(C)\) be its extension. The inequality \(\sum_{j\in E(C)}x_j\le |C|-1\) defines a facet of \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\) if any one of the following holds: (a) \(C=N\); (b) \(E(C)=N\) and \((C\setminus\{j_1,j_2\})\cup\{1\}\) is independent; (c) \(C=E(C)\), \(N\setminus E(C)\ne\varnothing\), and \((C\setminus\{j_1\})\cup\{p\}\) is independent, where \(p=\min\{j:j\in N\setminus E(C)\}\); or (d) \(C\subset E(C)\subset N\) and both independence conditions from (b) and (c) hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extended cover inequality is facet-defining under any of four stated sufficient regimes involving whether the cover or its extension equals the full item set and whether specified replacement sets are feasible.
assumptions_latex: C=\{j_1,\ldots,j_r\}\text{ is a minimal dependent set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [(a)\lor(b)\lor(c)\lor(d)]\Longrightarrow\left[\sum_{j\in E(C)}x_j\le |C|-1\text{ defines a facet of }\operatorname{conv}(S)\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extended Cover and Associated Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold extension of a minimal cover using the largest coefficient in that cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{i_1,\ldots,i_r\}\) be a minimal cover, choose \(i_j\in C\) such that \(a_{i_j}=\max_{i\in C}a_i\), and set \(E=\{k\notin C:a_k\ge a_{i_j}\}\). Then \(C^+=C\cup E\) is the associated extended cover, with constraint \(\sum_{i\in C^+}\delta_i\le r-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a minimal cover, add every outside index whose coefficient is at least the largest coefficient in the cover. The associated constraint bounds the sum of the corresponding variables by one less than the size of the original minimal cover.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C^+=C\cup E\text{ is an extended cover and }\sum_{i\in C^+}\delta_i\le r-1

children.title: Configuration Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Knapsack inequalities based on structured configurations beyond covers.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The standard \((1,k)\)-configuration inequality for a binary packing knapsack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\}\), where \(a_i>0\). Let \(N\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), choose \(t\in N\), and let \(1\le k<|N|\). If every set \(Q\subseteq N\setminus\{t\}\) with \(|Q|=k\) makes \(Q\cup\{t\}\) a cover, then every \(x\in K\) satisfies
\[
(|N|-k)x_t+\sum_{i\in N\setminus\{t\}}x_i\le |N|-1.
\]
If each such cover is minimal, \((N,t,k)\) is called a minimal \((1,k)\)-configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every k-element subset of the nondistinguished items forms a cover together with the distinguished item, the stated configuration inequality is valid.
assumptions_latex: Every \(k\)-subset of \(N\setminus\{t\}\), together with \(t\), exceeds capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((|N|-k)x_t+\sum_{i\in N\setminus\{t\}}x_i\le |N|-1\) is valid for \(K\).

children.title: Pack Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Knapsack inequalities derived from feasible item packs.

knowledge_statements.title: Pack Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic pack inequality for a binary covering knapsack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K^{\ge}=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\ge b\}\), with \(a_i>0\). A set \(P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a pack when \(a(P):=\sum_{i\in P}a_i<b\). Since selecting only items from \(P\) cannot attain the covering requirement, the associated pack inequality is
\[
\sum_{j\notin P}x_j\ge 1.
\]
It is valid for every point of \(K^{\ge}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any feasible covering-knapsack solution must select at least one item outside a set whose total weight is below the requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j\notin P}x_j\ge1\) is valid for \(K^{\ge}\).

children.title: Weight Inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Weight Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-weight strengthening of a pack inequality for a covering knapsack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(K^{\ge}=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i a_i x_i\ge b\}\), let \(P\) be a pack and define its deficit by \(r=b-a(P)>0\). The weight inequality associated with \(P\) is
\[
\sum_{j\notin P}\min\{a_j,r\}x_j\ge r.
\]
This inequality is valid for \(K^{\ge}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outside-item weights, truncated at the pack's deficit, must collectively cover that deficit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j\notin P}\min\{a_j,r\}x_j\ge r\) is valid for \(K^{\ge}\).

notation.meaning: residual weight required beyond the pack

children.title: Pack–Weight Strength Relations

knowledge_statements.title: Pack–Weight Strength Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance relation for the covering-knapsack pack and residual-weight inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be a pack with deficit \(r=b-a(P)>0\). The weight inequality
\[
\sum_{j\notin P}\min\{a_j,r\}x_j\ge r
\]
implies the pack inequality \(\sum_{j\notin P}x_j\ge1\). Thus the weight inequality dominates the pack inequality on \([0,1]^n\). The dominance can be strict whenever some \(j\notin P\) satisfies \(a_j<r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual-weight inequality always implies its pack inequality and may exclude additional fractional points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weight inequality dominates \(\sum_{j\notin P}x_j\ge1\) on \([0,1]^n\).

children.title: Knapsack-Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Exact, dynamic-programming, and heuristic separation regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Knapsack-Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation of unlifted cover inequalities for a binary packing knapsack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\bar x\in[0,1]^n\) and \(K=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:a^Tx\le b\}\), solve
\[
z^*=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n(1-\bar x_i)z_i:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i z_i>b,\ z\in\{0,1\}^n\right\},
\]
with \(z^*=+\infty\) when the feasible set is empty. If \(z^*<1\), output an optimizer \(z^*_{\mathrm{vec}}\), set \(C=\{i:(z^*_{\mathrm{vec}})_i=1\}\), and return the violated cover inequality \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\). Otherwise no unlifted cover inequality is violated. Enumeration is exact, integer-weight dynamic programming is pseudo-polynomial, and restricted candidate searches are heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate cover cuts by finding a minimum-cost subset whose weight exceeds capacity; an optimum below one identifies a violated cut, while infeasibility or an optimum of at least one certifies that none is violated.
assumptions_latex: For dynamic programming, \(a_i\) and \(b\) are nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^*<1\) holds exactly when an unlifted cover inequality is violated by \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: incidence vector of a candidate cover

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Node Flow-Cover Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical flow-cover inequality for one capacitated fixed-charge balance row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
X=\left\{(x,y):x\in\{0,1\}^n,\ 0\le y_i\le u_i x_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^n y_i\le b\right\},
\]
where \(u_i>0\). If \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a flow cover with \(\sum_{i\in C}u_i=b+\lambda\) and \(\lambda>0\), then
\[
\sum_{i\in C}y_i+\sum_{i\in C}(u_i-\lambda)^+(1-x_i)\le b
\]
is valid for \(X\), where \((q)^+=\max\{q,0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A capacity cover yields a valid inequality coupling used flow with penalties for closed arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in C}y_i+\sum_{i\in C}(u_i-\lambda)^+(1-x_i)\le b\) is valid for \(X\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Flow-Cover Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential lifting of variables omitted from a base flow-cover inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a nonempty compact mixed-binary single-node flow set and let \(g(x,y)\le\delta\) be a flow-cover inequality valid on the face where variables in \(L\) equal zero. Choose an order \(j_1,\ldots,j_m\) of \(L\) such that every coefficient subproblem below has a nonempty feasible set. After coefficients \(\gamma_{j_1},\ldots,\gamma_{j_{r-1}}\) have been fixed, set
\[
\gamma_{j_r}=\delta-\max\left\{g(x,y)+\sum_{s<r}\gamma_{j_s}x_{j_s}:(x,y)\in X,\ x_{j_r}=1,\ x_{j_s}=0\ \text{for all }s>r\right\}.
\]
The final inequality \(g(x,y)+\sum_{j\in L}\gamma_jx_j\le\delta\) is valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential lifting extends a face-valid flow-cover cut by solving one well-defined coefficient optimization problem for each omitted binary variable.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and compact, and its lifted variables are binary.
\(g(x,y)\le\delta\) is valid when every variable in \(L\) is zero.
Every lifting-coefficient subproblem has a nonempty feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x,y)+\sum_{j\in L}\gamma_jx_j\le\delta\) is valid for \(X\).

notation.meaning: set of binary variables to lift
left side of the base flow-cover inequality

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Flow-Cover Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flow-cover construction after complementing bounded reverse-flow variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a bounded mixed-binary row
\[
\sum_{i\in I^+}y_i-
\sum_{j\in I^-}y_j\le b,
\qquad 0\le y_k\le u_kx_k.
\]
For each \(j\in I^-\), introduce the complementary flow \(s_j=u_jx_j-y_j\). Substitution produces
\[
\sum_{i\in I^+}y_i+
\sum_{j\in I^-}s_j\le b+
\sum_{j\in I^-}u_jx_j.
\]
Any flow-cover inequality valid for the transformed mixed-binary set, including lifted inequalities accounting for the binary terms on the right, pulls back under \(s_j=u_jx_j-y_j\) to a generalized flow-cover inequality valid for the original set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementing reverse-flow variables converts a signed balance row into a form from which generalized flow-cover cuts can be pulled back.
assumptions_latex: All reverse-flow variables are complemented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inverse substitution \(s_j=u_jx_j-y_j\) preserves validity of every transformed flow-cover inequality.

children.title: Flow-Cover Extension Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Flow-Cover Extension Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the canonical cut without on-off flow-capacity linking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The on-off bounds are essential. Consider the relaxed set
\[
R=\{(x,y):x\in\{0,1\},\ 0\le y\le2,\ y\le1\},
\]
which omits \(y\le2x\). Taking \(u=2\), \(b=1\), and the cover \(C=\{1\}\) gives \(\lambda=1\). The formal flow-cover expression would assert \(y+(2-1)(1-x)\le1\). Yet \((x,y)=(0,1)\in R\) has left side \(2\), so the inequality is invalid. Generalized or lifted formulas therefore require the linking structure used in their derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without on-off capacity links, even the one-variable flow-cover formula can cut off a feasible point.
assumptions_latex: The constraint \(y\le ux\) is removed while \(0\le y\le u\) remains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical flow-cover inequality need not be valid after removing on-off linking bounds.

notation.meaning: relaxed set lacking the on-off link

children.title: Flow-Cover Separation
children.top_down_role: Exact and heuristic recognition of violated flow-cover inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Flow-Cover Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact separation and incomplete heuristic search for canonical flow-cover cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \((\bar x,\bar y)\), capacities \(u_i>0\), and a threshold \(b>0\), enumerate every \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) satisfying \(u(C)>b\). For each such set define \(\lambda_C=u(C)-b\) and
\[
v(C)=\sum_{i\in C}\bar y_i+
\sum_{i\in C}(u_i-\lambda_C)^+(1-\bar x_i)-b.
\]
If no such set exists, define the maximum violation to be \(-\infty\). Otherwise, return a maximizer \(C^*\) when \(v(C^*)>0\). If the maximum is nonpositive, no canonical flow-cover inequality is violated. Dynamic programming may replace enumeration for suitable integral data. Restricting candidate covers or greedily modifying them is heuristic and cannot certify nonexistence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact separation maximizes flow-cover violation over all capacity covers, with an empty cover family certifying that no cut exists; restricted or greedy searches cannot certify absence.
assumptions_latex: The searched family is the canonical unlifted flow-cover family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A violated canonical flow-cover cut exists exactly when \(\max_{C:u(C)>b}v(C)>0\), using the value \(-\infty\) for an empty index family.

notation.meaning: total capacity of candidate cover C
violation of the cut indexed by C

knowledge_statements.title: Flow-Pack Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic flow-pack inequality for a single-node fixed-charge covering row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
Y=\left\{(x,y):x\in\{0,1\}^n,\ 0\le y_i\le u_ix_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^ny_i\ge b\right\}.
\]
If \(P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a flow pack with \(u(P):=\sum_{i\in P}u_i<b\), then every \((x,y)\in Y\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{j\notin P}y_j-
\sum_{i\in P}u_i(1-x_i)\ge b-u(P).
\]
The inequality records both the residual flow required outside \(P\) and the additional deficit caused by closing members of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A capacity-insufficient pack forces residual flow outside the pack, with extra demand when packed arcs are closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j\notin P}y_j-\sum_{i\in P}u_i(1-x_i)\ge b-u(P)\) is valid for \(Y\).

children.title: Residual-Capacity Cuts
children.top_down_role: Capacity inequalities based on residual demand or residual capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Capacity Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-capacity inequality for a fixed-charge capacity-covering row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
Z=\left\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n u_ix_i\ge d\right\},
\]
where \(u_i>0\). For any \(F\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(u(F)<d\), define the residual requirement \(r=d-u(F)>0\). Then
\[
\sum_{j\notin F}\min\{u_j,r\}x_j\ge r
\]
is valid for \(Z\). In a capacitated network-design model, the same inequality applies to the activation variables of arcs crossing a cut whenever that cut must carry demand \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After fixing a capacity-insufficient subset, truncated capacities of remaining activated facilities or arcs must cover the residual requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j\notin F}\min\{u_j,r\}x_j\ge r\) is valid for \(Z\).

children.title: Fixed-Charge Network Cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Charge Network Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally defines cuts exploiting network balance and binary arc-activation structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a directed network and let \(F\) contain every \((x,y)\) satisfying flow balance, \(0\le x_a\le u_a y_a\), and \(y_a\in\{0,1\}\) for each \(a\in A\). A fixed-charge network cut is a linear inequality \(\alpha^\top x+\beta^\top y\le\gamma\) valid for \(F\) whose validity uses both the network balance equations and at least one activation implication \(y_a=0\Rightarrow x_a=0\). It is a proper cutting inequality for a relaxation \(R\supseteq F\) when some point of \(R\) violates it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-charge network cut is valid for activated network flows, exploits both flow balance and arc activation, and removes a point from the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq\{(x,y):\alpha^\top x+\beta^\top y\le\gamma\}\).

notation.meaning: binary activation variable for arc a

Available network-structure locator does not specifically identify fixed-charge network cuts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary and conditionally sufficient flow-cover violation condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preserves the one-way necessity and the additional saturation hypothesis required for sufficiency; symbols refer to source-defined (4.9) and (4.10).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Violation of an inequality of the source-defined form \((4.9)\) necessarily implies
\[
\xi>\sum_{j\in N^-}x_j^*-1.
\]
If, additionally, \(C^+\) is determined by an optimal solution of \((4.10)\) and
\[
y_j^*=a_jx_j^*\qquad(j\in C^+),
\]
then the displayed strict inequality is sufficient for violation of \((4.9)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Violation requires xi to exceed the sum of the negative-side activation values minus one. This condition becomes sufficient only when the positive set comes from an optimal solution of the associated problem and every corresponding flow is at its activation-scaled value.
assumptions_latex: \text{For sufficiency, }C^+\text{ is determined by an optimal solution to }(4.10)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{violated}(4.9)\Rightarrow \xi>\sum_{j\in N^-}x_j^*-1,\qquad \left[\xi>\sum_{j\in N^-}x_j^*-1\ \land\ \forall j\in C^+,\ y_j^*=a_jx_j^*\right]\Rightarrow\operatorname{violated}(4.9).

children.title: On-Off Capacity Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts coupling binary activation with continuous capacity usage.

knowledge_statements.title: On-Off Capacity Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull representation of one nonnegative capacity controlled by a binary variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(u\ge0\), consider the disjunction \(S=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,1):0\le x\le u\}\). Its convex hull is
\[\operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R\times[0,1]:0\le x\le uy\}.\]
Thus the on-off capacity inequality \(x\le uy\), together with \(x\ge0\) and \(0\le y\le1\), exactly describes the continuous convexification of a single activated capacity. In a larger relaxation, the same inequality is a valid cut whenever \(y=0\Rightarrow x=0\) and \(y=1\Rightarrow x\le u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inequality x ≤ uy is the exact convex-hull description of one nonnegative capacity that is zero when its binary controller is off.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,y):0\le y\le1,\ 0\le x\le uy\}\).
review_flags: Standard disjunctive convexification, but no supplied locator specifically supports the on-off capacity formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The single-variable convex-hull representation is mathematically standard and the representation content kind fits the exact convexification claim, but no inspectable source locator was supplied for the on-off capacity formulation.

children.title: Single Mixing-Set Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts for an individual mixing structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Single Mixing-Set Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical mixing inequalities for one continuous mixing variable and ordered binary controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(0=h_0\le h_1\le\cdots\le h_n\) and
\[M=\{(s,z)\in\mathbb R_+\times\{0,1\}^n:s+h_i z_i\ge h_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,n\}.\]
For every index sequence \(1\le i_1<\cdots<i_k\le n\), with \(i_0=0\), the mixing inequality
\[s+\sum_{t=1}^k(h_{i_t}-h_{i_{t-1}})z_{i_t}\ge h_{i_k}\]
is valid for \(M\). Hence it is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(M)\) and may cut fractional points satisfying only the individual inequalities \(s+h_i z_i\ge h_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any ordered subsequence of mixing thresholds, successive threshold differences give a valid inequality coupling the common continuous variable with its binary controls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s+\sum_{t=1}^k(h_{i_t}-h_{i_{t-1}})z_{i_t}\ge h_{i_k}\) is valid for \(M\).

children.title: Coupled Mixing-Cut Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cuts coupling multiple mixing rows or shared binary controls.

children.title: Joint Mixing Cuts
children.top_down_role: Mixing cuts coupling constraints through shared binary controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Mixing Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cuts derived from the convex hull of several mixing systems considered jointly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For rows \(r=1,\ldots,m\), let
\[M^{r}=\{(s_r,z):s_r\ge0,\ z\in\{0,1\}^n,\ s_r+h_{ri}z_i\ge h_{ri}\text{ for all }i\}.\]
Define the joint mixing set \(J=\{(s,z):(s_r,z)\in M^r\text{ for every }r\}\). A joint mixing cut is a linear inequality \(\alpha^\top s+\beta^\top z\ge\delta\) valid for \(J\) that uses coefficients from at least two rows. It is genuinely joint when it is not implied by the intersection of the separate row convex hulls \(\bigcap_r\{(s,z):(s_r,z)\in\operatorname{conv}(M^r)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint mixing cut couples at least two mixing rows sharing binary controls and strengthens the intersection of their separately convexified row sets.
assumptions_latex: The same binary vector \(z\) controls every row.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J\subseteq\{(s,z):\alpha^\top s+\beta^\top z\ge\delta\}\).

notation.meaning: mixing set associated with row r

review_flags: A source distinguishing joint mixing cuts from general multirow mixing cuts is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally meaningful, but no source establishes that coefficient support across two rows and nonimplication by separate row convex hulls are the canonical criteria for the specifically named joint mixing-cut family. The distinction from the sibling multirow family therefore remains unreliable.

children.title: Multirow Mixing Cuts
children.top_down_role: Mixing cuts derived from several rows simultaneously.

knowledge_statements.title: Multirow Mixing Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid inequalities for simultaneous convexification of multiple mixing rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[J=\{(s,z)\in\mathbb R_+^m\times\{0,1\}^n:s_r+h_{ri}z_i\ge h_{ri}\text{ for every }r,i\}.\]
A multirow mixing cut is any linear inequality \(\alpha^\top s+\beta^\top z\ge\delta\) valid for \(J\) whose support contains at least two components of \(s\). Such a cut strengthens rowwise mixing when it is not implied by applying all valid single-row mixing inequalities separately. Separation at a fractional point \((\bar s,\bar z)\) seeks coefficients satisfying validity on \(J\) and \(\alpha^\top\bar s+\beta^\top\bar z<\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multirow mixing cut is valid for several mixing rows simultaneously, contains at least two row variables, and can be stronger than separate single-row cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J\subseteq\{(s,z):\alpha^\top s+\beta^\top z\ge\delta\}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports a canonical multirow mixing-cut formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity condition is coherent, and definition is a plausible content kind, but the support-based characterization of a multirow mixing cut and its distinction from joint mixing cuts require a specific authoritative source.

children.title: Shared-Control Multirow Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes combining shared binary controls with multiple mixing rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Control Multirow Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural condition under which multiple mixing rows share activation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A family of mixing rows is in a shared-control multirow regime when its feasible set can be written
\[J=\{(s,z)\in\mathbb R_+^m\times\{0,1\}^n:s_r\ge h_{ri}(1-z_i)\text{ for every }r,i\},\]
so that each controller \(z_i\) appears in at least two distinct rows. Equivalently, for some \(i\) there exist \(r\ne q\) with \(h_{ri}>0\) and \(h_{qi}>0\). This shared incidence permits inequalities coupling \(s_r\) and \(s_q\); without shared controllers, the corresponding row blocks decompose and joint convexification supplies no cross-block coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regime occurs when one binary controller affects at least two mixing rows, creating a common discrete structure through which joint cuts can couple row variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists i,\exists r\ne q:\ h_{ri}>0\text{ and }h_{qi}>0\).

notation.meaning: threshold induced by controller i in row r

review_flags: Terminology and the claimed decomposition boundary require a dedicated multirow mixing reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement first requires every controller to appear in at least two rows but then calls this equivalent to the existence of one such controller; these quantifiers are not equivalent. The asserted no-coupling decomposition boundary also requires a dedicated source, so the intended corrected condition cannot be selected reliably.

children.title: Implied-Bound Cut Family
children.top_down_role: Cuts derived from bounds implied by discrete decisions and model rows.

children.title: Variable-Upper-Bound Cuts
children.top_down_role: Implied-bound cuts based on upper-bound implications.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Upper-Bound Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implied-bound inequalities linking a bounded variable to a discrete controller.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a mixed-integer feasible set containing a variable \(x\) and a binary variable \(y\). A variable-upper-bound implication is
\[y=0\Rightarrow x\le U_0,\qquad y=1\Rightarrow x\le U_1.\]
Its linear convex-hull inequality is
\[x\le U_0+(U_1-U_0)y.\]
This inequality is a variable-upper-bound cut for a relaxation \(R\supseteq X\) when the implication holds throughout \(X\) but the displayed inequality is absent from, or violated in, \(R\). The common on-off form is obtained from \(U_0=0\) and \(U_1=U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two upper bounds selected by a binary variable convexify to one affine variable-upper-bound inequality, which cuts a relaxation whenever the underlying implication is valid but unenforced.
assumptions_latex: \(U_0,U_1\in\mathbb R\) are valid conditional upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\subseteq\{(x,y):x\le U_0+(U_1-U_0)y\}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically documents variable-upper-bound cuts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine interpolation is valid under the two conditional upper bounds, but calling it the convex-hull inequality for an arbitrary mixed-integer set X is too broad without specifying the underlying two-branch set or projection. A variable-upper-bound source is needed to fix the canonical scope and terminology.

children.title: Variable-Lower-Bound Cuts
children.top_down_role: Implied-bound cuts based on lower-bound implications.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Lower-Bound Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implied-bound inequalities linking a variable’s lower bound to a discrete controller.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a mixed-integer feasible set containing a variable \(x\) and a binary variable \(y\). A variable-lower-bound implication is
\[y=0\Rightarrow x\ge L_0,\qquad y=1\Rightarrow x\ge L_1.\]
Its linear convex-hull inequality is
\[x\ge L_0+(L_1-L_0)y.\]
This inequality is a variable-lower-bound cut for a relaxation \(R\supseteq X\) when both conditional bounds hold on \(X\) and a point of \(R\) violates the displayed inequality. The activated lower-bound form \(x\ge Ly\) follows by taking \(L_0=0\) and \(L_1=L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two lower bounds selected by a binary variable convexify to one affine variable-lower-bound inequality, valid for the integer set and potentially violated by its relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(L_0,L_1\in\mathbb R\) are valid conditional lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\subseteq\{(x,y):x\ge L_0+(L_1-L_0)y\}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically documents variable-lower-bound cuts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine interpolation is valid under the two conditional lower bounds, but the claimed convex-hull status is not established for an arbitrary mixed-integer set X. A specific variable-lower-bound reference is needed to determine the intended disjunctive set and canonical cut definition.

children.title: Implied-Bound MIR Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Use of implied bounds within MIR derivation and strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Implied-Bound MIR Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Substitution of implied-bound slacks before mixed-integer rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a valid mixed-integer row containing \(x\), a binary controller \(y\), and a valid implied upper bound \(x\le U_0+(U_1-U_0)y\). Introduce the nonnegative slack
\[t=U_0+(U_1-U_0)y-x\ge0,\]
substitute \(x=U_0+(U_1-U_0)y-t\) into the row, and then apply the mixed-integer rounding rule using the declared integrality of \(y\) and nonnegativity of \(t\). Output the resulting MIR inequality in the original variables after eliminating \(t\). The output is valid because the substitution is valid for every mixed-integer feasible point satisfying the implied bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace a bounded variable by its implied-bound slack, apply MIR to the transformed row, and substitute back to obtain a bound-aware valid inequality.
assumptions_latex: The input row is valid for the mixed-integer feasible set.
\(y\in\{0,1\}\) and the implied upper bound is valid.
The selected MIR convention applies to the transformed row.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The transformed-and-substituted MIR inequality is valid for the original feasible set.}\)

notation.meaning: variable having an implied upper bound

review_flags: A precise source for implied-bound substitution within MIR derivation is required.
The exact MIR sign and normalization convention is intentionally left local to the input row.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate content kind for this procedural leaf, but the input row normalization and MIR convention are not specified, so the resulting inequality cannot be checked. A source giving the precise implied-bound substitution and MIR rule is required.

children.title: Implied-Bound Detection Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Presolve, propagation, and row-analysis sources of implied bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Implied-Bound Detection Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface for harvesting conditional bounds from presolve, propagation, and row analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a mixed-integer model and a set \(B\) of binary controllers, construct a repository of tuples \((x,y,L_0,L_1,U_0,U_1)\). For each \(y\in B\), obtain conditional bounds on \(x\) under \(y=0\) and \(y=1\) from presolve substitutions, domain propagation, or valid row activity calculations. Retain a tuple only after verifying
\[X\cap\{y=b\}\subseteq\{x:L_b\le x\le U_b\}\qquad(b\in\{0,1\}).\]
Return the certified tuples to cut generators; each tuple supplies affine variable-lower- and variable-upper-bound inequalities and may be used for bound-aware MIR substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Detection collects conditional bounds from presolve, propagation, or row activity, verifies each implication, and exposes certified tuples to implied-bound and MIR cut generators.
assumptions_latex: Every reported conditional bound is derived by a validity-preserving inference.
An unavailable lower or upper bound may be represented by an infinite endpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\cap\{y=b\}\subseteq[L_b,U_b]\text{ in the }x\text{-coordinate for }b=0,1\).

notation.meaning: certified conditional bounds when the controller equals b

review_flags: No supplied source locator covers solver interfaces for implied-bound detection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is a suitable content kind for the detection-interface leaf, and the retained-bound validity test is coherent. However, no cited solver or scholarly source supports the claimed presolve, propagation, and row-analysis interface or its handoff to cut generators.

children.title: Conflict-Graph Cut Families
children.top_down_role: Cuts derived from incompatibility structures among binary decisions.

children.title: Clique Cut Family
children.top_down_role: Cuts generated from mutually incompatible binary variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clique inequalities for stable-set and set-packing families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity characterization and dominance of nonmaximal clique inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G_A=(V,E) be the intersection graph of a 0,1 matrix A. For every Q\subseteq V, the inequality \sum_{j\in Q}x_j\leq1 is valid for S^P(A)=\operatorname{stab}(G_A) if and only if Q is a clique of G_A. Moreover, if K\subsetneq K' are cliques, then \sum_{j\in K}x_j\leq1 is implied by \sum_{j\in K'}x_j\leq1 together with x_j\geq0 for j\in K'\setminus K.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unit-right-hand-side subset inequality is valid for the stable-set family exactly when its support is a clique. An inequality for a nonmaximal clique is implied by that of a containing clique together with nonnegativity.
assumptions_latex: G_A\text{ is the intersection graph of }A
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j\in Q}x_j\leq1\text{ is valid for }\operatorname{stab}(G_A)\iff Q\text{ is a clique of }G_A.

children.title: Maximal-Clique Cuts
children.top_down_role: Clique cuts indexed by inclusion-maximal conflict cliques.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal-Clique Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique inequalities indexed by inclusion-maximal cliques of a binary conflict graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a conflict graph for binary variables \(x_v\), meaning that \(\{u,v\}\in E\) implies \(x_u+x_v\le1\) for every feasible binary point. If \(C\subseteq V\) is a clique, then
\[\sum_{v\in C}x_v\le1\]
is valid. If \(C\) is inclusion-maximal, no vertex outside \(C\) can be added with coefficient one while preserving the clique property. Every nonmaximal clique inequality is dominated on \(x\ge0\) by the inequality of any maximal clique containing it; maximality alone does not guarantee facetness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variables in a conflict clique cannot simultaneously equal one. A maximal clique yields an undominated clique extension, although its inequality need not define a facet.
assumptions_latex: Every edge of \(G\) represents a valid pairwise conflict.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{v\in C}x_v\le1\) is valid for every clique \(C\), and nonmaximal clique cuts are dominated by maximal extensions.

notation.meaning: binary variable associated with vertex v

children.title: Clique-Cut Extension Regimes
children.top_down_role: Strengthened clique inequalities beyond the base conflict support.

children.title: Lifted Clique Cuts
children.top_down_role: Clique inequalities strengthened by coefficients outside the base clique.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Clique Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential lifting of variables into a valid clique inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^V\) and let \(C\subseteq V\) satisfy \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le1\) on \(X\). Choose distinct variables \(j_1,\ldots,j_p\notin C\). Starting with \(L_0(x)=\sum_{i\in C}x_i\), define sequentially
\[\alpha_t=1-\max\{L_{t-1}(x):x\in X,\ x_{j_t}=1\},\qquad L_t(x)=L_{t-1}(x)+\alpha_t x_{j_t}.\]
Whenever each maximum is finite and its subproblem uses the previously lifted coefficients, \(L_p(x)\le1\) is valid for \(X\). The coefficients may depend on the lifting order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential lifting assigns each added binary variable the largest coefficient preserving validity of the current clique inequality; the final lifted inequality remains valid.
assumptions_latex: The initial clique inequality is valid for \(X\).
Each restricted lifting subproblem is feasible and has a finite maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{t=1}^p\alpha_t x_{j_t}\le1\) is valid for \(X\).

notation.meaning: inequality left-hand side after t liftings

children.title: Weighted Clique Cuts
children.top_down_role: Clique inequalities using nonuniform conflict weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Clique Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted validity for binary variables represented by a conflict graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{V}\), and let \(G=(V,E)\) satisfy \(x_i+x_j\le 1\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(ij\in E\). If \(Q\subseteq V\) is a clique and \(w_i\ge 0\) for \(i\in Q\), then every \(x\in X\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{i\in Q}w_i x_i\le \max_{i\in Q}w_i.
\]
Thus the displayed inequality is a weighted clique cut. For \(w_i=1\) for all \(i\in Q\), it reduces to the ordinary clique inequality \(\sum_{i\in Q}x_i\le 1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At most one variable in a conflict-graph clique can equal one, so its selected weight cannot exceed the largest clique weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in Q}w_i x_i\le\max_{i\in Q}w_i\) is valid for \(X\).

children.title: Lifted Weighted Clique Regimes
children.top_down_role: Clique-cut regimes combining lifting with weighted support.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Weighted Clique Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and sequential lifting conditions for extending a weighted clique inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{V}\), let \(Q,R\subseteq V\) be disjoint, and suppose \(\sum_{i\in Q}w_i x_i\le\beta\) is valid on \(\{x\in X:x_r=0\text{ for every }r\in R\}\). Coefficients \((\alpha_r)_{r\in R}\) define a valid lifted inequality exactly when
\[
\max_{x\in X}\left(\sum_{i\in Q}w_i x_i+\sum_{r\in R}\alpha_r x_r\right)\le\beta.
\]
For an ordering \(R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_k\}\), define
\[
M_t=\max\left\{\sum_{i\in Q}w_i x_i+\sum_{s<t}\alpha_{r_s}x_{r_s}:x\in X,\ x_{r_t}=1,\ x_{r_s}=0\text{ for }s>t\right\}.
\]
When each displayed subproblem is nonempty, sequential up-lifting sets \(\alpha_{r_t}=\beta-M_t\) for \(t=1,\ldots,k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted inequality is valid exactly when its maximum over the feasible set does not exceed the original bound. Sequential up-lifting computes each new coefficient from a subproblem in which the current variable equals one, previously lifted variables remain free, and variables scheduled for later lifting equal zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\sum_{i\in Q}w_i x_i\le\beta\) is valid when \(x_r=0\) for every \(r\in R\).
Each sequential lifting subproblem defining \(M_t\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficients \(\alpha_{r_t}=\beta-M_t\) yield the valid inequality \(\sum_{i\in Q}w_i x_i+\sum_{r\in R}\alpha_r x_r\le\beta\).

notation.meaning: restricted lifting-subproblem value at step t

children.title: Odd-Cycle Cuts
children.top_down_role: Conflict-graph inequalities derived from odd cycles.

knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Cycle Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable-set inequality induced by an odd cycle in a conflict graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{V}\), and let \(G=(V,E)\) be a conflict graph for \(X\). If \(C\) is a simple odd cycle with \(|C|=2k+1\), then any feasible support \(\{i:x_i=1\}\) contains at most \(k\) vertices of \(C\). Consequently,
\[
\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le k=\left\lfloor\frac{|C|}{2}\right\rfloor
\]
is valid for \(X\). The validity uses only the cycle edges; chords can strengthen the induced conflict structure but cannot invalidate this inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stable set contains at most half, rounded down, of the vertices of an odd conflict cycle.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a simple cycle of length \(2k+1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le k\) is valid for \(X\).

notation.meaning: vertex set of a simple odd cycle

knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Hole Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet statement for the stable-set polytope of an induced odd cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=(C,E_H)\) be a chordless cycle of odd length \(|C|=2k+1\ge5\), and let \(\operatorname{STAB}(H)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^S:S\subseteq C\text{ is stable in }H\}\). Then
\[
\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le k
\]
is valid and defines a facet of \(\operatorname{STAB}(H)\). When \(H\) occurs as an induced subgraph of a larger conflict graph, the same inequality remains valid for the larger stable-set model, although additional lifting or graph conditions are required to conclude that it defines a facet there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chordless odd cycle of length at least five, the odd-cycle inequality is facet-defining for that cycle’s stable-set polytope.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a chordless cycle on \(2k+1\ge5\) vertices.
\(\operatorname{STAB}(H)\) is the convex hull of incidence vectors of stable sets of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le k\) defines a facet of \(\operatorname{STAB}(H)\).

notation.meaning: odd hole, namely a chordless odd cycle
incidence vector of vertex set S

children.top_down_role: Effects of chords on the transition from odd cycles to odd holes.

knowledge_statements.title: Chord-Induced Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chords preserve an odd-cycle inequality's validity but may destroy its facet-defining or undominated status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a graph, let \(C\subseteq V\) be the vertex set of a simple odd cycle, and let \(\operatorname{STAB}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^S:S\subseteq V\text{ is stable in }G\}\). If edges with both endpoints in \(C\) are added to form \(G'\), then
\[
\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le\left\lfloor\frac{|C|}{2}\right\rfloor
\]
remains valid for \(\operatorname{STAB}(G')\), but it need not remain facet-defining or undominated. In particular, adding all five chords missing from a five-cycle produces \(K_5\); there the inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^{5}x_i\le2\) is dominated by the clique inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^{5}x_i\le1\) and is not facet-defining for \(\operatorname{STAB}(K_5)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding chords cannot invalidate the inequality associated with the original odd cycle, but it can make that inequality dominated and non-facet-defining; completing a five-cycle to a clique is a concrete example.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a graph and \(C\subseteq V\) is the vertex set of a simple odd cycle.
\(G'\) is obtained from \(G\) by adding edges whose endpoints both belong to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The odd-cycle inequality remains valid for \(\operatorname{STAB}(G')\), whereas facet-defining and undominated status need not be preserved.

notation.meaning: graph obtained by adding chords within the odd cycle

children.title: Conflict-Graph Separation

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Graph Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or heuristic detection of violated clique and odd-cycle inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a conflict graph \(G=(V,E)\), a fractional point \(\bar x\in[0,1]^V\), and a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). For clique cuts, solve or approximate the maximum-weight clique problem with vertex weights \(\bar x_i\); return \(Q\) when \(\sum_{i\in Q}\bar x_i>1+\varepsilon\). For odd-cycle cuts, search simple odd cycles \(C\) and return one satisfying
\[
\sum_{i\in C}\bar x_i>\left\lfloor |C|/2\right\rfloor+\varepsilon.
\]
An exact interface certifies absence of violations only after globally optimizing the relevant search problem; a heuristic interface may return a found violation but cannot certify nonexistence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation searches the conflict graph for a clique or odd cycle whose inequality is violated; only exact global search certifies that none exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a violated valid inequality, or, under exact optimization, a certificate that no inequality in the searched family is violated beyond \(\varepsilon\).

children.title: Network Connectivity Cut Interface
children.top_down_role: Interface to cutset, connectivity, and capacity inequalities owned by network chapters.

knowledge_statements.title: Network Connectivity Cut Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutset validity and minimum-cut separation for capacitated connectivity requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) be directed, let \(y_a\ge0\) denote installed capacity on arc \(a\), and require capacity \(k_{st}\ge0\) from \(s\) to \(t\). Every feasible design satisfies
\[
y(\delta^+(S)):=\sum_{a\in\delta^+(S)}y_a\ge k_{st}
\]
for every \(S\subset V\) with \(s\in S\) and \(t\notin S\). Given \(\bar y\), compute a minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cut using capacities \(\bar y_a\). If its value is below \(k_{st}\), return the associated cut inequality; otherwise all such \(s\)-\(t\) cutset inequalities are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connectivity and capacity requirements induce cutset inequalities, and a minimum-cut computation exactly separates them for each source-terminal pair.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible design supports \(k_{st}\) units of \(s\)-to-\(t\) flow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y(\delta^+(S))\ge k_{st}\) is valid and is separated by a minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cut.

knowledge_statements.title: Routing Cut Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subtour and rounded-capacity cut interfaces for undirected routing formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(\{r\}\cup N,E)\) be an undirected routing graph with depot \(r\), customers \(N\), demands \(d_i\ge0\), and vehicle capacity \(Q>0\). For a feasible collection of depot-rooted routes that serves every customer, respects capacity \(Q\), and has edge-traversal vector \(x\), every nonempty set \(S\subseteq N\) satisfies
\[
x(\delta(S))\ge2.
\]
Moreover, every such capacitated routing solution satisfies
\[
x(\delta(S))\ge2\left\lceil\frac{\sum_{i\in S}d_i}{Q}\right\rceil.
\]
The first family admits minimum-cut separation. Separation of the rounded-capacity family generally uses routing-specific exact or heuristic procedures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty customer set must have at least two route crossings to the rest of the graph, and vehicle capacity raises this lower bound to twice the number of vehicle loads required by the set's total demand.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(\{r\}\cup N,E)\) is undirected, with depot \(r\) and customer set \(N\).
Every customer is served by depot-rooted routes, and \(x_e\) counts aggregate traversals of edge \(e\).
Each route carries at most \(Q>0\), and customer demands satisfy \(d_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every nonempty \(S\subseteq N\), the subtour inequality \(x(\delta(S))\ge2\) and the rounded-capacity inequality \(x(\delta(S))\ge2\lceil\sum_{i\in S}d_i/Q\rceil\) are valid in their stated routing regimes.

notation.meaning: edges having exactly one endpoint in S

knowledge_statements.title: Other Structured-Polyhedra Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of application-specific valid inequalities through a formulation map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be an application-feasible set, let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a structured relaxation, and let \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be affine with \(\phi(F)\subseteq P\). If \(a^Ty\le b\) is valid for \(P\), then
\[
a^T\phi(x)\le b
\]
is valid for \(F\). Hence a separator for \(P\), applied to \(\phi(\bar x)\), supplies a valid cut in the original variables after affine substitution. Facetness transfers only under additional dimension and injectivity conditions and is not implied by validity alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid inequality from an application-specific polyhedron pulls back through an affine formulation map, though its facet status need not transfer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^T\phi(x)\le b\) is valid for \(F\).

children.title: Chvátal–Gomory Closure
children.top_down_role: Pure- and mixed-integer Chvátal–Gomory closures and their polyhedrality.

knowledge_statements.title: Chvátal–Gomory Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic pure- and mixed-integer Chvátal–Gomory closure for rational polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a rational polyhedron and let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index integer coordinates. Define
\[
P_{\mathrm{CG}}^I=\bigcap\left\{\left\{x\in P:a^Tx\le\lfloor\beta\rfloor\right\}:a^Tx\le\beta\text{ is valid for }P,\ a_i\in\mathbb Z\ (i\in I),\ a_j=0\ (j\notin I)\right\}.
\]
The rounding is valid because \(a^Tx\) is integral on \(\mathbb Z^I\times\mathbb R^{n-|I|}\). For \(I=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), this is the pure-integer Chvátal–Gomory closure. For rational \(P\), \(P_{\mathrm{CG}}^I\) is a rational polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The CG closure intersects all valid halfspaces obtained by rounding bounds whose left sides are integral on the designated mixed-integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathrm{CG}}^I\) is the displayed closure and is a rational polyhedron.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record makes nontrivial claims about the intrinsic mixed-integer CG operator and rational polyhedrality but supplies no source. A precise authoritative definition and polyhedrality locator are required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalized-multiplier representation of the Chvátal closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of the closure using componentwise-bounded aggregation multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\), \[P^{Ch}=\{x\in P:(uA)x\le\lfloor ub\rfloor\text{ for every }u\text{ such that }uA\in\mathbb Z^n\text{ and }0\le u\le1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Chvátal closure consists exactly of the points satisfying all aggregation-and-rounding inequalities generated by componentwise multipliers between zero and one whose aggregated normals are integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^{Ch}=\{x\in P:(uA)x\le\lfloor ub\rfloor\ \forall u\text{ with }uA\in\mathbb Z^n,\ 0\le u\le1\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Split Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive representation and polyhedrality of the split closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a rational polyhedron and let \(I\) index its integer coordinates. For \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^I\) and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\), extend \(\pi\) by zeros outside \(I\) and define
\[
P^{\pi,\pi_0}=\operatorname{conv}\left((P\cap\{\pi^Tx\le\pi_0\})\cup(P\cap\{\pi^Tx\ge\pi_0+1\})\right).
\]
The split closure is
\[
\operatorname{SC}(P)=\bigcap_{\pi\in\mathbb Z^I,\,\pi_0\in\mathbb Z}P^{\pi,\pi_0}.
\]
It contains every point of \(P\) satisfying the designated integrality restrictions, and for rational \(P\) it is a rational polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The split closure intersects the convexified two-term disjunctions obtained by excluding every open unit-width slab in the integer variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SC}(P)=\bigcap_{\pi,\pi_0}P^{\pi,\pi_0}\) is a rational polyhedron containing all mixed-integer points of \(P\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structure and strictness of single-split convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generator, recession, and strict-containment properties of single-split convexification and the split closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P be a nonempty polyhedron and let (\pi,\pi_0) be a split. (i) If \Pi_1,\Pi_2\ne\varnothing and finite sets V_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n satisfy \Pi_i=\operatorname{conv}(V_i)+\operatorname{rec}(\Pi_i) for i=1,2, then P^{(\pi,\pi_0)}=\operatorname{conv}(V_1\cup V_2)+\operatorname{rec}(P). (ii) P^{(\pi,\pi_0)}\subsetneq P if and only if some minimal face F of P satisfies F\subseteq\{x:\pi_0<\pi x<\pi_0+1\}. (iii) If P is rational, then P^{\mathrm{split}}\subsetneq P if and only if \operatorname{conv}(S)\subsetneq P.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convexification associated with one split is generated by the finite generators of its two nonempty sides together with the recession cone of P. It strictly strengthens P exactly when a minimal face lies in the open split strip. For rational P, the full split closure strictly strengthens P exactly when the mixed-integer hull is strictly smaller than P.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Split disjunctions, single-split convexification, and split closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions and representations for general integral splits in mixed-integer polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}, let I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}, let C=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus I, and let S=\{x\in P:x_j\in\mathbb Z\ (j\in I)\}. If (\pi,\pi_0)\in\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb Z and \pi_j=0 for all j\in C, every x\in S satisfies exactly one of \pi x\le\pi_0 and \pi x\ge\pi_0+1. Define \Pi_1=P\cap\{x:\pi x\le\pi_0\}, \Pi_2=P\cap\{x:\pi x\ge\pi_0+1\}, and P^{(\pi,\pi_0)}=\operatorname{conv}(\Pi_1\cup\Pi_2). An inequality is a split inequality associated with this split exactly when it is valid for P^{(\pi,\pi_0)}, and every such inequality is valid for \operatorname{conv}(S). Moreover, P^{(\pi,\pi_0)} is the projection onto x-space of the system Ax^1\le\lambda b,\ \pi x^1\le\lambda\pi_0,\ Ax^2\le(1-\lambda)b,\ \pi x^2\ge(1-\lambda)(\pi_0+1),\ x^1+x^2=x,\ 0\le\lambda\le1. The split closure is P^{\mathrm{split}}=\bigcap_{(\pi,\pi_0)\text{ split}}P^{(\pi,\pi_0)}, and \operatorname{conv}(S)\subseteq P^{\mathrm{split}}\subseteq P. If P is rational, P^{\mathrm{split}} is a rational polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integral linear form supported on the integer variables yields a two-term split disjunction. Convexifying the two corresponding parts of P gives the single-split convexification, whose valid inequalities are split inequalities and remain valid for the mixed-integer hull. This convexification has the stated extended formulation. Intersecting it over all splits gives the split closure, which lies between the mixed-integer hull and P and is rational polyhedral when P is rational.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is rational only for the rational-polyhedrality conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^{(\pi,\pi_0)}=\operatorname{conv}(\Pi_1\cup\Pi_2)=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\pi,\pi_0}),\quad \operatorname{conv}(S)\subseteq P^{\mathrm{split}}\subseteq P,\quad P\text{ rational}\Rightarrow P^{\mathrm{split}}\text{ is a rational polyhedron}.

children.title: MIR-GMI Closure Correspondence
