children.title: Tableau-Basis Separation Interface
children.top_down_role: Generation directly from simplex rows and bases.

children.title: Tableau-Row Separation
children.top_down_role: Cut generation driven directly by selected simplex rows.

assumptions_latex: A pure-integer tableau row is \(x_{B_i}=\bar b_i-\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_{ij}x_j\), with \(x_{B_i}\) and every \(x_j\) integer.
All nonbasic variables satisfy \(x_j\geq0\), and \(f_i=\bar b_i-\lfloor\bar b_i\rfloor\) lies in \((0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Gomory fractional inequality is valid and cuts off the current tableau solution.

notation.meaning: Fractional part of the tableau right-hand side.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer Gomory separation from one fractional simplex-tableau row.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select a tableau row whose basic integer variable has fractional value \(\bar b_i\). Compute the fractional parts \(\{\bar a_{ij}\}\) and \(f_i=\{\bar b_i\}\). Output the Gomory fractional inequality \[\sum_{j\in N}\{\bar a_{ij}\}x_j\geq f_i.\] It is valid for all nonnegative integer solutions satisfying the tableau equation. At the current basic tableau solution, every nonbasic variable equals \(0\), so the left-hand side is \(0\), whereas \(f_i>0\); hence the inequality separates that solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional pure-integer tableau row yields a Gomory fractional inequality that is valid for integer solutions and violated by the current basic solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Tableau-Row Separation

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

children.title: Basis-Driven Separation
children.top_down_role: Cut generation using simplex basis structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Driven Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation using tableau information induced by a chosen simplex basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the basis \(B\), form its tableau \(T(B)\) and identify the eligible row set \(R(B)\), such as rows whose basic integer variables have fractional values at \(\bar x\). Apply the specified valid tableau-cut formula to each selected row, evaluate every generated cut at \(\bar x\), and return a violated cut, optionally one maximizing a prescribed score. If no selected row produces a violated cut, report failure relative to \(B\), \(R(B)\), and the chosen generator. Such failure does not certify membership in the integer hull unless the associated basis-driven family is known to be complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis-driven separation generates valid cuts from eligible rows of the tableau associated with the current basic relaxation solution; failure for that basis does not generally certify integer-hull membership.
assumptions_latex: A rational linear relaxation has a simplex basis \(B\), and \(\bar x\) is the associated current basic relaxation solution.
The basis induces a tableau \(T(B)\) and a specified set \(R(B)\) of eligible rows.
The chosen tableau-cut generator produces a valid inequality from every row to which it is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned cut is valid and violated by \(\bar x\); a negative result is only relative to the selected basis, eligible rows, and generator unless that family is complete.

notation.meaning: Current basic relaxation solution associated with B.
Tableau induced by the basis B.
Eligible tableau rows under the chosen cut rule.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

children.title: Basis-Selection Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of generated cuts on the selected basis.

assumptions_latex: The same relaxation point \(\bar x\) admits distinct valid simplex bases \(B_1\) and \(B_2\).
A fixed tableau-row cut rule is applied to both induced tableaux.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In general, \(\mathcal C(B_1,\bar x)\neq\mathcal C(B_2,\bar x)\); cut availability and violation can depend on the selected basis.

notation.meaning: Set of cuts generated from basis B at the query point.
Violation of cut c at the query point.
Two bases representing the same relaxation point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noninvariance of tableau-derived candidates under alternative bases representing the same relaxation point.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed tableau-row generator, let \(\mathcal C(B,\bar x)\) be the cuts obtainable from the tableau induced by \(B\). Alternative bases can have different basic variables, row coefficients, and fractional right-hand sides. Therefore neither the candidate set nor its best violation is basis invariant: in general, \[\mathcal C(B_1,\bar x)\neq\mathcal C(B_2,\bar x)\quad\text{and}\quad \max_{c\in\mathcal C(B_1,\bar x)}v(c,\bar x)\neq\max_{c\in\mathcal C(B_2,\bar x)}v(c,\bar x).\] Thus failure to find a cut from one basis does not imply failure from every basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different simplex bases for the same point can expose different tableau cuts and different maximum violations; failure under one basis is not basis-independent.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Selection Sensitivity

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Basis dependence of tableau rows is plausible, but the cited introductory cutting-plane locator does not specifically support the asserted noninvariance of both candidate sets and best violation. The latter also requires a fixed cut normalization and a convention for empty candidate sets.

children.title: Incomplete Separation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Incomplete searches, restricted aggregations, and practical approximations.

children.title: Heuristic Separation
children.top_down_role: Incomplete searches intended to locate useful violated cuts.

assumptions_latex: Every inequality returned by the heuristic is valid for the target set \(S\).
The complete family \(\mathcal F\) may contain inequalities not examined by the heuristic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Heuristic success certifies separation, but heuristic failure does not certify \(\bar x\in\bigcap_{(a,b)\in\mathcal F}\{x:a x\leq b\}\).

notation.meaning: Subset inspected during one heuristic call.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound but incomplete separation over a query-dependent subset of a cut family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At query point \(\bar x\), inspect only \(\mathcal F_H(\bar x)\subseteq\mathcal F\). If the heuristic returns \((a,b)\in\mathcal F_H(\bar x)\) with \(a\bar x>b\), then \(a x\leq b\) is a verifiable separating inequality because validity for \(S\) is assumed independently. If the heuristic returns no cut, the only justified conclusion is that it found no violated member of its inspected subset. There may still exist \((a,b)\in\mathcal F\setminus\mathcal F_H(\bar x)\) satisfying \(a\bar x>b\). Hence heuristic separation is one-sided: positive outputs are certificates, while negative outputs generally are not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic’s returned valid cut certifies separation, but finding no cut does not certify that the full inequality family has no violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-sided correctness claim is mathematically plausible but has no citation. Moreover, the record is classified as a failure boundary even though the exact leaf is Heuristic Separation; an algorithm or condition record describing the heuristic interface would fit better, while missed-violation behavior belongs naturally in the separate Missed-Violation Boundaries container.

children.title: Restricted-Aggregation Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation over limited combinations of rows or constraints.

assumptions_latex: Valid inequalities are generated from aggregation multipliers \(\lambda\in\Lambda\).
The separator searches only a prescribed subset \(\Lambda_0\subseteq\Lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure is exact for the restricted family indexed by \(\Lambda_0\), but generally incomplete for the full family indexed by \(\Lambda\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimization over a restricted set of aggregation multipliers, with incomplete full-family coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\bar x\), solve \[v_0^*=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda_0}v(\lambda,\bar x).\] If an optimizer \(\lambda^*\) has \(v(\lambda^*,\bar x)>0\), output the valid inequality generated by \(\lambda^*\). If \(v_0^*\leq0\), certify only that no inequality generated by \(\Lambda_0\) is violated. Exact separation over the full aggregation family requires either \(\Lambda_0=\Lambda\) or a dominance property ensuring that every violated inequality indexed by \(\Lambda\) has an at-least-as-violated representative indexed by \(\Lambda_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted-aggregation separation optimizes violation over selected multipliers; a nonpositive optimum excludes violations only in that restricted subfamily.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Aggregation Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for the aggregation family, multiplier domain, or proposed dominance condition. Those details determine whether the generated inequalities are valid and whether the restricted search has the stated relationship to full-family separation.

children.title: Practical Approximation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Approximate separator designs used under computational limits.

assumptions_latex: The maximum family violation is \(V^*(\bar x)=\max_{y\in Y}v(y,\bar x)\geq0\).
An approximation routine returns \(\hat y\in Y\) satisfying a stated additive or multiplicative guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate separation detects only violations exceeding the guarantee's resolution; smaller positive violations may be missed.

notation.meaning: Maximum violation over the full family.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection guarantees for additive and multiplicative approximations to maximum violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under an additive guarantee \(v(\hat y,\bar x)\geq V^*(\bar x)-\varepsilon\), every query with \(V^*(\bar x)>\varepsilon\) yields \(v(\hat y,\bar x)>0\) and hence a separating inequality. When \(0<V^*(\bar x)\leq\varepsilon\), the routine may return a nonviolated inequality. Under a multiplicative guarantee \(v(\hat y,\bar x)\geq\rho V^*(\bar x)\) with \(\rho>0\), any positive optimum is detected, provided the guarantee applies directly to the nonnegative violation objective. Thus practical approximation must specify its objective normalization and whether its error is additive or multiplicative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive approximate separation can miss violations at most its tolerance; multiplicative guarantees detect positive violations only when applied to a nonnegative violation objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Practical Approximation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive and multiplicative implications are correct under the stated objective guarantees, but no source supports these approximate-separation conventions. A reference is needed because multiplicative guarantees depend critically on nonnegative objective normalization and on the precise approximation model.

children.title: Missed-Violation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where incomplete or restricted searches fail to detect violations.

knowledge_statements.title: Missed-Violation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between failure to find a cut and certification that no family member exceeds the specified violation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An incomplete separator has a missed-violation boundary at \(\bar x\) when it may return \(\mathtt{NONE}\) although some \((a,\beta)\in\mathcal C\) satisfies \(a^\top\bar x>\beta+\varepsilon\). Consequently, \(\mathtt{NONE}\) implies only that the routine found no violation in its searched subfamily or search trajectory. It implies \(\bar x\in P_{\mathcal C}^{\varepsilon}\) only if the routine is complete at tolerance \(\varepsilon\), meaning that every \(\mathtt{NONE}\) response guarantees \(a^\top\bar x\leq\beta+\varepsilon\) for all \((a,\beta)\in\mathcal C\). Exact membership in \(P_{\mathcal C}\) follows when \(\varepsilon=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incomplete separator may report no cut despite a violation beyond the chosen tolerance. Complete separation certifies membership in the tolerance-relaxed cut closure, and certifies exact membership only at zero tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the current relaxation and \(F\subseteq P\) is the feasible set.
\(\mathcal C\) is a family of inequalities valid for \(F\).
A separation routine queried at \(\bar x\in P\) returns either a violated member of \(\mathcal C\) or \(\mathtt{NONE}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A \(\mathtt{NONE}\) response certifies \(\bar x\in P_{\mathcal C}^{\varepsilon}\) only under complete separation at tolerance \(\varepsilon\); it certifies \(\bar x\in P_{\mathcal C}\) when additionally \(\varepsilon=0\).

notation.meaning: exact closure of the relaxation under the cut family
tolerance-relaxed closure under the cut family

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distinction between exact and incomplete separation

children.title: Separation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity distinctions among exact, parameterized, and heuristic separators.

children.title: Polynomially Separable Cut Families
children.top_down_role: Families admitting efficient exact separation under standard encodings.

assumptions_latex: Instances and rational query points use binary encoding.
\(\mathcal C(I)\) is the cut family associated with instance \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact separation for \(\mathcal C\) is polynomially solvable when its separator runs in time polynomial in the encoded input length.

notation.meaning: binary encoding length of the instance and query point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity definition for exact strong separation of a rationally encoded cut family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \(\mathcal C\) is polynomially separable if an algorithm exists that, given \((I,\bar x)\), runs in time \(L^{O(1)}\) and either returns \((a,\beta)\in\mathcal C(I)\) with \(a^\top\bar x>\beta\), or correctly certifies \(a^\top\bar x\leq\beta\) for every \((a,\beta)\in\mathcal C(I)\). The running time includes producing a rational encoding of the returned inequality and is polynomial in the total binary input length \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut family is polynomially separable when exact separation, including writing the returned inequality, takes polynomial time in the binary input length.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomially Separable Cut Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial-time separation criterion is standard and fits the leaf, but no source is supplied. A source should also confirm the bit-complexity and output-encoding convention; L should formally denote the length of the encoded pair rather than the pair itself.

children.title: Hard Separation Cut Families
children.top_down_role: Families whose exact separation captures difficult combinatorial optimization.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C(I)\) is a rationally encoded cut family.
The associated separation question is interpreted as a decision problem under polynomial-time many-one reductions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the separation decision problem is NP-hard, a polynomial-time exact separator would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).

notation.meaning: cut family associated with instance I

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard reduction-based separation hardness criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic hardness criterion rather than a claim about one particular named inequality family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the separation decision problem by asking, for input \((I,\bar x)\), whether there exists \((a,\beta)\in\mathcal C(I)\) such that \(a^\top\bar x>\beta\). The family is hard to separate when this problem is NP-hard under the stated encoding and reductions. Because any exact separator decides this question by either producing a violated inequality or certifying that none exists, a polynomial-time exact separator for an NP-hard family would yield \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family has hard separation when deciding whether any member is violated is NP-hard; exact polynomial-time separation would then imply P equals NP.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard Separation Cut Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduction-based NP-hardness criterion is mathematically coherent and the complexity-bound kind fits, but the encoding, reduction convention, and separation decision formulation lack a cited source.

children.title: Parameter-Dimension Separation Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Tractable separation regimes obtained by restricting structural dimensions.

children.title: Fixed-Parameter Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation tractability indexed by bounded structural parameters.

assumptions_latex: \(k=k(I)\) is a nonnegative integer parameter of the encoded instance.
The separator must be exact for every rational query point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The separation problem is fixed-parameter tractable with parameter \(k\) when its running time is \(f(k)L^c\) for computable \(f\) and constant \(c\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard fixed-parameter tractability definition applied to separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized bit complexity of exact separation; the polynomial exponent is independent of the parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact separation for \(\mathcal C\) is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to \(k\) if there are a computable function \(f\) and a constant \(c\), independent of \(k\), such that every input \((I,\bar x)\) is separated in time \(f(k(I))L^c\). The algorithm must either output a violated inequality from \(\mathcal C(I)\) or certify that none exists. Thus fixing \(k\) gives polynomial time, while arbitrary dependence on \(k\) is confined to \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-parameter separation runs in f(k) times a fixed polynomial in input length, with the polynomial exponent independent of k.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Parameter Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated f(k)L^c criterion correctly describes fixed-parameter tractable exact separation, but no authoritative parameterized-complexity or separation source is provided.

children.title: Fixed-Dimension Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation tractability under bounded geometric or formulation dimension.

assumptions_latex: The ambient dimension \(n\) is fixed independently of the binary input length.
All coefficients and the query point are rationally encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A separation procedure with running time \(L^{g(n)}\) is polynomial-time for each fixed \(n\), though not necessarily fixed-parameter tractable in \(n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity classification for separation algorithms whose polynomial degree may depend on dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cut family admits fixed-dimension separation if, for every fixed \(n\), an exact separator processes rational input of length \(L\) in time \(L^{g(n)}\) for some function \(g\). It returns a violated family inequality or certifies that none exists. This is polynomial time after fixing \(n\), but the bound is generally only in the class \(\mathrm{XP}\) parameterized by \(n\); it is fixed-parameter tractable only when a bound \(f(n)L^c\) with constant \(c\) is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-dimension separator is polynomial for every constant dimension, but a dimension-dependent exponent need not give fixed-parameter tractability.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Dimension Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between fixed-dimension polynomial time, XP, and FPT is correct, but the applicable complexity convention and geometric-separation context require a source.

children.title: Parameter–Dimension Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Complexity tradeoffs between parameter restrictions and dimensional restrictions.

assumptions_latex: \(k\) is a structural parameter and \(n\) is ambient dimension.
\(L\) is the rational binary input length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounds \(f(k,n)L^c\), \(f(k)L^{g(n)}\), and \(L^{h(k,n)}\) express progressively weaker parameter–dimension guarantees.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct comparison of standard parameterized running-time forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of exact-separation running times by structural parameter, dimension, and encoding length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For exact separation, a bound \(f(k,n)L^c\) with constant \(c\) is fixed-parameter tractable in the combined parameter \((k,n)\). A bound \(f(k)L^{g(n)}\) is polynomial for every fixed \((k,n)\) and fixed-parameter tractable in \(k\) whenever \(n\) is fixed, but it need not be fixed-parameter tractable in \((k,n)\). A bound \(L^{h(k,n)}\) provides only fixed-parameter polynomiality, customarily classified as \(\mathrm{XP}\), unless its exponent is uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: How parameters and dimension enter the exponent distinguishes combined fixed-parameter tractability from weaker fixed-dimension or XP guarantees.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter–Dimension Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The running-time comparisons are internally consistent and the property kind fits the tradeoff leaf, but no source supports the combined parameter and dimension classification.

children.title: Cutting-Plane Algorithm Families
children.top_down_role: Relaxation-refinement frameworks distinguished by cut source and integration with search.

children.title: Pure Cutting-Plane Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods relying on repeated relaxation refinement without explicit branching.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the target feasible set and \(P_0\supseteq F\) is a tractable relaxation.
Every generated inequality is valid for \(F\).
Each relaxation optimization problem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method maintains \(F\subseteq P_{t+1}\subseteq P_t\) and terminates only with an accepted feasible optimum or a stated stopping condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic minimization-form pure cutting-plane scheme without branching.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(t=0\) and \(P_0\supseteq F\). At iteration \(t\), solve \(x^t\in\arg\min\{c^\top x:x\in P_t\}\). If \(x^t\in F\), output \(x^t\); its relaxation optimality proves optimality over \(F\). Otherwise generate a nonempty finite set \(C_t\) of inequalities \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) valid for \(F\), with at least one violated by \(x^t\), and set \(P_{t+1}=P_t\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in C_t}\{x:a^\top x\leq\beta\}\). Repeat until acceptance, infeasibility, or an explicit resource limit; no branching is performed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly optimize a relaxation and add valid inequalities violated by its solution; accept a feasible relaxation optimum, and never branch.
knowledge_statements.title: Pure Cutting-Plane Methods

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fractional Cutting-Plane Relaxation Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure cutting-plane relaxation refinement for a nonnegative pure-integer linear feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For $S=\{x\in\mathbb Z_+^n:Ax\le b\}$, initialize $z_R^1(x)=cx$ for $x\in\mathbb R_+^n$ and $S_R^1=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax\le b\}$. Given an optimizer $x^t$ of the current relaxation, choose an inequality $\pi^t x\le\pi_0^t$ that is valid for $S$ and satisfies $\pi^t x^t>\pi_0^t$. Set $z_R^{t+1}(x)=z_R^t(x)$ and $S_R^{t+1}=S_R^t\cap\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:\pi^t x\le\pi_0^t\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin with the continuous relaxation. At each refinement, add a valid inequality that excludes the current relaxation optimizer while preserving every integer-feasible point, leaving the objective unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\subseteq S_R^{t+1}\subsetneq S_R^t\quad\text{and}\quad x^t\notin S_R^{t+1}

source_evidence.locator: General Algorithms / II.4.1. Introduction / Algorithm II.4.1-extra-3

children.title: Branch-Cut Interface
children.top_down_role: Root-node, tree-node, global-cut, and local-cut integration with enumeration.

children.title: Root-Node Cut Integration
children.top_down_role: Cut generation and selection at the root relaxation.

assumptions_latex: The root relaxation \(P_0\) contains the integer-feasible set \(F\).
All root-generated cuts are globally valid for \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After root processing, \(F\subseteq P_r\subseteq P_0\), so the strengthened root bound is valid for the entire search tree.

notation.meaning: root relaxation after r cut rounds
globally valid cuts added in round t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-only cut loop in a minimization branch-and-cut algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the root, initialize \(P_0\) with the model relaxation. For rounds \(t=0,\ldots,r-1\), solve the current relaxation, separate a finite set \(C_t\) of globally valid inequalities, and update \(P_{t+1}=P_t\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in C_t}\{x:a^\top x\leq\beta\}\). Stop root separation by the prescribed efficacy, progress, or resource rule, then initialize branching from \(P_r\). Since every added inequality is valid for \(F\), the root strengthening and its resulting objective bound remain valid throughout the descendant tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate globally valid cuts before branching, then use the strengthened root relaxation and bound throughout the search tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Root-Node Cut Integration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The root-only cut loop and global-validity conclusion are coherent, but no branch-and-cut source supports the integration and tree-wide bound claims.

children.title: Tree-Node Cut Integration
children.top_down_role: Cut generation during branch-tree exploration.

assumptions_latex: A search-tree node \(v\) has relaxation \(P_v\) containing its node-feasible integer set \(F_v\).
Each generated cut is declared global or valid on a specified subtree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cut insertion preserves \(F_v\subseteq P'_v\subseteq P_v\), and propagation is limited to nodes where the cut is valid.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut separation and validity-aware propagation at non-root branch-and-cut nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When node \(v\) is processed, solve its current relaxation \(P_v\), call separation at the resulting point, and form \(P'_v=P_v\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in C_v}\{x:a^\top x\leq\beta\}\). Reoptimize after accepted cuts until a stopping rule applies, then fathom or branch. A global cut may enter the global pool and all compatible nodes; a cut valid only under node restrictions is attached to \(v\) and propagated solely to descendants satisfying those restrictions. In every affected node, cut validity preserves containment of its integer-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a search node, separate and reoptimize before fathoming or branching, propagating each cut only across the portion of the tree where it is valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Node Cut Integration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The node processing and validity-aware propagation description fits the leaf, but its cut-pool, subtree-propagation, and reoptimization policies require an authoritative source.

children.title: Global Cut Scope
children.top_down_role: Cuts valid throughout the enumeration tree.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the feasible set of the original mixed-integer model.
The inequality is derived without relying on temporary branch restrictions, or its validity for all of \(F\) is independently established.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality may be imposed at every search node because it cannot remove any point of \(F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: defining validity condition for a global cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity predicate governing global cut propagation in branch-and-cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) has global scope precisely when \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in F\). Its derivation may use globally valid model information but must not depend on a branch condition absent elsewhere in the tree unless global validity is separately proved. Once admitted as global, the inequality may be added to the root relaxation, stored in a global cut pool, and enforced at any node without excluding an originally feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is global exactly when every original feasible point satisfies it, permitting enforcement anywhere in the branch-and-cut tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Cut Scope

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity condition for global scope is mathematically correct and the condition kind fits, but branch-and-cut scope terminology and propagation consequences are uncited.

children.title: Local Cut Scope
children.top_down_role: Cuts valid only within designated subtrees or nodes.

assumptions_latex: Node \(v\) has branch-restricted feasible set \(F_v\subseteq F\).
The candidate inequality is valid for \(F_v\), but global validity is not established.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality may be enforced at \(v\) and its descendants, but not outside that subtree without an additional validity argument.

notation.meaning: feasible set under the branch restrictions at node v

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: defining validity condition for a local cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subtree-relative validity predicate for cuts derived using branch restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) has local scope at node \(v\) when \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in F_v\), while validity for every \(x\in F\) is unknown or false. Because every descendant \(w\) of \(v\) satisfies \(F_w\subseteq F_v\), the inequality remains valid throughout the subtree rooted at \(v\). It must be deactivated after leaving that subtree and cannot enter a global cut pool unless global validity is separately certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local cut is valid under one node's branch restrictions and hence throughout its subtree, but cannot be used elsewhere without proving global validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Cut Scope

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Subtree validity follows correctly from descendant feasible-set containment, but the local-cut terminology and management claims require a cited branch-and-cut source.

children.top_down_role: Interaction between row generation and dynamic variable generation.

children.title: Cut Generation Interface
children.top_down_role: Row-generation integration within branch-cut-price frameworks.

assumptions_latex: A restricted master relaxation contains a current row set and column set.
The cut generator receives a primal relaxation solution expressed in the master variables.
Generated rows are valid for the full master formulation, including columns not currently present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only rows whose coefficients are defined and valid for all admissible columns can be safely passed from cut generation to the restricted master.

notation.meaning: set of all admissible master columns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-generation side of branch-cut-and-price, emphasizing validity under future column insertion.

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Column generation p. 42
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the restricted-master solution \(\bar x\), the cut-generation interface either returns \(\mathtt{NONE}\) or a row \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) violated by \(\bar x\). Before insertion, it must certify validity for the intended node domain and provide, explicitly or through a coefficient oracle, \(a_j\) for every admissible column \(j\in J\), including columns generated later. Insert the row, update pricing so reduced costs include its dual multiplier, and reoptimize by alternating row separation and column pricing until their stopping conditions are simultaneously met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cut interface returns violated valid rows whose coefficients remain defined for future columns, then coordinates reoptimization with pricing.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Generation Interface

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Column generation p. 42
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Column Generation Interface
children.top_down_role: Dynamic variable generation within branch-cut-price frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Generation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact restricted-master pricing at a fixed branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_N\) be the columns eligible at the current node, with \(a_j\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(c_j\in\mathbb R\) for every \(j\in J_N\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). For a nonempty restricted set \(J'\subseteq J_N\), solve \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J'}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J'}a_j\lambda_j=b,\ \lambda_j\geq0\}\) and obtain an optimal equality-row dual vector \(\pi\in\mathbb R^m\). Pricing finds \(j^*\in\arg\min_{j\in J_N}\{c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\}\). If \(c_{j^*}-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_{j^*}<0\), add \(j^*\) and reoptimize. If pricing certifies \(\min_{j\in J_N}(c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j)\geq0\), the current restricted-master solution is optimal for the full node LP over \(J_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the restricted master and add a node-eligible column of negative reduced cost; a certified nonnegative minimum over every eligible column proves full node-LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(J_N\) contains every column eligible at the current node.
The restricted master is feasible and has a finite optimum.
Exact pricing attains its minimum over \(J_N\), or otherwise supplies an equivalent certified lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{j\in J_N}(c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j)\geq0\) certifies optimality for the full node relaxation.

notation.meaning: Restricted and full node-eligible column sets.
Column vector, objective coefficient, and master variable for column j.
Dual multiplier for the master equality rows.

children.title: Row–Column Coordination
children.top_down_role: Interactions between evolving cut pools and restricted master columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Row–Column Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistent maintenance of active cut rows when columns are generated dynamically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each master column \(j\) have reconstruction vector \(a_j\in\mathbb R^n\), cost \(c_j\in\mathbb R\), and variable \(\lambda_j\geq0\), with \(x=\sum_j a_j\lambda_j\). For active cuts \(\alpha_k^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta_k\), indexed by \(k\in K\), the master must contain \(\sum_j(\alpha_k^{\mathsf T}a_j)\lambda_j\geq\beta_k\). Consequently, every future column \(a_j\) must receive coefficient \(\alpha_k^{\mathsf T}a_j\) in each active row. For a minimization master, let \(\pi\) denote the dual vector of its equality rows and let \(\sigma_k\geq0\) denote the dual multiplier of cut row \(k\). Pricing must then use the reduced cost \(c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j-\sum_{k\in K}\sigma_k\alpha_k^{\mathsf T}a_j\). Omitting an active-row coefficient or its dual contribution makes the restricted master and pricing oracle represent different full masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every generated column must be evaluated in every active cut, and minimization pricing must include the associated nonnegative row-dual contributions with the stated sign convention.
assumptions_latex: Every active inequality \(\alpha_k^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta_k\) is valid for all feasible reconstructed points.
The master is a minimization problem and its active cut rows use the displayed greater-than orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted master and pricing oracle represent the same full master only when all active-row coefficients and dual contributions are synchronized.

notation.meaning: Reconstruction vector, cost, and variable of column j.
Normal and right-hand side of active cut k.
Index set of active cut rows.
Equality-row dual vector and nonnegative dual multiplier of cut row k.

children.title: Pricing Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Effects of generated cuts on pricing structure and validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for valid pricing termination and node bounds under restricted or inexact pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_N\) be the complete set of columns eligible at the current node, and let \(\bar c_j\in\mathbb R\) be the reduced cost of column \(j\), including every active-row dual contribution. A pricing termination certificate is valid whenever it supplies \(L\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(L\leq\inf_{j\in J_N}\bar c_j\). Thus \(L\geq0\) certifies that no node-eligible improving column exists. Searching only \(\widehat J\subsetneq J_N\), omitting active dual terms, or returning an uncertified heuristic minimum cannot provide this conclusion without an additional valid bounding argument. A certified bound over a superset \(J^+\supseteq J_N\) is sufficient for termination when it is nonnegative, although any generated column must still belong to \(J_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing may terminate only from a certified lower bound valid for every node-eligible reduced cost; an incomplete or heuristic search is insufficient, while a nonnegative bound over a superset is conservative and valid.
assumptions_latex: The master is a minimization problem.
Reduced costs use an optimal restricted-master dual solution and include every active-row contribution.
\(J_N\) is the exact node-eligible column set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L\leq\inf_{j\in J_N}\bar c_j\) and \(L\geq0\), pricing terminates validly; without such a bound, failure to discover a column has no optimality implication.

notation.meaning: Complete column set eligible at the current node.
Full reduced cost including all active-row dual terms.
Certified lower bound on every node-eligible reduced cost.
Optional pricing superset containing all node-eligible columns.

children.title: Decomposition-Cut Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Boundary between integer-hull cuts and decomposition-generated master cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Cut Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP-recourse Benders cuts as projected-master inequalities rather than integer-hull cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\in Y\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), \(z\in\mathbb R^r\), \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\), \(T\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(q\in\mathbb R^r\). Define \(Q(y)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}z:Wz\geq h-Ty,\ z\geq0\}\) and let \(D\subseteq Y\) contain the points at which this recourse LP is feasible and has a finite optimum. With \(\Pi=\{\pi\in\mathbb R_+^m:W^{\mathsf T}\pi\leq q\}\), linear-programming duality gives \(Q(y)=\max_{\pi\in\Pi}\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\) for every \(y\in D\). Hence \(\operatorname{epi}_D Q=\{(y,\eta)\in D\times\mathbb R:\eta\geq\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\text{ for every }\pi\in\Pi\}\). If \(\Pi\) is nonempty and pointed, maximizing extreme points generate the required optimality cuts on \(D\). These projected-recourse cuts need not be facets or cutting planes of the integer hull of \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the domain where linear recourse is feasible and finite, dual-feasible recourse multipliers generate the master epigraph; these projected-value cuts are distinct from integer-hull cuts.
assumptions_latex: The recourse problem is a finite-dimensional linear program.
For every \(y\in D\), recourse is feasible and has a finite optimal value.
The extreme-point assertion additionally assumes that \(\Pi\) is nonempty and pointed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}_D Q=\{(y,\eta)\in D\times\mathbb R:\eta\geq\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\text{ for every }\pi\in\Pi\}\).

notation.meaning: Optimal recourse value at master point y.
Master points with feasible, finite recourse.
Master epigraph variable for recourse cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Cut Quality Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware diagnostics for one candidate inequality at an LP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a candidate cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq eta\), current point \( ar x\), and nonzero objective vector \(c\), define violation \(v=(a^{\mathsf T} ar x- eta)_+\), efficacy or Euclidean cutoff distance \(e=v/\lVert aVert_2\), and objective alignment \(o=|a^{\mathsf T}c|/(\lVert aVert_2\lVert cVert_2)\). Its support size is \(s=|\{i:a_i
eq0\}|\), and its coefficient dynamic range is \(d=\max_{i:a_i
eq0}|a_i|/\min_{i:a_i
eq0}|a_i|\). Larger \(v,e,o\) indicate stronger immediate geometric effect, while large \(s\) or \(d\) may signal greater computational or numerical cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Violation, normalized distance, objective alignment, support size, and coefficient range quantify complementary geometric and numerical aspects of one cut.
assumptions_latex: The cut is written in the orientation \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quality vector is \((v,e,o,s,d)\), with \(e\) and \(o\) invariant under positive rescaling of the cut.

notation.meaning: Violation, efficacy, alignment, support, and dynamic range.
