children.title: Cut-Direction Redundancy Control
children.top_down_role: Selection of complementary rather than redundant cut directions.

children.title: Cut-Direction Diversity
children.top_down_role: Selection criteria favoring complementary cut directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Direction Diversity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise angular diversity condition for a selected cut set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a set of cuts with nonzero normals \(a_i\). For a prescribed \(\rho\in[0,1)\), call \(S\) direction-diverse when \[\max_{i\neq j,\ i,j\in S}\frac{|a_i^{\mathsf T}a_j|}{\lVert a_i\rVert_2\lVert a_j\rVert_2}\leq\rho.\] Equivalently, the acute angle between every pair of cut hyperplanes is at least \(\arccos\rho\). This condition is invariant under nonzero rescaling or sign reversal of any normal and controls directional redundancy, not logical redundancy or dominance between inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut set is direction-diverse when every pair of normals has bounded absolute cosine similarity.
assumptions_latex: Every selected cut normal is nonzero.
Diversity is measured in the Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pairwise hyperplane angles in \(S\) are at least \(\arccos\rho\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied for its use as a cut-direction diversity criterion.

children.title: Near-Parallel Cut Filtering
children.top_down_role: Controls for rejecting geometrically redundant cut directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Parallel Cut Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy filtering after orienting and normalizing candidate inequalities consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input ordered candidate cuts \((a_i,\beta_i)\), quality scores \(q_i\), and threshold \(\tau\in(0,1)\). Orient all cuts as \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta_i\), normalize \(u_i=a_i/\lVert a_i\rVert_2\), and process candidates in nonincreasing \(q_i\). Accept candidate \(i\) exactly when \(u_i^{\mathsf T}u_j<\tau\) for every previously accepted \(j\); otherwise discard it as near-parallel to a no-worse accepted cut. Output the accepted set. The filter limits directional duplication but does not establish algebraic redundancy of discarded cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process cuts by quality and reject a candidate whose oriented normal is too parallel to an already accepted, no-worse cut.
assumptions_latex: All inequalities use a common orientation before comparison.
The score ordering resolves which near-parallel cut is retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Distinct accepted cuts satisfy \(u_i^{\mathsf T}u_j<\tau\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent greedy filtering policy and the algorithm kind fits, but near-parallel filtering has multiple orientation and similarity conventions; a source is required for this particular threshold rule.

children.title: Angular Similarity Measures
children.top_down_role: Geometric measures used to compare candidate cut orientations.

knowledge_statements.title: Angular Similarity Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oriented and sign-invariant similarities between nonzero cut normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero cut normals \(a,b\in\mathbb R^n\), define oriented cosine similarity \(s(a,b)=a^{\mathsf T}b/(\lVert a\rVert_2\lVert b\rVert_2)\), oriented angle \(\theta(a,b)=\arccos s(a,b)\), and hyperplane similarity \(s_{\mathrm{hp}}(a,b)=|s(a,b)|\). The acute hyperplane angle is \(\theta_{\mathrm{hp}}(a,b)=\arccos s_{\mathrm{hp}}(a,b)\in[0,\pi/2]\). Oriented measures distinguish parallel from antiparallel inequality normals; hyperplane measures identify directions up to sign. All four measures are invariant under positive rescaling of either normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cosine and angular measures compare cut normals either with inequality orientation preserved or with sign ignored.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean inner product and norm are used.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary inner-product definitions specialized to cut normals
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Euclidean definitions are internally correct and match the leaf, but the record has no citation with an inspectable locator connecting these measures to cut management.

children.title: Adaptive Cut-Family Portfolio
children.top_down_role: Context-dependent portfolios spanning several separator families.

children.title: Cut-Family Balancing
children.top_down_role: Allocation of selection capacity across multiple separator families.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Family Balancing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quota condition preventing one cut family from consuming the entire portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let candidate cuts be partitioned into families \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\), and let a round admit at most \(B\) cuts. A family-balanced selection \(S\) satisfies \(|S|\leq B\) and prescribed bounds \[\ell_f\leq|S\cap F_f|\leq u_f\qquad(f=1,\ldots,m),\] where \(0\leq\ell_f\leq u_f\), \(\sum_f\ell_f\leq B\), and only families having at least \(\ell_f\) eligible candidates receive positive lower quotas. Within these constraints, cuts may be ranked by quality. Feasible positive lower quotas prevent immediate family exclusion, while upper quotas bound concentration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Family balancing imposes feasible lower and upper selection quotas, then permits quality ranking within the remaining budget.
assumptions_latex: Candidates have a declared family partition.
The quota system is feasible for the current candidate pool.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every balanced selection respects the total budget and each family quota.

notation.meaning: Candidate cuts belonging to family f.
Total cut budget for the round.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quota condition is well formed under the explicit feasibility assumption, but it is a configurable portfolio policy rather than a canonical mathematical definition and requires a cut-management source.

children.title: Adaptive Cut Selection
children.top_down_role: Context-dependent selection based on evolving solver behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Cut Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online family-weight update using bounded observed cut rewards.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize family weights \(w_{f,1}=1\). At round \(t\), assign each eligible cut \(i\in F_f\) score \(w_{f,t}q_{i,t}\), select a budget-feasible set using these scores and applicable diversity constraints, and observe family reward \(r_{f,t}\in[0,1]\). Update \[w_{f,t+1}=\frac{w_{f,t}\exp(\eta r_{f,t})}{\sum_g w_{g,t}\exp(\eta r_{g,t})},\] with learning rate \(\eta>0\). Unobserved rewards require an explicit estimator or exploration rule; treating them as observed zeros changes the policy. Output the selected cuts each round and the updated family distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank candidates using quality times learned family weights, then update those weights from bounded post-selection rewards.
assumptions_latex: Candidate quality scores and family memberships are available each round.
Budget and diversity constraints define a feasible selection set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update produces \(w_{f,t+1}>0\) and \(\sum_f w_{f,t+1}=1\).

notation.meaning: Weight of family f at round t.
Current intrinsic quality score of cut i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized exponential update is mathematically valid after each update, but the navigation title does not determine this particular learning policy, reward estimator, or exploration mechanism. An authoritative source is required.

children.title: Portfolio Feedback Signals
children.top_down_role: Solver signals used to revise cut-family preferences.

knowledge_statements.title: Portfolio Feedback Signals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized solver observations used to update cut-family preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For family \(f\) at round \(t\), let \(A_{f,t}\) be its generated cuts and \(K_{f,t}\subseteq A_{f,t}\) the accepted cuts. Define acceptance \(p_{f,t}=|K_{f,t}|/\max\{1,|A_{f,t}|\}\), survival \(s_{f,t}=|K_{f,t}\cap P_{t+1}|/\max\{1,|K_{f,t}|\}\), normalized bound gain \(g_{f,t}\in[0,1]\), and normalized generation cost \(c_{f,t}\in[0,1]\). A portfolio reward may be specified as \(r_{f,t}=\alpha p_{f,t}+\beta s_{f,t}+\gamma g_{f,t}-\delta c_{f,t}\), with fixed nonnegative coefficients and an explicit normalization and attribution window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceptance, pool survival, bound gain, and generation cost form measurable feedback signals for each cut family.
assumptions_latex: Every signal uses a fixed observation window.
Bound improvement and cost are normalized before aggregation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tuple \((p_{f,t},s_{f,t},g_{f,t},c_{f,t})\) is an auditable family-level feedback record.

notation.meaning: Generated and accepted cuts of family f.
Cut pool observed at the next evaluation time.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The acceptance and survival ratios are explicit, but bound-gain normalization, cost normalization, attribution windows, and aggregate coefficients are solver-dependent and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Family Starvation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Portfolio regimes where useful cut families receive insufficient selection capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Family Starvation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of separator completeness when a necessary family receives no opportunities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two cut families \(F_1,F_2\) and a relaxation point \(\bar x\) for which every violated available valid inequality belongs to \(F_2\). If a portfolio policy assigns \(F_2\) zero generation or selection opportunity from some round onward, no subsequent round can separate \(\bar x\), even when an oracle for \(F_2\) would do so. More generally, an adaptive portfolio preserves access to every potentially necessary family only if it enforces recurring exploration, such as \(p_{f,t}\geq\varepsilon_f>0\), or a deterministic bounded waiting time between opportunities. Positive weights without such an opportunity guarantee do not prevent starvation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family excluded indefinitely can contain the only available separating cuts, destroying completeness despite their validity.
assumptions_latex: At least one family can uniquely supply a violated valid inequality.
Family scheduling controls whether its separator is invoked or its cuts selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Indefinite zero opportunity for a necessary family can prevent separation; recurring exploration excludes this starvation mechanism.

notation.meaning: Probability or share of opportunity assigned to family f.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The starvation mechanism is plausible and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but the recurring-exploration condition lacks a source, and the claim about all subsequent rounds implicitly requires the point and available separating families to remain relevant.

children.title: Cut Resource Budgeting
children.top_down_role: Limits on separator effort, accepted rows, rounds, and relaxation growth.

children.title: Separator Effort Budgets
children.top_down_role: Limits on computational effort allocated to separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Effort Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic per-node budget for computational work spent by cut separators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the finite set of enabled separators. For each \(s\in S\), let \(e_s\ge 0\) denote measured effort, such as oracle calls or elapsed time, and let \(b_s\ge 0\) be its individual allowance. Given a total allowance \(B_{\mathrm{sep}}\ge 0\), separator execution is budget-feasible exactly when \[e_s\le b_s\quad(s\in S),\qquad \sum_{s\in S}e_s\le B_{\mathrm{sep}}.\] Once either applicable bound is exhausted, no further invocation charged to that budget is permitted at the current search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separator work is feasible when every separator respects its allowance and their total measured effort does not exceed the node-level budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_s\le b_s\ (s\in S)\) and \(\sum_{s\in S}e_s\le B_{\mathrm{sep}}\).
review_flags: Operational effort units and exhaustion semantics require a solver-oriented source.
standard_field_rationale: resource limits are represented by individual and aggregate nonnegative budget inequalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the budget leaf, and the individual and aggregate inequalities are coherent. However, no citation supports the solver-specific effort units, charging interval, or exhaustion behavior; the statement also needs clarification that exhaustion of an individual allowance blocks only that separator, whereas exhaustion of the aggregate allowance blocks all charged invocations.

children.title: Accepted-Cut Budgets
children.top_down_role: Limits on the number of generated rows admitted to the relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Accepted-Cut Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cardinality budget on cuts admitted from separator output during one selection event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be the finite set of candidate cuts produced at a node or cut round, and let \(A\subseteq C\) be the cuts accepted for insertion. For a prescribed integer budget \(B_{\mathrm{acc}}\ge 0\), the acceptance decision is budget-feasible precisely when \[|A|\le \min\{B_{\mathrm{acc}},|C|\}.\] If cuts are partitioned into families \(C_f\) with quotas \(b_f\), feasibility additionally requires \(|A\cap C_f|\le b_f\) for every governed family \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The admitted portfolio may contain at most the total accepted-cut allowance and must also satisfy any family-specific quotas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|A|\le B_{\mathrm{acc}}\) and \(|A\cap C_f|\le b_f\) for each governed family \(f\).
review_flags: The inventory locators do not document cut-selection quota semantics.
standard_field_rationale: accepted-cut limits are finite-cardinality constraints, optionally refined by family quotas.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role and cardinality formulation fit Accepted-Cut Budgets. No cited source supports the selection-event scope or optional family-quota semantics, and the governed family index set and whether the families form a partition require source-backed specification.

children.title: Cut-Round Budgets
children.top_down_role: Limits on repeated rounds of separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Round Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A stopping condition limiting successive separation-and-reoptimization rounds at one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Index completed cut rounds at a fixed search node by \(r=0,1,\ldots\). Given an integer allowance \(R_{\max}\ge 0\), a new round may start only if \(r<R_{\max}\). Each completed round increments \(r\) by one, whether or not its generated candidates are accepted. Consequently the procedure must terminate the node's cutting phase no later than the first state satisfying \(r=R_{\max}\), unless an earlier stopping rule applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At most the prescribed number of separation-and-reoptimization rounds may be completed at a node, with empty or rejected rounds still counted.
assumptions_latex: Every initiated round eventually completes or is aborted and charged by a declared convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\le R_{\max}\), and a new round requires \(r<R_{\max}\).
review_flags: Whether aborted or empty rounds are charged is implementation-specific and needs a source.
standard_field_rationale: a round budget is an integer counter with a guarded transition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The guarded counter is appropriately classified as a condition for this leaf. A solver-oriented source is required to establish what constitutes a round and whether empty, rejected, or aborted rounds are charged; those conventions materially determine the claim.

children.title: Relaxation-Size Budgets
children.top_down_role: Limits on growth of the active linear relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Size Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A row-count budget controlling the size of the current linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_0\) be the indispensable base rows and \(R_t\supseteq R_0\) the active relaxation rows after update \(t\). For an integer bound \(B_{\mathrm{row}}\ge |R_0|\), the relaxation-size budget requires \[|R_t|\le B_{\mathrm{row}}\quad\text{for every }t.\] Before inserting a set \(I_t\) that would violate this bound, the manager must reject some proposed rows or remove at least \(|R_t\cup I_t|-B_{\mathrm{row}}\) eligible nonbase rows; rows in \(R_0\) are never removed by this budget rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every active relaxation must respect a row limit; excess insertions require rejection or removal of enough eligible nonbase rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|R_t|\le B_{\mathrm{row}}\) for every update \(t\).
review_flags: The supplied sources do not specify operational relaxation-size management.
standard_field_rationale: relaxation size is controlled by a cardinality invariant preserving indispensable rows.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The invariant is a suitable condition for Relaxation-Size Budgets. The available inventory is not cited and does not establish the asserted base-row protection or rejection/removal policy. The removal-count formula also depends on eligibility and set-overlap conventions that need source-backed specification.

children.title: Cut-Pool Lifecycle Interface
children.top_down_role: Lifecycle management for generated cuts and the evolving relaxation.

children.title: Active-Row Cut-Pool State Interface
children.top_down_role: Distinction between cuts in the current relaxation and stored reusable cuts.

children.title: Active Relaxation Rows
children.top_down_role: Cuts currently present in the solved relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Relaxation Rows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The state component containing constraints currently enforced by the node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At search node \(v\), let \(P_v\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the relaxation before managed cuts are imposed. An active-row set is a finite collection \(R_v=\{(a_i,\beta_i):i\in I_v\}\) of inequalities currently passed to the relaxation solver. Its enforced relaxation is \[P_v(R_v)=P_v\cap\bigcap_{i\in I_v}\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta_i\}.\] Membership in \(R_v\) records present enforcement, not merely storage in a cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active rows are the finite stored inequalities currently imposed on a node relaxation; pooled but unenforced cuts are excluded.
assumptions_latex: Every active row has compatible dimension \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_v(R_v)=P_v\cap\bigcap_{i\in I_v}\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta_i\}\).
review_flags: Active-row versus stored-pool state semantics need a solver-oriented reference.
standard_field_rationale: an active constraint set is represented by intersection with its inequality halfspaces.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct role, and the halfspace-intersection formula is mathematically coherent. No cited source establishes the interface distinction between currently enforced rows and cuts merely retained in storage, which is the terminal container's substantive claim.

children.title: Global Reusable Cut Pools
children.top_down_role: Globally valid cuts retained outside the current relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Reusable Cut Pools
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A repository of globally valid cuts eligible for reuse throughout the search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the global feasible set. A global reusable cut pool is a finite or locally finite indexed collection \(G=\{(a_i,\beta_i,m_i):i\in I\}\), where every stored inequality satisfies \[a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta_i\quad\text{for all }x\in F,\] and \(m_i\) contains retrieval metadata. A cut in \(G\) is eligible for activation at any search node whose variables and formulation mapping support the row, although eligibility does not require immediate activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global pool stores cuts valid for every globally feasible point, together with metadata enabling their reuse at compatible search nodes.
assumptions_latex: Every stored row is expressed in, or mapped consistently to, the global variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\subseteq\{(a,\beta,m):a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\text{ for all }x\in F\}\).
review_flags: The provided valid-cut locator does not establish global-pool lifecycle semantics.
standard_field_rationale: global reuse requires validity over the global feasible set and formulation compatibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the leaf, and global validity over the feasible set is the appropriate core requirement. A source is needed for reusable-pool eligibility, metadata, and formulation-mapping semantics. The alternative 'finite or locally finite indexed collection' is also undefined for this abstract indexed pool and should be justified or replaced by a sourced storage model.

children.title: Cut Promotion Between Pool States
children.top_down_role: Movement of reusable cuts into or out of the active row set.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Promotion Between Pool States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A guarded transition from local or inactive storage to broader reusable or active status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a stored cut \(c=(a,\beta)\), its current state \(q\), validity domain \(D(c)\), and target state \(q'\). First verify the target guard: promotion to the global pool requires \(F\subseteq D(c)\), while promotion to active rows at node \(v\) requires \(F_v\subseteq D(c)\) and formulation compatibility. If the guard holds, insert \(c\) into the target collection, preserve its validity metadata, and set \(q\leftarrow q'\); otherwise leave the state unchanged. Duplicate-equivalent target rows may be merged without changing the validity guard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut moves to a broader or active state only after its validity domain and formulation compatibility satisfy the target state's guard.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the global feasible set and \(F_v\subseteq F\) is the node-feasible set.
\(D(c)\) records a certified validity domain for the cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q'=\mathrm{global}\Rightarrow F\subseteq D(c)\), and \(q'=\mathrm{active}(v)\Rightarrow F_v\subseteq D(c)\).

notation.meaning: certified validity domain of cut c

review_flags: Promotion states, metadata preservation, and duplicate handling require an implementation reference.
standard_field_rationale: widening a cut's availability is sound only when its certified validity domain contains the target scope.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role for a guarded promotion transition. No source supports the state model, metadata preservation, compatibility guard, or duplicate merging. Moreover, q' is introduced as a requested target, so the conclusion incorrectly reads its implications as unconditional even when promotion fails; a sourced version must distinguish the requested target from the resulting state.

children.title: Local-Cut Scope Interface
children.top_down_role: Management of cuts valid only within restricted search regions.

children.title: Local-Cut Storage
children.top_down_role: Retention of cuts associated with restricted search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Cut Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scope-annotated representation of cuts valid only within designated search-tree regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A locally stored cut is represented by a tuple \[\ell=(a,\beta,r,\sigma,m),\] where \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) is the row, \(r\) is its owning search node, \(\sigma\) describes its validity scope, and \(m\) contains lifecycle metadata. A local-cut store is an indexed collection \(L\) of such tuples satisfying \(F_v\subseteq D(\sigma)\) for every node \(v\) at which \(\ell\) may be retrieved. The row and its scope descriptor must be stored inseparably.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each local cut is stored with an owner, validity-scope descriptor, and lifecycle metadata so retrieval cannot discard its limited validity.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\) denotes the feasible set under node-v restrictions.
\(D(\sigma)\) is the domain encoded by scope descriptor \(\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\subseteq\{(a,\beta,r,\sigma,m):F_v\subseteq D(\sigma)\text{ at every eligible node }v\}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifies a canonical local-cut storage tuple.
standard_field_rationale: safe local storage binds each inequality to explicit scope and lifecycle metadata.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct content kind for a scope-annotated storage tuple. The tuple fields and inseparable-storage requirement are uncited implementation choices. The statement also relies on D(sigma) being a certified domain on which the stored inequality is valid, but that relationship is not explicitly introduced and needs source-backed definition.

children.title: Local-Cut Validity Scope
children.top_down_role: Search regions within which stored local cuts remain valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Cut Validity Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity relative to the feasible region of a node and its eligible descendants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the global feasible set and let \(B_v\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) encode the branching restrictions at node \(v\), so \(F_v=F\cap B_v\). An inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) is local-valid at \(v\) when \[a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\quad\text{for every }x\in F_v.\] Its validity scope contains precisely those nodes \(w\) for which \(F_w\subseteq\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\}\); in particular, validity propagates to descendants satisfying \(F_w\subseteq F_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is local-valid at a node when all feasible points satisfying that node's branching restrictions obey it; validity passes to nested descendant regions.
assumptions_latex: A descendant \(w\) under consideration satisfies \(F_w\subseteq F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) for all \(x\in F_v\), hence also for all \(x\in F_w\subseteq F_v\).
review_flags: The supplied locators cover valid cuts generally but not node-local validity scope.
standard_field_rationale: validity on a set is universal satisfaction, and it is inherited by subsets.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct role, and validity on F_v with inheritance by subsets is mathematically precise. Nevertheless, the record cites no inspectable source for the branch-and-bound interpretation of node-local validity and descendant scope, so it cannot pass citation review as submitted.

children.title: Scope-Aware Cut Retrieval
children.top_down_role: Reuse of local cuts only in compatible search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Scope-Aware Cut Retrieval
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retrieval filters stored local cuts by certified validity at the requesting node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a requesting node \(v\), its feasible-region descriptor, and a local-cut store \(L\). For each stored tuple \(\ell=(a,\beta,r,\sigma,m)\), evaluate whether the scope predicate \(F_v\subseteq D(\sigma)\) is certified and whether the row is formulation-compatible at \(v\). Return \[Q(v)=\{\ell\in L:F_v\subseteq D(\sigma_\ell)\text{ and }\ell\text{ is compatible at }v\}.\] Cuts for which containment is false or uncertified are excluded; ranking or budget filters may subsequently select a subset of \(Q(v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retrieval returns only stored cuts whose recorded scope certifiably contains the requesting node's feasible region and whose row representation is compatible.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\ell\in L\) has a retained scope descriptor \(\sigma_\ell\).
Scope containment is checked by a sound certificate procedure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(v)\subseteq\{\ell\in L:F_v\subseteq D(\sigma_\ell)\}\).

notation.meaning: validity domain recorded for cut l
cuts eligible for retrieval at node v

review_flags: A source is needed for scope-certificate and formulation-compatibility retrieval semantics.
standard_field_rationale: sound retrieval filters by certified containment of the request region in each cut's validity domain.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the retrieval leaf, and the returned-set formula matches the plain statement. A source is required for the scope certificate, formulation-compatibility test, treatment of uncertified containment, and ordering relative to ranking and budget filters.

children.title: Cut Lifecycle Policy Family
children.top_down_role: Removal and later reuse of inactive or costly cuts.

children.title: Cut Aging Policies
children.top_down_role: Inactivity measures used to track declining cut utility.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Aging Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An inactivity counter used to identify cuts that have not recently influenced relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each managed cut \(c\), maintain an integer age \(g_t(c)\ge 0\) after solve \(t\). Given an activity predicate \(A_t(c)\), update \[g_{t+1}(c)=\begin{cases}0,&A_t(c)=1,\\ g_t(c)+1,&A_t(c)=0.\end{cases}\] The predicate may declare activity from binding status, sufficiently small slack, or another fixed influence test, but its definition must remain consistent during the aging interval. Age changes metadata only; reaching an age threshold makes \(c\) eligible for a later lifecycle action and does not itself invalidate the inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut's age resets when the declared activity test succeeds and otherwise increases; threshold age creates lifecycle eligibility, not mathematical invalidity.
assumptions_latex: \(A_t(c)\in\{0,1\}\) is evaluated after each charged solve.

notation.meaning: age of cut c after solve t

review_flags: Activity tests and aging intervals vary among solvers and need an implementation source.
standard_field_rationale: aging is conventionally modeled by reset-on-use and increment-on-inactivity counters.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate role, and the reset-or-increment recurrence is internally consistent. The activity predicate, charged-solve interval, threshold interpretation, and assertion that aging changes metadata only are solver-policy conventions without a cited source.

children.title: Cut Deletion Policies
children.top_down_role: Removal choices for inactive, costly, or low-value cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Deletion Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A guarded policy for removing expendable cuts from active or stored states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a managed cut set \(C_t\), ages \(g_t(c)\), a deletion threshold \(G\), a protected subset \(P_t\), and a capacity target \(K\). Form the eligible set \[E_t=\{c\in C_t\setminus P_t:g_t(c)\ge G\}.\] If \(|C_t|>K\), select \(D_t\subseteq E_t\) using a fixed priority rule and remove enough cuts to obtain \(|C_t\setminus D_t|\le K\), whenever \(|E_t|\) permits. Deletion removes the chosen state record or active row; it neither asserts that the cut is invalid nor permits deletion of protected base constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When capacity is exceeded, sufficiently old unprotected cuts are removed by a declared priority rule; deletion does not imply invalidity.
assumptions_latex: \(P_t\subseteq C_t\) contains all rows forbidden from deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_t\subseteq E_t\) and, when feasible, \(|C_t\setminus D_t|\le K\).
review_flags: Deletion priorities, protected categories, and state-removal semantics require a solver-oriented source.
standard_field_rationale: capacity-driven deletion is a guarded selection from old, explicitly unprotected records.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits Cut Deletion Policies, and the eligible-set construction is coherent. No citation supports the age threshold, protected categories, priority rule, or state-removal semantics. The phrase 'whenever |E_t| permits' should also be replaced by the explicit condition |E_t| >= |C_t|-K in a sourced formulation.

children.title: Cut Reactivation Policies
children.top_down_role: Return of previously inactive cuts to computational use.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Reactivation Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-and-budget policy for restoring dormant valid inequalities to an active relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an active cut set \(A\), a dormant pool \(D\), a relaxation solution \(\bar x\), violation threshold \(\tau\ge 0\), and budget \(K\in\mathbb Z_+\). For each cut \(i\in D\), written \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), compute \(v_i=a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b_i\). Order cuts with \(v_i>\tau\) by nonincreasing violation, using a fixed deterministic tie rule. Move the first \(\min\{K,|\{i\in D:v_i>\tau\}|\}\) cuts from \(D\) to \(A\). If no violation exceeds \(\tau\), leave both sets unchanged. The output is the updated active set and dormant pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reactivate at most K dormant cuts whose violations exceed a threshold, prioritizing the largest violations and applying a deterministic tie rule.
assumptions_latex: Every cut in \(D\) is valid for the intended feasible set.
Violations are evaluated using a common scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated active relaxation contains every selected cut and therefore excludes \(\bar x\) whenever at least one selected cut has positive violation.

notation.meaning: signed violation of dormant cut i at the current point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the reactivation-policy leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source supports this specific threshold-and-budget cut-pool policy.

children.title: Deletion–Reactivation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Memory, solution effort, plus future reuse consequences across the cut lifecycle.

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion–Reactivation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-recovery principle distinguishing safe dormancy from irreversible cut deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a finite family of valid cuts and let \(A\subseteq C\) be active. Suppose every cut in \(C\setminus A\) remains recoverable and, before a candidate \(x\) is accepted, all dormant cuts are tested and every violated one is reactivated. Then \(x\) is accepted exactly when it satisfies every cut in \(C\). Thus dormancy can reduce the simultaneously active formulation without changing the acceptance set, but it transfers work to pool storage and violation scans. Permanent deletion lacks this equivalence unless deleted cuts can be regenerated or are implied by the retained relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dormancy preserves the full cut system if every dormant cut is checked before acceptance; permanent deletion is safe only with regeneration or implication.
assumptions_latex: The family \(C\) is finite and its dormant members are recoverable.
Violation tests are exact and performed before acceptance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The acceptance set equals \(\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\text{ for every }i\in C\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle correctly distinguishes recoverable dormancy from permanent deletion and fits the tradeoff leaf, but it has no cited source.

children.title: Verifiable Cut Reliability System
children.top_down_role: Numerical controls and exact certificates supporting trustworthy cut validity.

children.title: Cut Representation Conditioning Calculus
children.top_down_role: Representation controls for magnitude, density, and cut comparison.

children.title: Cut Scaling
children.top_down_role: Coefficient magnitude management for stable cut representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive rescaling equivalence for a single linear valid inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) be valid for \(S\). For every scalar \(s>0\), the scaled inequality \((sa)^{\mathsf T}x\le s\beta\) has exactly the same satisfying set and is valid for \(S\). Scaling by \(s=0\) destroys the represented halfspace, while scaling by \(s<0\) reverses the inequality direction unless the relation is rewritten. Consequently, positive scaling may change coefficient magnitudes and numerical behavior but cannot change exact separation, dominance, or validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying both sides of a cut by a positive scalar preserves its halfspace and validity, although it can alter numerical conditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\}=\{x:(sa)^{\mathsf T}x\le s\beta\}\), and the scaled inequality is valid for \(S\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-scaling property is precise and standard, but the record supplies neither an authoritative citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Cut Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonical representations supporting reliable cut comparison.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical positive scaling of a nonzero linear cut under a selected norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). For a cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) with \(a\ne0\), its norm-normalized representation is \(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x\le\hat\beta\), where \(s=1/\|a\|\), \(\hat a=sa\), and \(\hat\beta=s\beta\). Then \(\|\hat a\|=1\), and positive scaling equivalence gives the same halfspace. To make the representation unique when sign-equivalent equality descriptions are involved, an additional fixed sign convention must be specified; no sign change is permitted for a one-sided inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize a nonzero cut by positively scaling its coefficient vector to unit norm, preserving the represented halfspace.
assumptions_latex: A norm on \(\mathbb R^n\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\hat a\|=1\) and \(\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\}=\{x:\hat a^{\mathsf T}x\le\hat\beta\}\).

notation.meaning: normalized cut coefficients and right-hand side

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly uses positive norm normalization for a nonzero inequality, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Cut Sparsification
children.top_down_role: Density reduction subject to validity plus numerical quality requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Sparsification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function test guaranteeing validity after coefficients are removed or modified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) be valid for \(S\), and let \(\tilde a\) be a sparsified coefficient vector. The replacement \(\tilde a^{\mathsf T}x\le\tilde\beta\) is valid precisely when \(\sup_{x\in S}\tilde a^{\mathsf T}x\le\tilde\beta\). A sufficient perturbation test is obtained by writing \(\tilde a=a+d\): if a certified bound \(U\ge\sup_{x\in S}d^{\mathsf T}x\) is available, then choosing \(\tilde\beta=\beta+U\) preserves validity. Merely setting small coefficients to zero while leaving \(\beta\) unchanged need not satisfy this condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparsified cut remains valid when its right-hand side bounds the new support function; a certified perturbation bound supplies a safe adjustment.
assumptions_latex: The original inequality is valid for \(S\).
The relevant support supremum or a valid upper bound is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U\ge\sup_{x\in S}(\tilde a-a)^{\mathsf T}x\), then \(\tilde a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta+U\) is valid for \(S\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-function condition and perturbation allowance are mathematically sound and fit the sparsification leaf, but no source supports the formulation.

children.title: Representation Quality Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions among coefficient magnitude, density, comparability, plus cut strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Quality Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact validity versus sparsity, coefficient size, and numerical separation margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equivalent positive scalings of \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\), the exact halfspace is invariant, but raw violation \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x-\beta\) and coefficient magnitudes scale together. Hence violation rankings are representation-dependent unless a common normalization is used. Sparsification can reduce storage and evaluation cost, but it preserves validity only with a certified right-hand-side adjustment or a direct validity check; such adjustment may weaken separation. Therefore representation quality must distinguish exact halfspace equivalence, normalized efficacy, sparsity, encoding size, and numerical conditioning rather than optimize a single raw coefficient measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling changes raw numerical scores, while sparsification can improve compactness but require weakening; representation quality therefore needs several separate criteria.
assumptions_latex: Cuts are linear inequalities over a common ambient space.
Comparisons use exact arithmetic unless numerical conditioning is explicitly assessed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Raw violation is not scaling-invariant, whereas normalized efficacy \((a^{\mathsf T}\bar x-\beta)/\|a\|\) is invariant under positive scaling.

notation.meaning: point at which cut efficacy is evaluated

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation tradeoffs and scaling-invariance claim are coherent, but the solver-oriented claims about storage, evaluation cost, efficacy, and conditioning require a specific source.

children.title: Validity-Preserving Coefficient Cleanup
children.top_down_role: Validity-preserving treatment of approximate coefficients.

children.title: Validity-Preserving Coefficient Rounding
children.top_down_role: Controlled rounding of approximate cut coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Preserving Coefficient Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe coefficient rounding over a bounded domain using a certified perturbation allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and suppose \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) is valid for \(S\). Let the rounded coefficient vector be \(\hat a=a+d\). If finite bounds \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\) hold for every \(x\in S\), define \(U(d)=\sum_{j=1}^n\max\{d_j\ell_j,d_j u_j\}\). Then the rounded inequality \(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta+U(d)\) is valid for \(S\). Retaining the unadjusted right-hand side \(\beta\) is justified only if \(U(d)\le0\) is certified or validity is verified independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient rounding is safe when the right-hand side absorbs a certified worst-case rounding error over the bounded feasible domain.
assumptions_latex: Finite bounds \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\) hold for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta+U(d)\) is valid for \(S\).

notation.meaning: box-based upper bound on rounding error

children.title: Coefficient Cleanup
children.top_down_role: Removal or adjustment of numerically insignificant coefficient artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Cleanup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified cleanup pipeline for scaling, rounding, and removing negligible coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a valid cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\), certified bounds \(\ell\le x\le u\) on the intended feasible set \(S\), a positive scaling factor \(s>0\), and a cleanup map. Form \(a'=sa\) and \(\beta'=s\beta\). Apply the cleanup map to obtain \(\hat a=a'+d\), and compute \(U(d)=\sum_j\max\{d_j\ell_j,d_j u_j\}\). Output \(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta'+U(d)\), optionally followed by a common positive normalization. If a required variable bound or the perturbation computation is uncertified, reject the cleanup candidate or submit it to an exact validity check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positively scale the cut, simplify its coefficients, compensate for the certified worst-case perturbation over the variable bounds, and reject uncertified candidates.
assumptions_latex: The input inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) is valid for \(S\).
Finite certified bounds \(\ell_j\le x_j\le u_j\) cover every modified coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the bounds and perturbation computation are certified, then \(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta'+U(d)\) is valid for \(S\).

notation.meaning: aggregate cleanup perturbation relative to the scaled coefficients

children.title: Post-Cleanup Validity Assessment
children.top_down_role: Verification of cut validity after coefficient treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Post-Cleanup Validity Assessment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-bound certificate for accepting a cleaned linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) be valid for \(S\), and let \(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x\le\hat\beta\) be a cleaned candidate. A post-cleanup validity certificate is a rigorously computed number \(U\) satisfying \(U\ge\sup_{x\in S}(\hat a-a)^{\mathsf T}x\), together with the verified inequality \(\hat\beta\ge\beta+U\). Possession of this certificate establishes that the cleaned candidate is valid for \(S\); failure to obtain it leaves validity unestablished.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cleaned cut is certified valid when a rigorous perturbation bound fits within its right-hand-side allowance; absence of that certificate leaves validity unestablished.
assumptions_latex: The original cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) is valid for \(S\).
The bound \(U\) and the comparison \(\hat\beta\ge\beta+U\) are verified with rigorous arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((U,\hat\beta\ge\beta+U)\) certifies validity of \(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x\le\hat\beta\) for \(S\).

notation.meaning: certified support bound for the cleanup perturbation

children.title: Exact Cut Recovery Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Exact recovery or validation of cuts generated numerically.

children.title: Rational Coefficient Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of rational cut coefficients from numerical approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Rational Coefficient Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-denominator recovery of exact rational cut data from floating-point approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input approximations \(y_1,\ldots,y_m\in\mathbb R\), a denominator bound \(Q\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). For each \(y_k\), enumerate or compute by continued fractions the reduced rational \(p_k/q_k\) with \(1\le q_k\le Q\) and \(|y_k-p_k/q_k|\le\varepsilon\). Accept only if exactly one such rational exists for every component; otherwise report failure. Assemble the recovered coefficients and right-hand side, clear denominators by their positive least common multiple if desired, and submit the resulting exact inequality to an independent validity check before installation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover each approximate coefficient as a unique bounded-denominator rational, then validate the assembled exact cut independently.
assumptions_latex: A denominator bound \(Q\) and error tolerance \(\varepsilon\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On success, the output is the unique componentwise rational vector satisfying the stated denominator and tolerance constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-denominator uniqueness rule fits rational reconstruction, but the claim that the required rational can be computed by continued fractions is not sourced or specified sufficiently to assess the intended algorithmic variant.

children.title: Exact Cut Validity Checks
children.top_down_role: Exact assessment of reconstructed or numerically generated cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Cut Validity Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Farkas-multiplier certificate for validity over a rational polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) be a nonempty rational polyhedron, and let \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) be a rational inequality. The inequality is valid for \(P\) if and only if there exists a rational vector \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=a\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}\lambda\le\beta\). Such a multiplier, with all relations checked in exact rational arithmetic, is an exact validity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational cut is valid over a nonempty rational polyhedron exactly when it has a nonnegative rational Farkas aggregation certificate checked in exact arithmetic.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) is a nonempty rational polyhedron.
The data \(a,\beta\) and certificate arithmetic are rational and exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut is valid for \(P\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=a\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}\lambda\le\beta\).

notation.meaning: rational polyhedron defined by the base inequalities

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11

children.title: Reconstruction Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity, instability, or excessive size limiting reliable exact recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness and invalidity boundaries for bounded-denominator rational recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Bounded-denominator reconstruction cannot be certified when the tolerance neighborhood contains two admissible rationals. For \(Q\ge2\), the distinct reduced rationals \(1/Q\) and \(1/(Q-1)\) differ by \(1/(Q(Q-1))\). At their midpoint \(y\), both lie within \(1/(2Q(Q-1))\). Thus any componentwise rule allowing \(\varepsilon\ge1/(2Q(Q-1))\) can be ambiguous on this example. Even unique coefficient recovery does not establish cut validity: reconstruction transfers approximate data to exact rational data, whereas validity still requires an independent certificate over the intended feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction fails when multiple bounded-denominator rationals fit the tolerance, and unique recovery alone never certifies cut validity.
assumptions_latex: Reconstruction accepts every rational within tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(y=\tfrac12(1/Q+1/(Q-1))\), uniqueness fails whenever \(\varepsilon\ge1/(2Q(Q-1))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ambiguity example is correct and the failure-boundary content kind fits the leaf, but no authoritative rational-reconstruction or rational-separation source is supplied.

children.title: Verifiable Cut Certificates
children.top_down_role: Independently checkable certificates for generated cuts and final bounds.

assumptions_latex: A cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal P\) has an exact rational verifier for every inference rule.
The initial rational system and claimed terminal bound are part of the verifier input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance certifies that every recorded cut is valid for the preceding relaxation and that the terminal inequality proves the claimed bound.

notation.meaning: Cutting-plane proof system and its exact verifier
Sequence of cuts with rule witnesses

knowledge_statements.scope_note: System-parameterized certificate covering local cut validity and the terminal bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A verifiable cut certificate for a rational instance \(F\) is a finite transcript \(\pi=((a_i,b_i,w_i))_{i=1}^L\), together with a terminal bound witness, such that an exact checker confirms for every \(i\) that \(w_i\) establishes \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) by an allowed rule of \(\mathcal P\) from \(F\) and earlier accepted cuts. The checker additionally verifies that the terminal system implies the claimed objective bound or infeasibility assertion. Acceptance uses exact rational arithmetic and entails validity of every cut and of the final claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate records each cut, its rule witness, and a terminal bound witness; exact independent checking certifies all local inferences and the final claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Verifiable Cut Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf, but soundness depends on the precise inference rules, witness formats, and method used to certify terminal implication. No source is supplied for those substantive conventions.

children.title: Cutting-Plane Proof Complexity
children.top_down_role: Cut sequences viewed as finite certificates and measured by rank, length, and encoding.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: Proof Length-Rank Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Sequence length and closure depth as proof-system measures.

children.title: Proof Length Complexity
children.top_down_role: Derivation size measured through the number of proof lines or cuts.

assumptions_latex: A cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal P\) and a finite rational instance \(F\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proof-length complexity is \(L_{\mathcal P}(F)=\min\{|\pi|:\pi\text{ is a }\mathcal P\text{-refutation of }F\}\), with value \(+\infty\) when no refutation exists.

notation.meaning: Number of derived inequalities in a proof
Minimum proof length for the instance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Number of derived inequalities, excluding encoding size and arithmetic cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal P\), the length of a proof \(\pi\) is the number \(|\pi|\) of derived inequalities, counting repeated derivations separately and excluding the initial inequalities. For an infeasible rational instance \(F\), its proof-length complexity is \[L_{\mathcal P}(F)=\min\{\,|\pi|: \pi\text{ is a valid }\mathcal P\text{-refutation of }F\,\}.\] If no such refutation exists, set \(L_{\mathcal P}(F)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof-length complexity is the minimum number of derived inequalities in a refutation of the instance under the fixed cutting-plane system.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof Length Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a suitable definition of proof-length complexity, but whether initial inequalities are excluded and repeated derivations are counted is proof-system-specific and presently uncited.

children.title: Rank Complexity
children.top_down_role: Closure depth required to obtain target inequalities.

assumptions_latex: A cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal P\) has a specified round structure or closure operator.
A finite rational instance \(F\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rank complexity is \(R_{\mathcal P}(F)=\min\{r:\mathcal P^r(F)=\varnothing\}\), or \(+\infty\) if no finite round refutes \(F\).

notation.meaning: Relaxation after applying all permitted cuts for r rounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel-round rank for a fixed cutting-plane closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P^0(F)\) denote the initial relaxation and let \(\mathcal P^{r+1}(F)\) be obtained by adding every cut permitted by one application of the fixed closure rule to \(\mathcal P^r(F)\). For infeasible \(F\), its rank complexity is \[R_{\mathcal P}(F)=\min\{\,r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:\mathcal P^r(F)=\varnothing\,\}.\] Equivalently, it is the least number of sequential closure rounds needed for a refutation; it is \(+\infty\) if no finite round suffices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank complexity is the least number of sequential cutting-plane closure rounds required to make the relaxation empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits rank complexity, but the closure operator, parallel-round convention, and applicability to the stated instance class require an authoritative source.

children.title: Length–Rank Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Proof families exhibiting contrasting derivation length versus closure depth.

assumptions_latex: A cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal P\) assigns every proof a length and a rank.
A finite rational instance \(F\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(L_F(r)\) is nonincreasing, and its finite points give the Pareto tradeoff between proof length and rank.

notation.meaning: Length and rank of a proof
Minimum length subject to rank at most r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-wise Pareto profile for bounded-rank refutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The length-rank tradeoff of \(F\) in \(\mathcal P\) is represented by \[L_F(r)=\min\{\,\ell(\pi):\pi\text{ refutes }F\text{ and }\rho(\pi)\le r\,\},\] with \(L_F(r)=+\infty\) when the feasible set of proofs is empty. Because every proof of rank at most \(r\) is also admissible at rank \(r+1\), \(L_F(r+1)\le L_F(r)\). The nondominated pairs \((\rho(\pi),\ell(\pi))\) form the Pareto frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tradeoff profile gives the shortest refutation allowed at each rank budget; increasing the rank budget cannot increase minimum length.
knowledge_statements.title: Length–Rank Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto-profile representation and monotonicity statement are mathematically coherent, but the rank assigned to individual proofs and the bounded-rank proof class are not sourced.

children.title: Coefficient-Encoding Complexity Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Certificate size measured through coefficient growth and finite encoding.

children.title: Coefficient Magnitude Complexity
children.top_down_role: Growth of coefficient magnitudes within cutting-plane certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Magnitude Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Magnitude after primitive-integral normalization of a rational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\le \beta\) be a rational inequality. Let \(D\) be the least positive integer for which \((D\alpha,D\beta)\in\mathbb Z^{n+1}\), let \(g\) be the positive greatest common divisor of the entries of \((D\alpha,D\beta)\), and set \((a,b)=(D\alpha,D\beta)/g\). The coefficient magnitude of the inequality is \[M(a,b)=\|(a,b)\|_\infty=\max\{|a_1|,\ldots,|a_n|,|b|\}.\] For a proof \(\pi\), its coefficient-magnitude complexity is the maximum of \(M(a,b)\) over all inequalities written in \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert each rational inequality to its primitive integer form using positive scaling. Its coefficient magnitude is the largest absolute coefficient, including the right-hand side; proof complexity is the largest such magnitude among its lines.
assumptions_latex: The inequality is represented with a fixed relation orientation, and normalization uses only positive scaling.
Every proof line is a rational inequality with finitely many coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized inequality has coefficient magnitude \(M(a,b)=\max\{|a_1|,\ldots,|a_n|,|b|\}\), and a proof's coefficient-magnitude complexity is the maximum of this quantity over its lines.

notation.meaning: Original rational coefficient vector including the right-hand side
Primitive integral coefficient vector obtained by positive scaling

source_refs.locator: 3.13 Encoding Size of Vertices, Extreme Rays, and Facets p. 112

source_witnesses.locator: 3.13 Encoding Size of Vertices, Extreme Rays, and Facets p. 112

children.title: Coefficient Bit Complexity
children.top_down_role: Finite representation cost of individual cut coefficients.

assumptions_latex: Coefficients are represented as primitive signed integers in binary.
Variable indices and proof-rule metadata are accounted for separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient bit complexity is \(B(a,b)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\ell_{\mathbb Z}(a_j)+\ell_{\mathbb Z}(b)\), where \(\ell_{\mathbb Z}(z)=1+\lceil\log_2(|z|+1)\rceil\).

notation.meaning: Signed binary length of an integer
Total coefficient bit length of one inequality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense signed-binary encoding of normalized integer coefficients.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primitive integral inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), define the signed binary length of \(z\in\mathbb Z\) by \(\ell_{\mathbb Z}(z)=1+\lceil\log_2(|z|+1)\rceil\). Its coefficient bit complexity is \[B(a,b)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\ell_{\mathbb Z}(a_j)+\ell_{\mathbb Z}(b).\] The coefficient bit complexity of a proof is the sum of \(B(a,b)\) over its written inequalities; rule identifiers, indices, and witnesses contribute additional encoding cost when total certificate size is measured.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient bit complexity sums the signed binary lengths of all normalized integer coefficients; proof coefficient complexity sums this quantity over all proof lines.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Bit Complexity

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

children.title: Certificate Encoding Size
children.top_down_role: Aggregate storage required for a complete cutting-plane certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Encoding Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total binary size, including coefficients and inference witnesses, under a fixed self-delimiting transcript encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a proof certificate be \(\pi=(d_1,\ldots,d_L)\), where each derivation record \(d_i\) contains a derived inequality, its inference-rule identifier, antecedent indices, and every rational or integral witness required by the verifier. Fix a self-delimiting binary encoding for records and define \(\operatorname{enc}(\pi)\) to be the concatenation of \(\operatorname{enc}(d_1),\ldots,\operatorname{enc}(d_L)\). Its certificate encoding size is \[S(\pi)=|\operatorname{enc}(\pi)|=\sum_{i=1}^{L}|\operatorname{enc}(d_i)|.\] Thus \(S(\pi)\) includes coefficient bits, record delimiters, indices, rule metadata, and witness data, and it need not be bounded by the number of proof lines alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a fixed self-delimiting record format, certificate encoding size is the total number of bits in the concatenated proof records, including coefficients, indices, rule metadata, delimiters, and witnesses.
assumptions_latex: A fixed self-delimiting binary encoding is specified for every derivation record.
A proof transcript \(\pi=(d_1,\ldots,d_L)\) contains finitely many derivation records.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate encoding size is \(S(\pi)=|\operatorname{enc}(\pi)|=\sum_{i=1}^{L}|\operatorname{enc}(d_i)|\) bits.

notation.meaning: Concatenated self-delimiting binary encoding of the proof certificate

children.title: Magnitude–Encoding Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Connections between coefficient growth plus overall certificate size.

assumptions_latex: A normalized inequality has \(d\ge1\) primitive integer entries including its right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(M=\max_i|q_i|\) and \(B=\sum_i\ell_{\mathbb Z}(q_i)\), then \(d+\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\le B\le d(1+\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil)\).

notation.meaning: Maximum coefficient magnitude and total bit length

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elementary comparison under the stated dense signed-binary convention.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.1 Problems, Instances, Encoding Size p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q=(q_1,
\ldots,q_d)\in\mathbb Z^d\), let \(M=\max_i|q_i|\), and let \(B=\sum_{i=1}^d\ell_{\mathbb Z}(q_i)\). Then \[d+\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\le B\le d\bigl(1+\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\bigr).\] Hence bounded magnitude gives a linear-in-\(d\) bit bound, while a bit bound \(B\) implies \(M<2^B\). Magnitude alone does not measure certificate size because the number of coefficients and proof lines also contribute.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed number of coefficients, binary encoding grows logarithmically with maximum magnitude; total certificate size also depends on dimension and proof length.

children.title: Cutting-Plane Proof Hardness Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Families requiring large rank, long derivations, or large coefficients.

children.title: Proof-Length Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Instance families forcing long cutting-plane derivations.

assumptions_latex: A cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal P\) and an indexed family of infeasible instances \((F_n)\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A function \(g\) is a proof-length lower bound when \(L_{\mathcal P}(F_n)\ge g(n)\) for every relevant \(n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family-wise lower bound relative to a fixed proof system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proof-length lower bound \(g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) for a family \((F_n)\) in \(\mathcal P\) is the assertion \[L_{\mathcal P}(F_n)\ge g(n)\] for every index \(n\) in the family. Equivalently, every valid \(\mathcal P\)-refutation of \(F_n\) contains at least \(g(n)\) derived inequalities. The parameter \(n\), the instance encoding, the permitted inference rules, and whether auxiliary variables are allowed must remain fixed when interpreting asymptotic bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof-length lower bound states that every refutation of each family member requires at least a specified number of derived inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof-Length Lower Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind and family-wise formulation fit the leaf, but no source supports the line-count convention or the proof-system-relative lower-bound framework.

children.title: Rank Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Instance families requiring large cutting-plane rank.

assumptions_latex: A cutting-plane closure \(\mathcal P\) and an indexed family of infeasible instances \((F_n)\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A function \(r\) is a rank lower bound when \(R_{\mathcal P}(F_n)\ge r(n)\) for every relevant \(n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family-wise lower bound for sequential closure depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rank lower bound \(r:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) for a family \((F_n)\) under closure \(\mathcal P\) is the assertion \[R_{\mathcal P}(F_n)\ge r(n)\] for every relevant \(n\). Thus fewer than \(r(n)\) successive applications of the closure cannot derive infeasibility. The bound concerns dependency depth rather than the number of inequalities: arbitrarily many cuts may be generated within one round without reducing the required rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank lower bound says that no refutation can make an instance empty in fewer than a specified number of sequential closure rounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Lower Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement has the correct role and is internally coherent, but its sequential closure-round interpretation requires a sourced, instantiated closure definition.

children.title: Coefficient-Size Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Instance families forcing large coefficients or encodings.

assumptions_latex: A cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal P\) and an indexed family of infeasible rational instances \((F_n)\) are fixed.
Every proof inequality uses primitive integral normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A function \(h\) is a coefficient-size lower bound when every refutation \(\pi\) of \(F_n\) satisfies \(\max_{q\in\pi}\|q\|_\infty\ge h(n)\).

notation.meaning: Primitive coefficient vector of a proof inequality, including its right-hand side

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum-magnitude lower bound under primitive normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coefficient-size lower bound \(h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) for \((F_n)\) in \(\mathcal P\) asserts that every refutation \(\pi\) of \(F_n\) obeys \[\max\{\,\|q\|_\infty:q\text{ is the primitive coefficient vector of a line of }\pi\,\}\ge h(n).\] Consequently, every refutation contains some coefficient whose signed binary representation requires at least \(1+\lceil\log_2(h(n)+1)\rceil\) bits. The statement depends on the normalization and permitted extension rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coefficient-size lower bound forces every refutation to contain at least one normalized inequality with a coefficient of the stated magnitude.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Size Lower Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximum-magnitude lower-bound formulation fits the leaf, but its meaning changes with normalization, auxiliary-variable rules, and allowed extensions; no authoritative source fixes those conventions.

children.title: Hard Proof Families
children.top_down_role: Canonical families witnessing cutting-plane proof difficulty.

assumptions_latex: A cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal P\), an instance-size measure \(s(F)\), and a complexity measure \(C_{\mathcal P}(F)\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is hard when \(C_{\mathcal P}(F_n)\ge g(s(F_n))\) for all relevant \(n\), for a declared lower-bound function \(g\).

notation.meaning: Binary input size of an instance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hardness is relative to a proof system, size parameter, and declared resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An indexed family \((F_n)\) is hard for \(\mathcal P\) with respect to resource \(C\) and growth function \(g\) if \[C_{\mathcal P}(F_n)\ge g(s(F_n))\] for every relevant \(n\), where \(s(F_n)\) is the binary input size. The resource \(C\) may be minimum proof length, minimum rank, minimum unavoidable coefficient magnitude, or certificate encoding size, but it must be fixed in the claim. Polynomial, superpolynomial, or exponential hardness refers to the corresponding growth of \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard proof family has a declared proof resource growing at least as a specified function of binary instance size under a fixed proof system.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard Proof Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly makes hardness relative to a proof system, resource, size measure, and growth function, but no source supports this taxonomy or the listed resource variants.

children.title: Simultaneous Proof Hardness
children.top_down_role: Families hard under multiple proof-complexity measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Proof Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint lower bounds for three resources in a fixed cutting-plane proof system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a cutting-plane proof system \(\mathcal S\). For an instance \(I\), let \(L_{\mathcal S}(I,\pi)\), \(R_{\mathcal S}(I,\pi)\), and \(B_{\mathcal S}(I,\pi)\) denote the length, rank, and maximum coefficient bit-length of a proof \(\pi\). A family \((I_n)_{n\ge1}\) has simultaneous hardness bounds \((\ell_n,r_n,b_n)\) if every \(\mathcal S\)-proof \(\pi\) of \(I_n\) satisfies \[L_{\mathcal S}(I_n,\pi)\ge \ell_n,\qquad R_{\mathcal S}(I_n,\pi)\ge r_n,\qquad B_{\mathcal S}(I_n,\pi)\ge b_n.\] The quantification over one common proof distinguishes simultaneous hardness from separate lower bounds attained by different proofs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every proof of each instance must simultaneously have large length, large rank, and large coefficient encoding size.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) and all three resource measures are fixed uniformly over the family.
Each \(I_n\) has at least one finite \(\mathcal S\)-proof.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall n\,\forall \pi:\ L_{\mathcal S}(I_n,\pi)\ge\ell_n,\ R_{\mathcal S}(I_n,\pi)\ge r_n,\ B_{\mathcal S}(I_n,\pi)\ge b_n.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No evidence supports this proof-system-independent resource definition. Moreover, separate universal lower bounds on length, rank, and coefficient size are logically equivalent to their conjunction over a common proof, so the asserted distinction from separate lower bounds requires a different quantifier or tradeoff formulation. The exact proof system and appropriate role—definition or complexity bound rather than a generic property—also require authoritative support.

children.title: Cut Effectiveness Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Ways valid cuts can fail to produce effective computational progress.

children.title: Low-Novelty Cut Geometry
children.top_down_role: Cuts supplying little new geometric restriction.

children.title: Shallow Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts providing only limited separation from the current relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Shallow Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean depth convention at a specified relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\bar x\in P\), and let \(a^Tx\le b\) be valid for the intended feasible set but violated by \(\bar x\), with \(a\ne0\). Its Euclidean cut depth at \(\bar x\) is \[d(a,b;\bar x):=\frac{a^T\bar x-b}{\lVert a\rVert_2}.\] For a prescribed tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), the cut is \(\varepsilon\)-shallow at \(\bar x\) when \(0<d(a,b;\bar x)\le\varepsilon\). This predicate is invariant under positive rescaling of the inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A violated cut is shallow when the point-to-cut-hyperplane distance is positive but no greater than a chosen tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^Tx\le b\) is \(\varepsilon\)-shallow at \(\bar x\) exactly when \(0<(a^T\bar x-b)/\lVert a\rVert_2\le\varepsilon\).

children.title: Nearly Parallel Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts adding little directional diversity to existing rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Nearly Parallel Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oriented cosine criterion for inequalities written with the same sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a^Tx\le b\) and \(c^Tx\le d\) be cuts with nonzero normals, both written with feasible halfspaces on the \(\le\) side. Their oriented cosine similarity is \[\rho(a,c):=\frac{a^Tc}{\lVert a\rVert_2\lVert c\rVert_2}.\] Given \(\varepsilon\in[0,2]\), the cuts are \(\varepsilon\)-nearly parallel when \(\rho(a,c)\ge1-\varepsilon\). Equivalently, their normalized normals satisfy \(\lVert a/\lVert a\rVert_2-c/\lVert c\rVert_2\rVert_2\le\sqrt{2\varepsilon}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two consistently oriented cuts are nearly parallel when the cosine of the angle between their normals is close to one.
assumptions_latex: Both inequalities use the same \(\le\) orientation and \(\varepsilon\in[0,2]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(a,c)\ge1-\varepsilon\), equivalently \(\lVert a/\lVert a\rVert_2-c/\lVert c\rVert_2\rVert_2\le\sqrt{2\varepsilon}\).

notation.meaning: oriented cosine similarity of cut normals

children.title: Redundant Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts contributing no material restriction beyond retained inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact redundancy relative to the current LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le q\}\) be the current relaxation and let \(a^Tx\le b\) be a proposed cut. The cut is redundant for \(P\) if \[P\cap\{x:a^Tx\le b\}=P,\] equivalently, if \(P\subseteq\{x:a^Tx\le b\}\). When \(P\ne\varnothing\), this is equivalent in the extended-real sense to \(\sup\{a^Tx:x\in P\}\le b\). Adding a redundant cut does not change the relaxation feasible region or its optimal value for any objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is redundant when every point of the current relaxation already satisfies it, so adding it leaves the relaxation unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le q\}\) is the current relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\cap\{x:a^Tx\le b\}=P\), equivalently \(P\subseteq\{x:a^Tx\le b\}\).
