children.title: Geometric Novelty Loss
children.top_down_role: Regimes where depth or directional similarity yields negligible new restriction.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Novelty Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-space novelty diagnostic relative to retained relaxation rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let nonzero retained row normals be \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\), let \(S=\operatorname{span}\{a_i/\lVert a_iVert_2:1\le i\le m\}\), and let \(a^Tx\le b\) be a candidate cut with \(a
e0\). Define its normal-space novelty by \[
u(a\mid S):=\operatorname{dist}_2\!\left( rac{a}{\lVert aVert_2},Sight).\] At tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), geometric novelty loss occurs when \(
u(a\mid S)\le\varepsilon\); the new normal then contributes little direction outside the span of retained normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Novelty is lost when a normalized candidate-cut normal lies within a chosen distance of the span of retained row normals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}_2(a/\lVert a\rVert_2,S)\le\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed span-distance score is a coherent stipulated diagnostic, but no source establishes it as geometric novelty loss for cuts. It ignores offsets and becomes identically zero whenever retained normals span the ambient space, so authoritative support or a better-justified metric is required.

children.title: Cut-Progress Relaxation-Growth Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Diminishing progress and excessive relaxation growth across cut rounds.

children.title: Cut-Round Tailing Off
children.top_down_role: Declining relaxation improvement over successive cut rounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Round Tailing Off
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed bound-improvement diagnostic for a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(L_t\) be the nondecreasing relaxation lower bound after cut round \(t\). Given a window \(w\in\mathbb N\), absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\ge0\), and relative tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\), tailing off is detected at \(t\ge w\) when \[L_t-L_{t-w}\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|L_{t-w}|\}.\] Thus the total bound gain over the last \(w\) rounds is below the prescribed mixed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tailing off occurs when several recent cut rounds produce no more than a prescribed absolute-plus-relative bound improvement.
assumptions_latex: \((L_t)_{t\ge0}\) is a finite, nondecreasing sequence of minimization lower bounds.
\(t\ge w\ge1\) and both tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_t-L_{t-w}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|L_{t-w}|\}.\)

notation.meaning: relaxation lower bound after round t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The windowed mixed-tolerance predicate is internally precise and fits a diagnostic condition, but its particular scaling and interpretation as cut-round tailing off are implementation conventions without cited support.

children.title: Relaxation Row Bloat
children.top_down_role: Excessive growth of the active relaxation from retained cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Row Bloat
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-growth condition relative to the initial relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_0\ge1\) be the number of rows in the initial relaxation and \(m_t\) the number retained after cut round \(t\). For a prescribed growth factor \(\gamma>1\), relaxation row bloat is present at round \(t\) when \[m_t\ge\gamma m_0.\] If \(k_s\) rows are added and \(d_s\) rows are deleted during round \(s\), then \(m_t=m_0+\sum_{s=1}^t(k_s-d_s)\); hence the condition measures net retained-row growth, not merely generated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row bloat occurs when the retained LP row count reaches a prescribed multiple of its initial value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_0+\sum_{s=1}^t(k_s-d_s)=m_t\ge\gamma m_0.\)

notation.meaning: retained row count after round t
rows added and deleted in round s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The row-count identity and threshold condition are clear, but calling a prescribed multiple of the initial row count “row bloat” is an operational convention requiring a solver or cut-management source.

children.title: Progress–Size Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Regimes where relaxation growth outpaces useful bound improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Progress–Size Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound gain per net added relaxation row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(L_0\le L_t\) be the relaxation bounds and let \(m_t>m_0\) be the retained row counts before and after \(t\) cut rounds. Define progress per net added row by \[\eta_t:=\frac{L_t-L_0}{m_t-m_0}.\] Given a threshold \(\eta_{\min}\ge0\), a progress–size imbalance occurs when \(\eta_t\le\eta_{\min}\): relaxation size has increased while the average lower-bound gain per retained additional row remains below the chosen threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An imbalance occurs when relaxation growth yields too little lower-bound improvement per net retained row.
assumptions_latex: \(L_t\ge L_0\) are finite minimization lower bounds.

notation.meaning: bound progress per net added row

children.title: Cut-Round Stopping Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Operational boundaries for ending unproductive cut generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Round Stopping Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite stopping predicate for a cut-generation phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At cut round \(t\), let \(v_t\) be the largest candidate-cut violation, \(G_t\) the accepted optimality gap, \(m_t\) the retained row count, and \(\Delta_t=L_t-L_{t-w}\) for \(t\ge w\). Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_v,\varepsilon_G,\varepsilon_L\ge0\) and budgets \(M,T\in\mathbb N\), the cut phase reaches a stopping boundary when \[v_t\le\varepsilon_v\quad\lor\quad G_t\le\varepsilon_G\quad\lor\quad (t\ge w\ \land\ \Delta_t\le\varepsilon_L)\quad\lor\quad m_t\ge M\quad\lor\quad t\ge T.\] The corresponding disjunct records separation exhaustion, target gap, tailing off, row budget, or round budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop cutting upon weak separation, target gap, stalled bound progress, exhausted row budget, or exhausted round budget.
assumptions_latex: \(v_t,G_t,m_t,L_t\) are evaluated consistently at completed cut rounds.
\(w,M,T\in\mathbb N\) with \(w\ge1\), and all tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_t\le\varepsilon_v\lor G_t\le\varepsilon_G\lor(t\ge w\land\Delta_t\le\varepsilon_L)\lor m_t\ge M\lor t\ge T.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The disjunctive predicate is structurally suitable as a stopping condition, but it combines solver-policy choices without evidence. The definitions and scaling of the gap, violation, and progress measures must be fixed by a cited implementation or algorithmic source.

children.title: Degeneracy-Reoptimization Cost Coupling
children.top_down_role: Adverse interaction between added rows, basis degeneracy, and repeated LP solution.

children.title: Basis Degeneracy from Added Rows
children.top_down_role: Degenerate relaxation structure associated with accumulated cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Degeneracy from Added Rows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy of a slack-basic warm-start extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a basic feasible solution of an LP, and append linearly independent cuts \(a_j^Tx\le b_j\) with slack variables \(s_j=b_j-a_j^Tx\). In the standard warm-start extension that declares the new slacks basic, every added cut tight at \(\bar x\) has \(s_j=0\). Consequently, if at least one such zero slack is basic, the extended basic feasible solution is degenerate. Multiple tight added rows can increase the number of zero basic variables, subject to basis nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tight added cut creates a zero basic slack under the usual slack-basic warm start, making the extended basis degenerate.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is a basic feasible solution before row addition.
The augmented basis is nonsingular and takes each new slack \(s_j\) as basic.
At least one added cut satisfies \(a_j^T\bar x=b_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_j=b_j-a_j^T\bar x=0\) for a basic slack, so the augmented basic feasible solution is degenerate.

children.title: LP Reoptimization Cost
children.top_down_role: Repeated solution burden after changes to the active cut set.

knowledge_statements.title: LP Reoptimization Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal and cumulative computational cost after cut insertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_t\) be the LP relaxation after cut round \(t\), and fix a solver, warm-start rule, hardware model, and resource measure \(R\). The marginal LP reoptimization cost is \[C_t^{R}:=R(\text{solve }P_t\text{ from the retained state for }P_{t-1}).\] The cumulative reoptimization cost through round \(T\) is \(C_{1:T}^{R}:=\sum_{t=1}^{T}C_t^{R}\). Typical choices of \(R\) include simplex pivots, barrier iterations, linear-system solves, or elapsed time; costs using different measures are not directly interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reoptimization cost is the measured resource required to solve each strengthened LP from its retained prior solver state.
assumptions_latex: A solver, warm-start rule, hardware model, and resource measure \(R\) are fixed.
Each \(P_t\) is solved from the retained state associated with \(P_{t-1}\).

notation.meaning: LP relaxation after cut round t
marginal reoptimization cost under resource R

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definitions are internally consistent and the content kind fits, but the retained-state cost model and listed resource measures are solver- and hardware-dependent conventions with no cited source.

children.title: Degeneracy-Driven Solver Stalling
children.top_down_role: Poor solver progress caused by degeneracy during repeated reoptimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Driven Solver Stalling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed simplex diagnostic coupling degenerate pivots and weak progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider simplex reoptimizations over rounds \(t-w+1,\ldots,t\). Let \(N_t>0\) be their total pivots, \(D_t\) the pivots producing zero objective change, and \(L_t-L_{t-w}\) the resulting minimization-bound gain. Given \(\rho\in[0,1]\), \(N_{\min}\in\mathbb N\), and \(\varepsilon_L\ge0\), degeneracy-driven stalling is diagnosed when \[N_t\ge N_{\min},\qquad \frac{D_t}{N_t}\ge\rho,\qquad L_t-L_{t-w}\le\varepsilon_L.\] This condition attributes observed stalling only diagnostically; it does not establish that degeneracy is the unique cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stalling is diagnosed when many pivots occur, a large fraction are degenerate, and recent bound improvement remains small.
assumptions_latex: The same simplex pivot and objective-change conventions are used throughout the window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_t\ge N_{\min}\land D_t/N_t\ge\rho\land L_t-L_{t-w}\le\varepsilon_L.\)

notation.meaning: total simplex pivots in the monitoring window

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The windowed conjunction is a coherent simplex diagnostic and appropriately avoids claiming unique causation. Nevertheless, its pivot classification, thresholds, and use of the label “degeneracy-driven” require an authoritative solver or computational-optimization source.

children.title: Row-Addition Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Bound improvement weighed against the solution cost of added rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Addition Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Net-merit criterion balancing relaxation improvement against reoptimization and future row-processing costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the current LP relaxation and let \(R\) be a finite set of valid cuts. For a minimization problem, denote the LP-bound improvement after adding \(R\) by \(B(R)\ge 0\), the immediate reoptimization cost by \(C_{\mathrm{reopt}}(R)\), and the expected subsequent processing cost by \(C_{\mathrm{future}}(R)\). Given conversion weights \(\lambda,\mu>0\), define \[M(R)=B(R)-\lambda C_{\mathrm{reopt}}(R)-\mu C_{\mathrm{future}}(R).\] Under this merit model, adding \(R\) is preferable to adding no rows exactly when \(M(R)>0\); bound improvement alone does not establish positive net merit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut batch is worthwhile under the stated merit model only when its bound improvement outweighs immediate reoptimization and expected future row-processing costs.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ consists of inequalities valid for the integer-feasible set}

notation.meaning: modeled net merit of adding the rows

children.title: Cut-Search-Pricing Interference
children.top_down_role: Cuts that improve current bounds while degrading search or column generation.

children.title: Cut–Branching Interference
children.top_down_role: Cut effects that degrade branching decisions or downstream tree search.

assumptions_latex: P\text{ and every }P_k^i\text{ and }P_k^i\cap C\text{ used in the comparison have finite LP optima}
C\text{ is valid throughout the node subtree}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k,\ell:\ s_k(P)>s_\ell(P)\ \land\ s_k(P^C)<s_\ell(P^C)

notation.meaning: optimal objective value of minimization relaxation Q
minimum child bound gain for branch candidate k in relaxation Q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ranking instability of candidate branches after strengthening the node relaxation with cuts.

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Using a Branch-and-Bound/Cut System p. 123

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a node relaxation for a minimization problem, with finite optimum \(z(P)\), and let branch candidate \(k\) produce children \(P_k^0,P_k^1\). Define \[s_k(P)=\min_{i\in\{0,1\}}\bigl(z(P_k^i)-z(P)\bigr).\] Let \(C\) be a cut set valid throughout the node subtree, set \(P^C=P\cap C\), and take the children of \(P^C\) for candidate \(k\) to be \(P_k^i\cap C\). Assuming all relaxations used in the scores have finite optima, define \[s_k(P^C)=\min_{i\in\{0,1\}}\bigl(z(P_k^i\cap C)-z(P^C)\bigr).\] Cut-branching interference occurs when there are candidates \(k,\ell\) such that \(s_k(P)>s_\ell(P)\) but \(s_k(P^C)<s_\ell(P^C)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cuts interfere with branching when strengthening the relaxation reverses the finite bound-gain ranking of two branch candidates.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut–Branching Interference

source_witnesses.locator: 7.5 Using a Branch-and-Bound/Cut System p. 123

children.title: Cut–Pricing Interference
children.top_down_role: Cut effects that impair column generation or pricing behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut–Pricing Interference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of a newly added cut and its dual multiplier on column reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization master problem whose existing row multipliers are \(\pi\). If the column indexed by \(j\) has objective coefficient \(c_j\) and old-row column \(a_j\), its reduced cost is \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi\). After adding a cut with column coefficient \(d_j\), let \(\pi'\) and \(\mu\) be the reoptimized multipliers for the old rows and new cut. Then \[\bar c'_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi'-d_j\mu.\] Consequently, pricing decisions based on \(\bar c_j\) remain correct only if they are invariant under both the dual displacement \(\pi'-\pi\) and the new term \(d_j\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a cut changes reduced costs through both reoptimized old-row multipliers and the cut's new dual multiplier, potentially invalidating stale pricing decisions.
assumptions_latex: \pi',\mu\text{ are dual multipliers of the reoptimized master}
c_j,a_j,d_j\text{ are represented consistently in the master}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar c'_j-\bar c_j=-a_j^{\mathsf T}(\pi'-\pi)-d_j\mu

notation.meaning: old-row dual multipliers before and after adding the cut
dual multiplier of the added cut
reduced costs before and after cut addition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost displacement identity is mathematically coherent under the stated sign convention and the property fits the leaf. No source or inspectable locator is supplied, however, so the convention and its application to cut-pricing interference require an authoritative column-generation or decomposition source.

children.title: Bound–Search Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Current bound gains contrasted with later branch-search performance.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W(h)<W(0)\iff \frac{N(h)}{N(0)}<\frac{t_{\mathrm{base}}}{t_{\mathrm{base}}+t_h}

notation.meaning: nodes processed under bounding strategy h
additional bounding time per processed node under strategy h
other expected processing time per node

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work comparison between stronger node bounds and the resulting reduction in search-tree size.

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Using a Branch-and-Bound/Cut System p. 123

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let strategy \(h\) add expected strengthening time \(t_h\ge 0\) at each processed node, let \(t_{\mathrm{base}}>0\) be the other expected node-processing time, and let \(N(h)\) be the number of nodes processed before termination. Under the additive work model, \[W(h)=N(h)(t_{\mathrm{base}}+t_h).\] Let \(h=0\) denote a baseline with \(t_{h=0}=0\) and \(N(0)>0\). Then stronger bounding improves modeled total work exactly when \[\frac{N(h)}{N(0)}<\frac{t_{\mathrm{base}}}{t_{\mathrm{base}}+t_h}.\] Thus a smaller search tree alone is insufficient under this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the additive work model, stronger bounds reduce total work only when the proportional reduction in processed nodes outweighs the added per-node computation.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound–Search Tradeoffs

source_witnesses.locator: 7.5 Using a Branch-and-Bound/Cut System p. 123

children.title: Bound–Pricing Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Current bound gains contrasted with pricing tractability or column quality.

assumptions_latex: \min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_jx_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_jx_j=b,\ x_j\ge0\}\text{ is the full master with finite optimum }z_{\mathrm{full}}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall j\in J\setminus J_R,\ \bar c_j\ge0)\Longrightarrow b^{\mathsf T}y\le z_{\mathrm{full}}

notation.meaning: full, possibly implicit column index set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-pricing condition required for a restricted-master dual value to certify a global bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the minimization master \[z_{\mathrm{full}}=\min\left\{\sum_{j\in J}c_jx_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_jx_j=b,\ x_j\ge0\text{ for all }j\in J\right\}.\] Let \(J_R\subseteq J\) be the restricted-master column set and let \(y\) be a restricted-master dual solution, so \(a_j^{\mathsf T}y\le c_j\) for every \(j\in J_R\). For each omitted column \(j\in J\setminus J_R\), define \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y\). If pricing certifies \[\bar c_j\ge0\qquad\text{for every }j\in J\setminus J_R,\] then \(y\) is feasible for the full dual and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le z_{\mathrm{full}}\). Without this full-pricing certificate, restricted-master dual feasibility alone does not certify that lower bound for the full master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted-master dual solution certifies a lower bound for the full minimization master once pricing verifies nonnegative reduced cost for every omitted column.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound–Pricing Tradeoffs

children.title: Numerical Validity Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Reliability failures caused by approximate arithmetic, scaling, and scope errors.

children.title: Unsafe Floating-Point Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Validity risk caused by approximate aggregation and cancellation.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Floating-Point Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for a floating-point approximation of a nonnegative aggregation of valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) be valid for every \(x\in X\), and let \(\lambda_i\ge0\). Their exact aggregation \(A^{\mathsf T}x\le B\), where \(A=\sum_i\lambda_i a_i\) and \(B=\sum_i\lambda_i b_i\), is valid. Suppose floating-point computation returns \(\widehat A=A+\delta a\) and \(\widehat B=B+\delta b\). The computed row is guaranteed valid on \(X\) if \[\sup_{x\in X}(\delta a^{\mathsf T}x-\delta b)\le0.\] If this condition is not established, cancellation or rounding can make \(\widehat A^{\mathsf T}x>\widehat B\) for an otherwise feasible point, so exact validity does not follow from the aggregation multipliers alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rounded aggregation is safe only when its coefficient and right-hand-side errors cannot create positive violation anywhere in the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{x\in X}(\delta a^{\mathsf T}x-\delta b)\le0\Longrightarrow \widehat A^{\mathsf T}x\le\widehat B\quad\forall x\in X

notation.meaning: exact aggregated coefficients and right-hand side

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact aggregation and perturbation condition are mathematically consistent, and failure_boundary fits the numerical-validity leaf. No source or locator supports the floating-point aggregation claim, so an authoritative numerical MIP or verified-cut source is required.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Cut Coefficients
children.top_down_role: Cuts whose coefficient ranges undermine stable relaxation solution.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0<|a^{\mathsf T}x-b|\le E(x)\Longrightarrow \text{the perturbation bounds do not certify preservation of the residual's strict sign}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware coefficient-range diagnostic together with a rigorous residual-uncertainty condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), choose positive variable scales \(s_j\) and set \(q_j=|a_j|s_j\). When \(a\ne0\), define its scaled nonzero coefficient range by \[\kappa_s(a)=\frac{\max_{j:q_j>0}q_j}{\min_{j:q_j>0}q_j}.\] Under perturbations satisfying \(|\delta a_j|\le\eta_j\) and \(|\delta b|\le\beta\), the change in the cut residual at \(x\) has magnitude at most \[E(x)=\sum_j\eta_j|x_j|+\beta.\] Consequently, when \(0<|a^{\mathsf T}x-b|\le E(x)\), these perturbation bounds alone do not certify preservation of the residual's strict sign. A large value of \(\kappa_s(a)\) is a scale-dependent coefficient-range diagnostic; a numerical threshold or claimed solver effect requires a specified arithmetic model and supporting source.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient range is a scale-dependent diagnostic, while residual classification is uncertified when the exact residual is no larger than the applicable perturbation bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Cut Coefficients

children.title: Tolerance-Dependent Validity
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between mathematical validity and numerical feasibility tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Dependent Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap between exact cut feasibility and a solver's tolerance-expanded acceptance region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) be an exactly valid inequality, and suppose a numerical feasibility test accepts the row whenever \[a^{\mathsf T}x-b\le\tau\] for a tolerance \(\tau>0\). Its numerical acceptance region is therefore \(H_\tau=\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b+\tau\}\), whereas the mathematical halfspace is \(H_0=\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}\). Every point satisfying \(0<a^{\mathsf T}x-b\le\tau\) belongs to \(H_\tau\setminus H_0\): it is accepted numerically but violates the exact cut. Thus tolerance-based acceptance cannot itself certify mathematical feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive feasibility tolerance enlarges a cut's accepted halfspace, so points with small positive violations may be numerically accepted but mathematically infeasible.
assumptions_latex: a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\text{ is interpreted exactly}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0<a^{\mathsf T}x-b\le\tau\Longrightarrow x\in H_\tau\setminus H_0

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The absolute-tolerance model, enlarged halfspace, and set-difference conclusion are precise and mutually consistent, and failure_boundary is appropriate. Because no source is supplied, the selected absolute feasibility-test convention and its relevance to solver behavior need an inspectable solver or numerical optimization reference.

children.title: Local–Global Scope Errors
children.top_down_role: Incorrect reuse of cuts outside the search region supporting their validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Local–Global Scope Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete exclusion caused by promoting a locally valid cut to global scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the global feasible set be \(F=\{-1,1\}\subset\mathbb R\), and let a search node impose the local restriction \(L=\{x:x\le0\}\). The inequality \(x\le0\) is valid for the node-feasible set because \(F\cap L=\{-1\}\). It is not globally valid, since \(1\in F\) and \(1>0\). If the locally justified row is installed globally, the resulting feasible set becomes \[F\cap\{x:x\le0\}=\{-1\},\] incorrectly deleting the feasible point \(1\). Therefore a cut derived using local bounds or branch assumptions must retain that scope unless global validity is independently established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the feasible set {-1,1}, the node restriction x≤0 is locally valid but globally applying it wrongly deletes the feasible point 1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\cap L=\{-1\}\ne F
